title: Sequences: refuse a zero or negative frame rate instead of panicking
author: storybored379
body:
file.newSequence and sequence.settings accepted fps 0 (or a negative
rate). The next frame computation divided by zero; over MCP the panic
poisoned the session lock and every later call failed with "session lock
poisoned" until the server was restarted, losing unsaved work.

Both commands now reject rates whose frame duration is not positive.


### How it was found and tested
- Reproduced end-to-end through the headless MCP server (`filmcraft-cli mcp`), then fixed.
- Regression test added; verified it **fails without the change and passes with it**. `cargo test -p filmcraft-engine` passes on current `main` apart from one pre-existing failure; `cargo fmt --check` clean on the touched crate. (One unrelated failure, `shortcuts_tests::assign_reassigns_conflicts_and_undoes`, also fails on current `main`: the default keymap has duplicate bindings for Cmd+9, Cmd+Shift+M and Cmd+T.)
- Files: `crates/engine/src/commands.rs`, `crates/engine/src/tests.rs`
- Clean-room: no third-party source consulted; only public specs and black-box tools (poppler/ffprobe etc.) as oracles.

Found and fixed with Claude Code (AI-assisted).

title: Media: apply the container's display rotation (portrait phone video)
author: storybored379
body:
Phones record portrait video as landscape pictures plus a rotation in the container. FilmCraft parsed the MP4/MOV `tkhd` matrix (`Track.matrix`) but never used it, so **every portrait phone clip imported sideways**, at its landscape size, and a sequence made from it was landscape too.

- **isobmff:** `Track::display_rotation()` reads 0/90/180/270° from the matrix (ISO/IEC 14496-12 §8.3.2: p′ = a·p + c·q + x, q′ = b·p + d·q + y; only the signs of a, b, c, d matter). Mirrored or sheared matrices are left alone.
- **matroska:** parses `Projection` (type, yaw, pitch, roll; RFC 9559 §5.1.4.1.28.41–46). `VideoInfo::display_rotation()` covers rectangular projections; roll is counter-clockwise, so −90 is a quarter turn clockwise.
- **frame:** `VideoFrame::rotated()` turns every plane at its own resolution (parallel per output row). 4:2:2 chroma is widened to 4:4:4 for quarter turns, since half-width chroma would become half-height, which has no `Chroma` variant. The PAR is swapped.
- **codecs:** `Mp4Source` / `MkvSource` report the displayed size and PAR, and `GopCache` rotates decoded frames before caching them, on all decode paths including the nested private decode.
- **web:** the WebCodecs source configures the decoder with the coded size and rotates its output the same way (`cargo check -p filmcraft-web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` passes).

### How it was found and tested
- Found by importing real portrait iPhone HEVC clips (matrix {0, 1, −1, 0}, ffprobe `rotation=-90`). After the fix, a rendered frame matches ffmpeg's auto-rotated frame (≈46 dB on an SDR clip; the same orientation on an HLG one). A synthetic MJPEG MOV/MKV muxed by ffmpeg with `-display_rotation ±90` matches ffmpeg at 65 dB both ways, which also confirmed the Matroska roll sign. ffmpeg was used as a black-box oracle only.
- New tests, which **fail without the change and pass with it**:

title: Timeline: fit a new empty sequence again when its first clip arrives
author: storybored379
body:
Opening a sequence fits the timeline once, on the first frame. An **empty** sequence fits its 1 s minimum duration, so clips added afterwards show at frame-level zoom: the first clip fills the whole track and the rest are off screen. This happens after File ▸ New Sequence followed by a drag or an insert, and with `file.newSequence` + `timeline.place` over the control channel/MCP. (Sequence From Clip isn't affected, since that sequence isn't empty when it opens.)

Now the zoom an empty-sequence fit chose is remembered (`TimelineView::fit_empty`, not serialized). When the sequence gets content and the zoom is still that value, the timeline fits again. A zoom the user changed in between is kept.

### How it was found and tested
- Found driving the desktop app over the control bridge: the timeline showed 00:00–00:01 with one clip spanning the track. It reproduces the same way in the headless harness.
- New test `sequence_ui::new_empty_sequence_fits_its_first_clip`:
  - The placed clip's out edge (`ui.timeline.locate`) must be inside the window. Without the fix it sits at x ≈ 13,100 px.
  - A zoom set while the sequence is still empty is kept.
- It **fails without the change and passes with it**. `cargo test -p filmcraft-ui-egui` passes; `rustfmt --check` is clean on the touched files.
- Clean-room: no third-party source consulted.

title: Control: screenshots and ui.elements wait for the UI to settle
author: storybored379
body:
Over the control channel (MCP bridge mode), agents read the live app right after an edit and got pictures of a state that was still changing:

- **`render_frame` in bridge mode** moves the playhead and screenshots the Program monitor. After a seek the monitor shows the nearest cached picture until the exact frame is decoded. A deep seek into a long file (21 min into a 1 GB recording) therefore returned the *previous* picture, even one from the previous sequence, while the timecode showed the new time. The same call repeated a moment later returned the right frame.
- **`ui.elements`** answered while the timeline zoom was still animating (the fit after opening a sequence), with clip rects that moved afterwards (603 px wide, settling at 686 px).

Changes:
- Screenshots are taken once paused monitors show their exact frames (`monitor_inexact`, set by the monitor when it draws a stand-in) and the timeline zoom is at rest. The wait is capped at 5 s, after which whatever is on screen is captured. This mirrors effectcraft, which already waits for in-flight viewer frames before capturing.
- `ui.elements` retries until the zoom has been at rest for two frames, because `Automation::query` answers from the frame before the last one.

### How it was found and tested
- Found and verified on Windows (RTX 5090) driving the desktop app through `filmcraft-cli mcp --bridge`.
  - Before: the first `render_frame` after the deep seek differed from the next one at the same time.
  - After: both are pixel-identical. The headless render of that frame matches ffmpeg's frame at 41–44 dB, so the decode itself was fine.
- New test `view_ui::elements_wait_for_the_timeline_zoom_to_settle`: rects read right after opening a sequence must equal the settled ones. It **fails without the change and passes with it**.
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-ui-egui` passes; `rustfmt --check` is clean on the touched files.
- Clean-room: no third-party source consulted.

title: Media: AIFF files import (enable symphonia's aiff reader)
author: storybored379
body:
AIFF is listed as an importable audio format (`.aif` / `.aiff` / `.aifc` go to the symphonia-backed `AudioFileSource`) and FilmCraft exports AIFF, but the symphonia dependency is built with only the `wav` reader enabled. Every AIFF import, including FilmCraft's own AIFF exports, fails with "unsupported media: end of stream".

This enables symphonia's `aiff` feature. It is served by the same MPL-2.0 `symphonia-format-riff` crate that already reads WAV, so `Cargo.lock` doesn't change.

title: Export: start/end times without a range mean a custom range
author: storybored379
body:
`file.exportMedia` (and `export.resolve`, `export.quick`, `export.queue.add`) document `startSeconds` / `endSeconds` next to `range`, but start/end times passed without `"range": "custom"` were silently ignored: the whole sequence (or In/Out) was exported instead. An agent asking for "seconds 0–2" got a full-length file and no error.

`range_param` now treats bare `start…` / `end…` times as a custom range. A start without an end goes through the existing custom-range check and returns its error. Requests that pass `range` explicitly behave as before.

### How it was found and tested
- Found through the headless MCP server (`filmcraft-cli mcp`): `file.exportMedia` with only `startSeconds`/`endSeconds` rendered the whole sequence.
- `export_tests::ranges_resolve_and_sidecar_captions_are_written` gains two checks: bare times resolve to the same 30 frames as `range: "custom"`, and a start without an end is an error. It **fails on current `main` without the change and passes with it**.

title: Timeline: transitions stay on their cuts after ripple trim, roll, slide and ripple speed
author: storybored379
body:
Ripple trims (`trim` in ripple mode and `ripple_trim_group`), rolling edits, slides and Speed/Duration with ripple move clips but leave every transition at its old timeline position. After e.g. a 1 s ripple trim, the dip to black between the next two clips plays 1 s after their cut, dissolving into the outgoing clip's handle mid-shot and then hard-cutting. A rolled cut keeps its dissolve where the cut used to be.

After these edits each transition now shifts by as much as its anchor moved: the incoming clip's start, or the outgoing clip's end for a fade to nothing. That keeps its alignment on the edit point. Insert, extract, ripple delete and close gap already shift transitions and are unchanged.

### How it was found and tested
- Reproduced end-to-end through the headless MCP server (`filmcraft-cli mcp`): after `timeline.trim` in ripple mode the transitions kept their old positions, then fixed.
- New test `tests::transitions_stay_on_their_cuts` (filmcraft-edit): three clips with two cross dissolves and a fade-out, then ripple trim out/in, ripple trim group, roll, slide and a ripple speed change, checking after each edit that every transition is still centred on its cut. It **fails on current `main` without the change and passes with it**.
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-edit` passes; `rustfmt --check` clean on the touched files; `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-edit --all-targets` adds no warnings; `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask wasm` pass.
- Independent of the "Slide moves linked audio" PR (different files); the two branches merge cleanly together and the tests of both pass on the merge.

title: Timeline: Slide moves linked audio with the video
author: storybored379
body:
`timeline.slide` (the Slide tool drag and the control-channel/MCP command) only moved the clip it was given. Sliding a linked video clip left its audio partner behind: the audio kept its old start and source In, a visible A/V desync of the slide distance. Slip, Trim, Rate Stretch and the keyboard slide (`timeline.slideLeft` / `timeline.slideRight`) already include linked partners.

The command now slides every linked partner (`with_links`) by a common delta, clamped across the partners the way `timeline.trim` does, so a shorter handle on one track can't slide the pair apart.

### How it was found and tested
- Found through the headless MCP server (`filmcraft-cli mcp`): after `timeline.slide` on the demo project's second video clip, its linked audio was 5 frames off.
- New test `tests::slide_moves_linked_audio_with_the_video` (filmcraft-engine): slides a linked clip by 5 frames and checks the audio partner's start and source In match the video's. It **fails on current `main` without the change and passes with it**.

title: Licensing: standard LICENSE files, NOTICE, ArtCraft brand terms
author: echelon
body:
Brings FilmCraft in line with the Crafting Apps licensing standard. Only docs and licence files change; no code.

- `LICENSE-MIT` / `LICENSE-APACHE`: standard text. The copyright holder is now "ArtCraft Team and the FilmCraft contributors", and the Apache text uses the canonical apache.org layout.

title: Rules: never crash (AGENTS.md §0, clippy.toml, forbid unsafe)
author: echelon
body:
Steering for the never-crash rollout (standard: `craftrules/standards/never-crash.md`).

- **AGENTS.md §0 Never crash** at the top of the rules: why (a crash loses someone's work), that it outranks feature work, the bans (`unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!`/`unreachable!`/`todo!`/`unimplemented!`, `unsafe`), `Result`/`?` patterns, hostile input-derived numbers (`get()`, checked math, no zero division, capped allocations), bounded recursion, lock poisoning, background `catch_unwind`, the last-resort guard (`crates/ui-egui/src/crash.rs` hook + UI-pass `catch_unwind`), and a regression test per crash fix. §3.1 now points to §0.
- **CLAUDE.md**, **CONTRIBUTING.md**, **docs/contributing.md**: short Never crash notes pointing to AGENTS.md §0.
- **clippy.toml** (new): `allow-{unwrap,expect,panic,indexing-slicing}-in-tests = true`.
- **Cargo.toml**: `[workspace.lints.rust] unsafe_code = "forbid"` (was `deny`; there is no `unsafe` or `allow(unsafe_code)` in the workspace).

No code changes. Follow-up PRs clean the crates one by one and add `#![deny(clippy::unwrap_used, …)]` to each.

### Checks
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask assets`, `cargo xtask wasm`: pass.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --release -- -D warnings`: **already failing on main** with the current stable toolchain (Rust 1.99), unrelated to this PR: new lints `clippy::chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` (ac3, cfb, frame, h264enc, isobmff, mpegts, mxf, opus, scopes, testkit, text), `clippy::drain_collect` and `clippy::needless_late_init`. title: vp9: never crash (no unwrap/expect/panic, deny them)
author: echelon
body:
Never-crash rollout (AGENTS.md §3.1, `craftrules/standards/never-crash.md`): `filmcraft-vp9` now has no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` in production code and denies them.

- Transforms, 8-tap filters and default probability tables take fixed-size views with `first_chunk(_mut)` instead of slice + `try_into().unwrap()/expect()`; the happy path is unchanged.
- Tile size fields are read with `get()`; a short one returns `Error::Invalid`.
- The buffer pool tolerates a poisoned lock.
- A failed `vp9-post` thread spawn used to `panic!`. The job now reaches the thread over a channel, so it is still in hand on failure and runs inline.
- Without the `threads` feature, an unpublished reference band reads as empty instead of panicking.
- `#![cfg_attr(not(test), deny(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic, clippy::unimplemented, clippy::todo, clippy::unreachable))]`. It uses `cfg_attr(not(test))` so this PR doesn't depend on the `clippy.toml` from #10; once every crate is clean the lints move to `[workspace.lints.clippy]` and these attributes go.

Independent of the other never-crash PRs (touches only `crates/vp9`).

### Checks
- `cargo fmt --check`: pass
- `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-vp9 --all-targets --release -- -D warnings`: pass (also `--no-default-features`), with `-A clippy::chunks_exact_to_as_chunks -A clippy::drain_collect -A clippy::needless_late_init`. title: Codecs: never crash (ac3, audio-dsp, opus, mpeg2v, prores, dnx)
author: echelon
body:
Never-crash rollout (AGENTS.md §3.1, `craftrules/standards/never-crash.md`) for six codec crates. None of them has panicking calls in production code any more, and each denies the panicking lints.

- **ac3**: the LFE channel is taken without `expect`.
- **audio-dsp**: the channel-matrix `match` is exhaustive (no `unreachable!`). An unknown internal parameter id reads as 0 (with a `debug_assert!`) instead of `panic!`.
- **opus**: dual-stereo bands and SILK frames take the optional Y buffer and range decoder with `if let` instead of `expect`.
- **mpeg2v**: `peek32` reads through `get()` + `first_chunk`. The literal VLC table parser no longer `panic!`s (it has a `debug_assert!`; the codes are crate literals covered by the table tests).
- **prores / dnx**: IDCT rows come through `as_chunks::<8>()`. The ProRes 8-wide block store and alpha slices have no `unwrap`/`expect`, and the DNx header timecode is read through `get()`.

title: time: never crash (zero rates and timebases, huge timecodes)
author: echelon
body:
Never-crash rollout (AGENTS.md §3.1, `craftrules/standards/never-crash.md`).

**Real crashes found by mutation fuzzing** (mutated ffmpeg-made files through `filmcraft_codecs::open_bytes`):
- an MP4 whose track `timescale` is 0 panicked on import in `Tick::from_rational` (`attempt to divide by zero`, via `codecs/src/mp4.rs` duration);
- an MPEG-TS stream whose timestamps gave a zero frame rate panicked in `FrameRate::tick_of` (via `codecs/src/mpeg.rs` `describe_video`).

- New `FrameRate::sane()`: a zero or negative rate counts as the default rate in `frame_duration`, `frame_at`, `tick_of` and `timecode_base`. Valid rates are unchanged.
- `Tick::clamp` uses `max`/`min`, so crossed bounds don't panic.
- `parse_timecode`, `fields_to_frames` and `frames_to_fields` use saturating math; huge typed or agent-sent timecodes overflowed.
- Regression test `tests::hostile_rates_and_timecodes_never_panic`. It panicked before this change, in release too (integer division by zero).

title: Export: same file on every machine (fixed mux interleave, H.264 slices by frame size)
author: storybored379
body:
Exporting the same project twice can give two different files. This happens with a decode-free Bars and Tone sequence too, so it is not a decode or prefetch race. Two export parameters followed the number of cores the process sees:

- **Mux layout.** `Exporter::step` renders one batch per call (`rayon::current_num_threads().clamp(2, 16)` frames), then writes that batch's video packets and the audio up to its end. Each batch becomes one chunk per track, so `stsc`/`stco` and the PCM chunk sizes changed with the core count. The samples themselves did not: video `framemd5` and decoded audio were identical. Example: ProRes + PCM, 240 frames, gave 30 chunks of 8 frames in one run and 24 chunks of 10 in the next.
- **H.264 slices.** `h264_factory` left `EncoderConfig::slices` at 0, so the encoder chose `min(available_parallelism, MB rows / 4)` slices. A different slice count gives a different bitstream and different decoded pictures, every frame of a textured clip. A flat Bars and Tone picture sometimes decodes the same either way.

Two exports in a row differ whenever the visible core count changes between them: a CPU quota in a container, a cgroup or affinity limit, power management. With the core count pinned, main's exports were byte-identical: 3 runs at 2 CPUs each for H.264 bars and an H.264 clip. Changing the count from 2 to 4 changed the file. The render path itself was already deterministic. ProRes is intra-only and does not depend on the core count, and ProRes exports of an imported H.264 clip gave the same pictures in 12 runs, three at a time with `RAYON_NUM_THREADS=32`. Export never reads preview or monitor stand-in frames: it uses `full_res_provider`, and the GOP cache gives draft frames only to draft requests.

**Scope.** This makes export independent of the core count. Checked on Windows (32 threads) as well: an imported H.264 clip exported as H.264 and as ProRes gives the same file on Windows and Linux, byte for byte. A generated Bars & Tone project gives t…

title: engine: last-resort guard around commands and background jobs
author: echelon
body:
Never-crash rollout (AGENTS.md §0, last-resort guard; `craftrules/standards/never-crash.md`).

**State before this PR.** The desktop app already had a last-resort guard: `crates/ui-egui/src/crash.rs` installs a panic hook that writes a crash log, and the UI pass runs under `catch_unwind`, so a panic shows the error window and the session and project survive. Frame-decode workers also catch panics. Two gaps remained:
1. **Commands outside the UI pass.** In headless use (`filmcraft-cli`, MCP over stdio) a panicking command ended the process and lost the unsaved session.
2. **Background jobs** (export, render previews/audio, proxies, Project Manager, mask tracking, scene detection) ran their body on a bare thread. A panic killed the thread and the job showed as "running" forever. AGENTS.md §0.6 already requires these to catch panics.

**This PR** (minimal, no redesign):
- `Session::execute` runs the command body under `catch_unwind` and returns `EngineError::Other("internal error in \`<id>\` (see the crash log); the command did not complete")`. The panic hook has already logged the location.
- `export_tools::guard_job(progress, result, run)` wraps every job body. A panic marks the job finished, with the error in `progress.error` and the job result. It's applied at all seven job spawn sites, and covers both the thread path and the inline (`wait` / wasm) path.
- Regression test: `export_tools::guard_tests::panicking_job_is_reported_as_failed`.

This is a safety net, not a substitute for the per-crate fixes in the other never-crash PRs. The never-crash engine PR #24 also edits `crates/engine/src/lib.rs`, but only its first lines; this PR changes `Session::execute` (~line 600). They merge cleanly in either order.

title: MCP: tool annotations, core tools, resources, export progress and cancellation
author: storybored379
body:
A proposal rather than a fix: a few MCP conventions that make the server easier for agents to use, built on top of the existing design. Every existing tool, name and argument still works. It's split into three commits so any of them can be dropped or reworked on its own.

### Why
Things an agent runs into on current `main`, using `filmcraft-cli mcp --demo`:

- **No hints for the client.** `tools/list` gives each tool a name, a description and a schema, but no `title` and no annotations. A client can't tell `sequence_inspect` from `ui_click`, so it asks the user before every call or before none of them. With this branch:
  ```json
  {"name": "sequence_inspect", "title": "Inspect the active sequence",
   "annotations": {"readOnlyHint": true, "destructiveHint": false, "idempotentHint": true, "openWorldHint": false}}
  ```
- **A mistyped argument is ignored without a word.** `render_frame {"second": 2.0}` (instead of `seconds`) returns a PNG of the playhead frame, which is the wrong frame, and nothing says so. With this branch the call fails:
  `-32602 unknown argument "second" for render_frame; expected: max_side, seconds`.
- **A line that isn't JSON gets no reply.** rmcp drops it, so the client waits until it times out. Now it gets `-32700 parse error` (id `null`), and the server keeps serving.
- **A panic wedges the session.** After any command panics, the session mutex is poisoned and every later call fails with `session lock poisoned` until restart (AGENTS.md §0.6).
- **Long exports are a black box.** `command_run file.exportMedia {"wait": true}` blocks with no feedback (16 s for 4 s of 720p H.264 here) and can't be stopped from the client. With `_meta.progressToken` the server now sends standard MCP progress:
  ```json
  {"method": "notifications/progress", "params": {"progressToken": "exp", "progress": 24, "total": 96, "message": "Exporting 96 frames (H.264)"}}
  ```
  `notifications/cancelled` stops the export and deletes the partial file.

title: GPU1: blend modes on the GPU compositor (#30)
author: echelon
body:
Part of #30. All 27 blend modes now composite on the GPU, so a clip with a blend mode no longer forces the whole frame through the CPU renderer.

- **Normal and Dissolve** use fixed-function "over" blending. Dissolve's per-pixel pattern is the CPU's 64-bit hash, rebuilt in WGSL, and matches it exactly.
- **The other 25 modes** first copy the accumulator region under the layer into a backdrop texture. The fragment shader then composites with the CPU reference math. Only layers that need the destination pay for the copy.
- **`render::plan`**: `PlanLayer` has a new `blend` field. Inside transitions the mode is forced to Normal, matching the CPU reference. Adjustment layers, effects and non-dissolve transitions keep their existing CPU fallback.

**Parity (GPU vs CPU reference)**
- Edge cases (black/white, Divide by zero, Dodge/Burn at 0 and 1, zero and partial alpha): every mode is within one half-float step (≤ 4.9e-4). Normal, Dissolve and Hard Mix are exact.
- Full sequences through `plan_frame`: interior p99 is 1 for every mode.

**Benchmark** (`stack3-blend`: three 1080p layers with Screen and Overlay, at Full resolution)

| | shown/dropped | CPU ms/frame |
|---|---|---|
| before | 19/173, 138/54 | 168–214 |
| after | 191/1, 192/0 | 86–87 |

After the change, the blended stack costs the same as the plain Normal stack. Details are in `docs/performance.md`.

`cargo xtask ci` is green.

title: HW1: platform crate + VideoToolbox H.264/HEVC hardware decode (#30)
author: echelon
body:
Part of #30. Stacked on #32; the first commit here is #32's.

Adds the hardware video decoding path on macOS, with the pure-Rust decoders as the tested fallback.

### What's new
- **`crates/platform`** (L5): the one crate allowed `unsafe`, for OS media FFI only. It sets `unsafe_code = "deny"`, and only the `videotoolbox` module opts in. Every block has a `// SAFETY:` comment (enforced by `clippy::undocumented_unsafe_blocks = "deny"`), and the public API is safe and returns `Result`. The policy is in AGENTS.md §0.3 and `docs/adr/0001-platform-ffi.md`, as craftrules' never-crash standard requires.
- **VideoToolbox decoder** for H.264 and HEVC (8- and 10-bit, 4:2:0 and 4:2:2):
  - hardware is required, so Apple's software decoder is never used in place of ours;
  - asynchronous decode with two frames in flight;
  - a reorder buffer sized from the stream's SPS;
  - output copied out to planar Y'CbCr. Zero-copy into wgpu is a follow-up.
- **`HybridDecoder`**: if a session fails mid-stream, it replays the samples since the last restart point through the software decoder and carries on in software.
- **Setting**: Settings ▸ Playback ▸ Hardware decoding, Auto (default) or Off.
- **Counters**: `perf.stats` gains `decode.hardware {enabled, frames, softwareFrames, sessions, declined, fallbacks}`.
- **Startup**: the desktop app and the CLI/MCP register the decoder. On other OSes registration does nothing.

### Tests
- **Parity**: H.264 High, HEVC Main (open GOP, CRA+RASL) and HEVC Main10 are bit-exact with our software decoders on every frame. Pts order, colour and pixel aspect also match, after reset, reseek and flush.
- **Robustness**: mutation fuzz of samples and parameter sets, with a hang timeout.
- **Fallback**: forced failures at 5 points, plus an in-band SPS change.
- **Setting**: Off selects the software decoder.

title: GPU2: standard effects on the GPU compositor (#30)
author: echelon
body:
Part of #30. The most common standard effects now run on the GPU. A clip using only these effects no longer forces a CPU render of that layer.

**On the GPU (31 effect ids)**
- **Colour:** Brightness & Contrast, ProcAmp, Tint, Black & White, Color Balance, Leave Color, Change to Color, Color Pass, Color Replace, Channel Mix, ASC CDL, Gamma Correction, Levels, Extract, Invert, Posterize, Alpha Adjust.
- **Geometry:** Horizontal/Vertical Flip, Crop (feather, zoom), Edge Feather, Transform, Mirror, Offset.
- **Blur:** Gaussian Blur (incl. legacy), Camera Blur, Directional Blur (incl. legacy).
- **Sharpen:** Sharpen, Unsharp Mask.

**Still on the CPU:** Lumetri, keys, Vignette, Video Limiter, effect/opacity masks, and everything else. A clip goes to the GPU only when *all* of its enabled effects are supported; otherwise its layer renders on the CPU exactly as before.

**How it works**
- `render::gpufx::FxOp` evaluates each effect's parameters once (keyframes, clamping). The CPU path and the GPU plan share it, so both evaluate identically by construction. The CPU math moved here unchanged.
- `filmcraft-gpu` runs each op as compute passes on `Rgba32Float` working textures at the CPU's decode size. The result is then drawn with the layer's matrix, opacity and blend mode.
- Box blurs cost O(1) per pixel at any radius.
- Devices without compute shaders or storage textures fall back to CPU effects inside the compositor.
- Sampling uses `textureLoad` with manual filtering, and storage textures are write-only, so no optional GPU features are needed.

**Parity with the CPU reference**
- **Single effects:** 78 cases, including hostile parameters (contrast 900, gamma ≤ 0, blur 1e9, NaN). Max relative difference 6.7e-5; most cases exact.
- **Chains:** ≤ 8.5e-7.
- **Composited plans:** interior 8-bit p99 1.
- **Golden:** a 5-track project. Its effect clips plan as GPU layers; Emboss still falls back.

**Benchmark** (`stack3-fx`, load average 107–170): worker time per frame drops fro…

title: Captions: report invalid TTML timing parameters on import
author: storybored379
body:
A TTML file declaring a zero or negative frame rate currently imports using a default rate. Invalid tick rates and incomplete frame-rate multipliers are similarly replaced with defaults, so the imported caption timing can differ from what the file declares.

Return a caption syntax error naming the invalid parameter. Defaults still apply when attributes are absent. Rate products use checked arithmetic, and an explicit tick rate takes precedence over the derived default. This follows the positive-integer and two-component multiplier requirements in [TTML2 §7.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/ttml2/#parameter-attribute-frameRate).

Validation: the public caption-import regression test fails on main for `frameRate="0"` and passes with the change. Tests cover ordinary invalid values, empty attributes, incomplete multipliers, omitted attributes, and valid frame/subframe/tick-rate combinations. All 49 caption unit and round-trip tests pass. A CLI smoke test imports a valid caption and reports an error for zero, negative, and empty frame-rate attributes. Formatting, strict workspace clippy, assets, layers, and all 41 wasm crates pass. The release workspace run has 1,651 passing tests and 16 failures; the failing tests exactly match the recorded results on the same upstream base (`694e405`, 1,649 passing / 16 failing). These are existing FFmpeg oracle and keymap failures; this change adds two passing tests and no new failures.

Found and fixed with OpenAI Codex (AI-assisted).

title: MEM1–MEM4 + HW1: clip memory on a timeline from 12 GB to 1.9 GB; hardware decode actually on
author: justjohn12345
body:
## Summary

Dropping twelve H.264 clips on a timeline took the desktop release build to a **12 GB** footprint. After this branch the same project sits at **1.9 GB**, and hardware decoding, which the desktop app was never using, now takes every stream.

Measured on macOS (Apple silicon) with `footprint`, `heap`, `malloc_history` (`MallocStackLogging=lite`) and `perf.stats`.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| App footprint, 12 clips | 12 GB | 1.9 GB |
| Hardware / software frames | 0 / all | 31,880 / 0 |
| Live decoders (12 open sources) | 12 | 4 |

## Commits

- **MEM1: desktop reads media files in place.** `FsServices` had no `Services::reader`, so `MediaPool::open_file` read each clip whole and kept its bytes (2.9 GB). It now returns a `FileReader` with positional reads, as the web host already does through `BlobReader`.
- **MEM2: idle sources give up their decoders beyond a cap.** Every source kept its decoder for good, about 290 MB per H.264 clip (3.5 GB). The GOP caches share a pool: beyond four live decoders, caches idle for 3 s drop theirs, least recently used first. A cache asked for a frame in the last 3 s always keeps its decoder, so a composite of many layers never restarts decoders per frame.
- **MEM3: one frame budget shared by all sources.** Each GOP cache kept up to 384 MB with nothing bounding the total (3.8 GB). Frames of all caches now count against a 1 GiB budget; idle caches give up frames first, caches in use keep their own budget.
- **HW1: register the hardware decoders in every desktop run.** `filmcraft_platform::register()` was an argument of `log::info!`. Log macros do not evaluate their arguments when no logger takes the level, and the app installs none, so VideoToolbox was never registered (`decode.hardware.sessions` was 0). The CLI and bench were not affected.
- **MEM4: decode into the planes of evicted frames.** With MEM1–MEM3 the footprint was 5.1 GB with only 2.5 GB live: per-picture plane allocations left the system allocator holdin…

title: codecs: resampled MP4 audio reads apply the edit list once
author: punkhop
body:
## What was wrong
Audio from an MP4/MOV whose sample rate differs from the sequence's came out with loud spikes, repeating through the clip, in every export and in playback. Any 48 kHz clip in a 44.1 kHz sequence shows it when the file has an edit list (AAC priming).

In `Mp4Source::audio`, `s0` already has the edit-list offset subtracted. The resample branch then derived its sub-sample phase from `s0` again, so the offset was applied twice: the read position started about 1024 samples early, was clamped to index 0 with a large negative fraction, and the linear interpolation extrapolated a ramp over the start of every request. Export pulls audio one batch of frames at a time, so the ramp repeats.

## Shortest way to see it
```sh
ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc2=size=640x360:rate=24 -f lavfi -i sine=frequency=880:sample_rate=48000 \
  -t 6 -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -c:a aac -shortest tone48.mp4
cat > s.jsonl <<'EOF'
{"id":"file.import","params":{"paths":["tone48.mp4"]}}
{"id":"file.newSequence","params":{"name":"s","fps":24,"sampleRate":44100}}
{"id":"timeline.place","params":{"item":1,"time":0}}
EOF
filmcraft-cli --save-as s.fcproj run s.jsonl
filmcraft-cli --project s.fcproj export out.mp4
```
The source peaks at about 0.25; decoded as float, `out.mp4` peaks above 11 on `main`. With this change it matches the source.

## What the change does
Two lines: keep the pre-offset window start and take the phase from it. The Matroska, MPEG, MXF and Ogg readers subtract no offset and are not affected.

## Tested
New ffmpeg-oracle test (`require_ffmpeg!`), fixture generated into `target/fixtures`. `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p <touched crates> --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p <touched crates>` and `cargo xtask layers` pass. I did not get a full `cargo xtask ci` green locally: `filmcraft-gpu`'s `gpu_effects_match_cpu_exactly` fails for me on untouched `main` as well, and I do not have the wasm target installed.

title: engine: a project saved after an interchange import opens again
author: punkhop
body:
## What was wrong
A project that was saved after importing an interchange file could not be opened again: `project file is damaged: invalid type: null, expected f64`.

The importers create intrinsic effects with `d.instance()`, whose point parameters are the NaN "auto" sentinel. Placing a clip resolves those with `resolve_auto_points`; the import path did not. `serde_json` writes NaN as `null`, and the reader refused `null`. The picture renders correctly, so nothing warns you until the reopen, and by then the session's work is in a file the app will not read.

## Shortest way to see it (v0.2.0 and `main`)
```sh
filmcraft-cli --demo exec file.exportInterchange format=xml path=/tmp/demo.xml
echo '{"id":"file.import","params":{"paths":["/tmp/demo.xml"]}}' > /tmp/in.jsonl
filmcraft-cli --save-as /tmp/demo.fcproj run /tmp/in.jsonl
filmcraft-cli --project /tmp/demo.fcproj inspect project   # project file is damaged
```

## What the change does
- Auto points are resolved for imported clips the same way they are for placed ones: frame points at import, anchors when the media links and its real size is known. One place, so every importer is covered.
- `null` reads as "auto" for effect point parameters only (`ParamValue::Vec2`), so projects already saved in this state open. A `null` anywhere else in the model is still refused.

Details and the reasoning for not bumping the schema are in the commit message.

## Tested
New tests in `project`, `format` and `engine` (import, save, reopen; a source whose size differs from the sequence). `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p <touched crates> --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p <touched crates>` and `cargo xtask layers` pass. title: engine: timeline.move takes linked partners along
author: punkhop
body:
Stacked on #44: both touch `timeline.move`, so this one contains that commit too. I will rebase it once that one is in, or fold them together if you prefer.

## What was wrong
`timeline.move` moved only the clips listed. With Linked Selection on, a picture clip moved by command left its linked sound where it was, out of sync. `timeline.trim` already takes linked partners along; move did not. Same family as #8 (slide).

## Shortest way to see it
```sh
echo '{"id":"timeline.move","params":{"moves":[{"clip":44,"track":"V1","time":5668102440000}]}}' > /tmp/m.jsonl
filmcraft-cli --demo run /tmp/m.jsonl
# the last picture clip is now at frame 535; its linked sound clip is still at 511
```

## What the change does
With Linked Selection on, a linked partner that is not itself listed moves by the same offset on its own track. A partner on a locked track is skipped, a partner that would not move at all is left untouched, and a group that would cross the sequence start is shifted as one.

**Behaviour change to be aware of:** a caller that moves only a picture clip now also moves its sound, in overwrite mode like any other move, so it can replace audio at the destination. `linked: false` gives the old behaviour, and the timeline drag passes it because Alt-drag moves one side of a link on purpose. If you would rather have this opt-in (`linked: true`), say so and I will flip the default.

The command now returns `{"moved": [ids]}`.

title: edit: a ripple trim takes a later split edit along
author: punkhop
body:
## What was wrong
A ripple trim on the clip before a split edit left the later clip's sound behind. Take two clips in a row on V1 where the second one's linked sound starts 12 frames before its picture (a J cut) and sits on a sync-locked track on which the first clip has no partner. `timeline.trim {mode: "ripple", edge: "out", deltaFrames: 8}` on the first clip moved the second picture 8 frames later and left its sound where it was: the 12-frame lead became 20, with no error. The same trim with `-8` was refused as a sync-lock conflict, because the early sound sits in the stretch that closes.

## What the change does
In `ripple_trim_group`, a clip that starts before the cut, reaches past it and is linked to a clip that shifts now shifts with it, on the tracks that ripple (the members' tracks and sync-locked tracks). It no longer counts as material in the way of a shortening.

A linked clip that ends before the cut is not treated as a split edit and stays where it is, as before; so do the trimmed clip's own partners. A transition into the following clip from a clip that stays behind would be left over a gap, so it is removed.

Not changed: tracks that are locked or not sync-locked still do not ripple, so a split sound on such a track stays put, as any other clip there does. title: edit: ripple delete closes one gap for a clip with a split edit
author: punkhop
body:
## What was wrong
`edit.rippleDelete` on a clip whose linked sound has a different edge than its picture (a J or an L cut) treated the picture's range and the sound's range as two gaps and closed both on every affected track. With two or more clips after it, the later ones were moved up twice and the edit was refused ("items overlap"). With a single clip after it the delete went through, and sequence markers after it were moved by both gaps (one that landed inside the second gap was removed).

## What the change does
One set of stretches closes on every track: the time the deleted clips covered, less whatever stays on the tracks that lose a clip. Those tracks move up by the same amount, into time that is free on all of them, so the clips after stay in sync and nothing is overwritten.

- For a J or an L cut that is the picture's range.
- Straight cuts close as before, also with the sounds on alternating audio tracks.
- A locked track loses nothing and does not count.

`ripple_delete_items` now returns the stretches it closed and the command ripples the markers by those, so the two cannot disagree.

**Behaviours to be aware of:**
- A gap can stay on one track when a clip that stays on another of the tracks covers part of the deleted time. A sound shorter than its picture, with other sound right up against it, closes only the sound's stretch. The same holds for unlinked clips on different tracks deleted in one call: they share one set of stretches, so a title that stays on the second clip's track can keep part of the first clip's gap open. Deleting them one at a time closes each fully.
- When nothing can close at all, the edit is refused ("no gap can close") and nothing changes. Some such calls went through before, moving clips by a gap another track did not have.
- A selection wholly on locked tracks is refused as locked. Before, it deleted nothing and still shifted the sync-locked tracks.

title: edit: a speed change with ripple moves later clips once
author: punkhop
body:
## What was wrong
`clip.speedDuration` with `ripple: true` on a clip that has linked sound set the speed on the picture and then on its sound, and each one rippled the later material on its own. At 50% the later clips moved by twice the change and a double gap was left. At 200% the edit was refused ("items overlap") when more than one clip followed: the second ripple pulled the farther clips onto the nearer ones.

## What the change does
A new `set_speed_group` in the edit crate changes a clip and its linked partners on other tracks as one edit and ripples once, on the members' tracks and on sync-locked tracks. It works on a copy, so a failure changes nothing. `set_speed` keeps its signature and its behaviour for one clip.

The command groups the selected clips by link, one clip per track in a group. Clips that are not linked, and linked clips of one track, still change one after the other, as before.

**Behaviour to be aware of:** when the members' lengths change by different amounts (a split edit: the sound is longer than its picture), the later material moves by the largest change. No member is overlapped and the tracks stay in sync; the shorter member is followed by a gap. Moving each track by its own change would put the next clip out of sync.

## Tested
New edit-crate test (slower, faster, a split edit both ways, two clips of one track and a missing clip refused with nothing changed) and engine tests through `clip.speedDuration`: slower with undo and redo; faster; two clips in one call; no ripple; picture and sound both named with Linked Selection off; linked clips of one track; a split edit; a clip that is not in the sequence. title: engine: timeline.place on an audio track places the sound there
author: punkhop
body:
Stacked on #44: both touch how `timeline.place` reads its track parameters, so this one contains that commit too. I will rebase it once that one is in, or fold them together if you prefer.

## What was wrong
`timeline.place {item, track: "A3"}`, an audio track given as `track`:
- for an item with picture and sound it put a video item on the audio track A3 and a second, sound clip on the default audio track;
- for a sound-only item it ignored `track` and placed on the default audio track.

## What the change does
`track` is where the picture goes and `audioTrack` where the sound goes. An audio track given as `track` now places the sound alone, on that track.

What cannot be meant is an "invalid parameters" error that says why, and changes nothing:
- an audio track as `track` together with `audioTrack`;
- a video track as `audioTrack`;
- an audio track for an item that has no sound;
- a video track alone for an item that has no picture.

Calls that name a video track as `track` and an audio track as `audioTrack` are unchanged; that is what the timeline panel's drop sends. The parameter hint and `docs/agents.md` describe it.

**Your call:** if you would rather have an audio track in `track` be an error (with `audioTrack` the only way to name it), say so and I will change it. I chose "the sound alone" because an agent that says "put this on A3" means exactly that, and there was no way to place only the sound of a clip without changing source patching.

Not in this change: `timeline.move` still accepts a video clip on an audio track.

title: interchange: an FCP7 master clip lands in its bin when a sequence used it first
author: punkhop
body:
## What was wrong
An FCP7 XML document may name a file first inside a sequence and later again in the `<clip>` master clip that sits in a bin. Premiere's own exports and editor packages with "stringout" sequences ahead of the footage bins do exactly this. FilmCraft filed the media item where it first saw the file, so every such clip landed loose at the top of the project and its bins came out empty.

Seen on a real 675-take project: before the change all 675 takes sat at the top level; after it, every take is in its bin and none is loose (969 media linked, none offline, no errors either way).

## What the change does
In `master_clip`, when the file's media item already exists and sits at the top level (where a sequence's clip items file media), it is moved into the master clip's bin. An item already in a bin stays where it is, so with the same master clip in two bins the first bin wins. The item is in the tree exactly once.

## Tested
New test in `crates/interchange/tests/fcp7.rs`: a stringout sequence ahead of a nested Footage/Comedy bin; the take ends up in Comedy, once. It fails without the change. `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` pass, apart from `filmcraft-gpu`'s `gpu_effects_match_cpu_exactly`, which fails for me on untouched `main` too.

Not in this change: the moved item goes to the end of its bin rather than in document order.

title: project: Clear deletes a bin it is given, with everything in it
author: punkhop
body:
## Problem

No command can delete a bin. `project.delete` (Clear) takes item ids; a bin's id passed to it answers ok and changes nothing. After a Final Cut XML import, once every clip has been moved into new bins, the imported bins stay in the project for good, empty.

## Fix

`project.delete` also accepts bin ids in `items` (bins and items share one id allocator, so an id names one or the other).

- A named bin leaves the tree with its sub-bins, and every item inside goes the way a named item goes: out of the project and off every timeline.
- A bin inside another named bin, or an item that is named and also inside a named bin, is counted once.
- The project's own top bin is never removed.
- The reply now says what went: `{"items": n, "bins": n}` (it was `null`; no caller in the app reads it).
- One undo step brings everything back, as before.

## Not in this PR

- The Project panel still has no way to send a bin to Clear: its Delete sends the item selection, and the bin's right-click menu has no Clear. This PR covers the command, for scripts and agents.
- Clear still needs something selected in the Project panel even when `items` names its targets. That is the existing gate, and it is not changed here.

## Test

`clear_deletes_a_bin_with_everything_in_it` (engine) covers an empty bin, a bin holding a sub-bin holding a clip, undo, overlapping names counted once, and the top bin left alone. It fails before the fix, because the bins stay. `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-engine -p filmcraft-project --all-targets -D warnings`, and `cargo test -p filmcraft-engine -p filmcraft-project` all pass.

title: Windows on ARM64: release builds, tested on ARM64 hardware (#54)
author: echelon
body:
Closes #54.

**Release:**
- `release.yml` builds, signs and packages a **Windows ARM64** MSI and portable zip alongside x64 and x86: `filmcraft-<version>-windows-arm64.msi` and `…-arm64-portable.zip`. The release job already picks up every `release-*` artifact, so they land in the draft release and `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

title: graphics: all eight layer handles scale towards the pointer
author: justjohn12345
body:
Dragging a handle of a graphic layer in the Program monitor scaled about the layer's anchor. A text layer's anchor is at its left edge, so it grew in directions unrelated to the handle being dragged (the bottom-right corner grew it upwards as well as down), and the edge-middle handles were drawn but could not be grabbed.

title: Fonts: use craft-fonts as an optional build input (Japanese UI and title fallback)
author: echelon
body:
Makes [storytold/craft-fonts](https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts) an **optional build input** ([standard](https://github.com/storytold/craftrules/blob/main/standards/fonts.md)) for Japanese in the UI and in titles. Without `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` nothing changes.

### How
- **`crates/text/build.rs`** (the craft-fonts `docs/integration.md` recipe): with `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR=<absolute path of a checkout>` it embeds every font in `fonts/manifest.txt` as `filmcraft_text::fonts::CRAFT_FONTS`. Unset, the slice is empty. A bad dir is a `cargo::warning`, or an error with `CRAFT_FONTS_REQUIRED=1`. On **wasm32** it embeds only BIZ UDPGothic Regular. No network access, and no `Cargo.toml` changes. `filmcraft-text` is the lowest crate that both the UI and the title engine use.
- **UI (`theme.rs`)**: the Jpan faces go at the end of every egui font family, after Inter and JetBrains Mono. BIZ UDPGothic comes first, with Bold first in the `semibold` and `medium` families.
- **Japanese interface (#38, merged)**: `i18n::install_japanese_font` now uses the craft-fonts when they are present, so there's no system scan and it works on the web too. Otherwise it falls back to the installed system font exactly as before.
- **Title engine (`fonts.rs`)**: craft faces are registered after the bundled faces (origin `craft-fonts`). `fallback_for` tries them after the bundled faces and before system faces: Mincho for serif text, Gothic otherwise, then the nearest weight.

### Fonts moved
None. FilmCraft main never bundled a Japanese font, because #38 landed using system fonts only. Binary size without craft-fonts is unchanged.

### Web size
Release `cargo xtask web` (no wasm-opt): **35.1 MB** wasm without craft-fonts and **39.8 MB** with it (BIZ UDPGothic Regular only). Gzipped: 11.4 MB vs 14.4 MB. FilmCraft has no wasm size check. The uncompressed wasm was already above Cloudflare's 25 MiB per-file limit before this PR, so the font doesn't change that situation.

title: NEST1–NEST3: nested sequences safety and Premiere-matching Nest (fixes two crashes)
author: justjohn12345
body:
Nested sequences: safety and correctness. Four commits, based on `main`; no docs.

Behaviour described as Premiere's below was observed in Premiere Pro 26.5.2 on macOS on 2026-10-06, by driving the app with a small test project.

## NEST1: a sequence can never contain itself — fixes two crashes

Nothing stopped a sequence being placed into its own timeline, directly or through another nest. Doing so crashed the app with a stack overflow, in two places:

- **Sound:** nested audio mixing recursed with no depth limit.
- **Picture:** the frame plan's multi-camera shortcut recursed with no depth limit.

Both are reproduced by new tests that aborted with `stack overflow` before the fix.

- **render:** the audio mixer and the multi-camera shortcut now stop at the same depth as the picture (`MAX_NEST_DEPTH`, 8).
- **project:** `Project::nest_cycle` finds a sequence that contains itself.
- **engine:** `Session::edit` refuses any edit that would create one, so it holds for every command (place, Source insert/overwrite, paste, …) without each having to check.
- A project file that already holds such a sequence still opens and can be edited and repaired; only edits that *introduce* a cycle are refused.

Premiere 26.5.2 refuses the same drops, silently. FilmCraft says why: "a sequence cannot be nested inside itself".

## NEST2: Nest… and Make Subsequence as Premiere does them (two commits)

Checked against Premiere Pro 26.5.2:

- **Transitions** whose clips are all nested go into the nest. Before, they were dropped. A test checks the frame in the middle of a transition is the same before and after nesting.
- **The nest never lands on another clip.** Before, it could overlap an unselected clip on the same track. Where it goes now follows Premiere: with L the lowest selected video track and *a* the number of the highest audio track holding selected audio, the picture takes the lowest track T from L up such that T is free for the nest's whole length, and so is every video track num…

title: codecs: look video frames up by the nearest timestamp unit (WebM at 30 fps drops every third frame)
author: EthanSuquet
body:
WebM stores frame timestamps rounded to 1 ms, so at 30 fps frame 2 (66.67 ms) is stored as 67. `MkvSource::video_frame` floored the requested time to 66 and showed frame 1, so every frame whose stamp was rounded up was skipped and its predecessor shown twice. The same bug hit 29.97, 60, 59.94, 24 and 23.976 fps, and MP4/MOV files whose video track uses a 1 ms timescale (`Mp4Source::video_at`, and the web build's WebCodecs path). MPEG-TS/PS and MXF look frames up by index and aren't affected. Export goes through `video_frame`, so this fixes export as well as playback.

- New `Tick::to_rational_round` (nearest unit, halves up, no panic on zero or negative timebases), used for the lookup and the catch-up threshold in `mkv.rs`, `mp4.rs` and `webcodecs.rs`. Exact timebases (90 kHz, 15360, 30000/1001) convert as before; at worst a frame is chosen half a timebase unit early.
- Regression test `crates/codecs/src/rounded_pts_tests.rs`: synthetic MJPEG in WebM (1 ms timestamps) and MOV (1 ms timescale) at 7 frame rates, with both rounded and truncated stamps; each picture encodes its own frame number. Every frame must be shown exactly once over 3 s, and each frame's midpoint must show that frame. Before the fix: `30 fps, Nearest ms stamps: 30 of 90 frames never shown [2, 5, 8, 11]…, 30 shown twice [1, 4, 7, 10]…`. After: 2 passed.
- Unit tests for `to_rational_round` cover the halfway points, negative times and degenerate timebases.

Ran: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-time -p filmcraft-codecs --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test` for time, codecs (ffmpeg oracle tests included), export, render, matroska and isobmff, all green. `webcodecs.rs` wasn't compiled locally (no wasm32 target here); it's a same-signature method swap, so please rely on CI's `cargo xtask wasm`. Not done here: the O(n) `sample_at_pts` scan the issue also mentions.

Fixes #73

title: render: draw layers with an alpha plane on the CPU
author: dcarnelutti
body:
## Problem

A ProRes 4444 layer with transparency (a lower-third banner, an outro, a subscribe bar) is drawn as an opaque black box in the Program monitor, covering the footage under it. Exporting the same sequence is correct.

Cause: the GPU compositor uploads only the Y'CbCr planes of a decoded frame (`prepare_frame` / the `Yuv16 { planes, bits, .. }` arms in `crates/gpu/src/lib.rs`) and never uses the alpha plane. `plan_frame` sent every "plain" layer to the GPU, so a frame with an alpha plane lost it. The CPU compositor handles the alpha, which is why exports were fine.

I found it using a ProRes 4444 overlay (`yuva444p12le`) over H.264 footage. With the overlay track enabled the monitor showed black except the bar itself; with it disabled the footage showed.

## Change

`crates/render/src/plan.rs`: a layer whose decoded frame carries an alpha plane (`Yuv8`/`Yuv16` with `alpha: Some(_)`) is no longer "plain", so it takes the existing CPU-rendered layer path and the alpha is composited correctly. Nine lines.

## Test

`layer_with_alpha_plane_is_drawn_on_the_cpu_and_stays_transparent` in `crates/render/src/tests.rs`. It uses a small `MediaSource` that returns a 4:4:4 10-bit frame with an alpha plane, transparent on the left half. It asserts that the planned layers carry no Y'CbCr frame with alpha, and that the transparent half shows the footage while the opaque half covers it.

It fails without the change ("a layer with an alpha plane reached the GPU path, which drops the alpha") and passes with it. Checking only the composited pixels would not catch this, because `execute_cpu` already handles alpha; the assertion is on the plan.

## What I ran (macOS, Apple Silicon, Rust 1.99)

- `cargo fmt --check`: clean
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --release -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo test --workspace --release --no-fail-fast`: 1775 passed, 1 failed, 39 ignored

title: timeline.move: report the clips an overwrite move covers
author: punkhop
body:
## Problem

`timeline.move` (default, overwrite mode) lands a clip on top of whatever already sits there, as
Premiere's drag does: the clip underneath is shortened, split in two, or removed. The command's
reply only listed the clips it moved, so a script moving clips one at a time (narration lines laid
out in a new order, say) had no way to learn that an earlier move had cut a line it had not reached
yet. The line came out shorter with no error. When the covered part is the head, the remainder also
lives on under a new clip id, so the old id quietly stops existing.

## Solution

The edit itself is unchanged: overwrite-on-drop stays, matching Premiere and the UI drag. The
reply gains `overwritten`, one entry for every clip the move changed without being asked to move:

```json
{"moved": [12], "overwritten": [{"clip": 15, "was": 254016000000, "now": 127008000000, "pieces": [31]}]}
```

- `was` / `now`: its length in ticks before and after (`now: 0`, `pieces: []` = removed).
- `pieces`: the clip ids what is left of it now lives on as (one when trimmed at either end, two
  when the moved clip lands inside it).
- Insert-mode moves shift clips and never cover one, so they always report `[]`.

Refusing the move was considered and rejected: every other overwrite edit (place, paste, the drag)
overwrites, and the UI relies on it.

## Tests

`timeline_move_tests::a_move_that_lands_on_another_clip_reports_what_it_cut`: onto empty space
(nothing reported), over the head of the next clip (shortened, new id named), over the tail
(shortened in place), squarely on top (removed), inside a longer clip (split in two), and an
insert-mode move (nothing covered). Locally: `cargo fmt --check` and the workspace clippy pass, and the
`timeline_move` tests pass; the full workspace test run was not finished locally (the machine was
needed), so this PR's CI is the first full run.

title: h264enc: strict ffmpeg oracle that sees damaged slices (#74)
author: EthanSuquet
body:
ffmpeg's `-ec 0` flags **every multi-slice H.264 picture** as `corrupt decoded frame`, whichever encoder made it: libx264's own streams get the same flag (2 or 4 slices: 28/30 frames; all-intra: 10/10), with unchanged pixels. Single-slice streams are clean. FilmCraft cuts 1080p pictures into 17 slices, hence the 119/120 in #74.

FilmCraft's exports look correct:
- ffmpeg's decode, ffmpeg with `-ec 0`, and VideoToolbox's hardware decode are bit-identical.
- Strict `-err_detect +crccheck+bitstream+buffer+explode -xerror` reports nothing.
- The slice headers check out with `trace_headers`.

The real problem was the oracle (`crates/h264enc/tests/common/mod.rs`): at `-v error -ec 0` a stream with **a whole slice missing** decoded silently.

The oracle now:
- decodes with default concealment at `-v warning` and `-err_detect +crccheck+bitstream+buffer+explode`;
- fails on any decoder output or a non-zero exit;
- still compares every pixel with the encoder's reconstruction, which is what rules out concealment hiding damage.

A new negative control, `oracle_reports_damaged_slices`, drops and truncates slices (CAVLC and CABAC, 3 slices). It fails with the old flags (`the oracle missed a dropped slice in picture 1`) and passes now. The READMEs and `docs/testing.md` are updated.

Ran `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-h264enc --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p filmcraft-h264enc` (debug and release; 9 oracle + 13 unit + 1 doc test) and `cargo xtask layers`, all green; ffmpeg 8.1.1.

This should resolve the corrupt-frame report in #74. The slow rate-control start mentioned there is separate and not addressed, so I've left the issue open for that.

Refs #74

title: codecs: an MP4/MOV clip lasts as long as its edit list plays it
author: EthanSuquet
body:
`Mp4Source` took a clip's duration from the media header (`mdhd`), which runs on the decode timeline. With an edit list, the presentation is the sum of the edits (ISO/IEC 14496-12 §8.6.6, in the movie timescale), as `tkhd` records it. So:
- **every ffmpeg/x264 MP4 with B-frames imported one frame too long** (a 120-frame file became 121 frames), because the edit that skips the reorder delay was ignored;
- a video track delayed by a leading empty edit **lost its last frame**.

Found by running a batch of real-world H.264 and ProRes files through import → decode → export against ffmpeg.

- New `presentation_duration`: the sum of the track's edit `segment_duration`s converted from the movie timescale. It saturates instead of overflowing. Fragmented files, missing edit lists, a zero movie timescale, and edit lists that sum to nothing or overflow a `Tick` all keep the media duration as before.

**Tests:**
- Unit `duration_follows_the_edit_list`: a synthetic four-frame ProRes MOV gives 4 frames with no edits, 3 with a skip-first-frame edit, and 5 with a one-frame empty edit plus all four frames.
- ffmpeg oracle test in `tests/mp4_oracle.rs`: an x264 B-frame MP4 of 60 frames imports as 60 (was 61).

Ran `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings` and `cargo test` for codecs, isobmff, media, export and engine, all green.

title: Ripple trim: a shorter head on a J-cut take is no longer refused
author: punkhop
body:
## Problem

A ripple trim that shortens a clip's head was refused ("this edit would break sync on a sync-locked track")
whenever a sync-locked track had anything in the stretch just BEFORE the cut. With a J cut, the incoming
take's sound sits on a second audio track and starts early, and the outgoing clip's sound runs right up to
the cut on the first audio track. So the J-cut take's head could never be shortened by ripple. A plain cut
got through only because both sounds share one track, and a member's own track skips the check.

Shortening a head takes away the stretch just AFTER the cut: the clip keeps its start, loses its first `d`,
and everything later moves up by `d`. Material on a sync-locked track in that stretch is what would be cut
through. Material before the cut stays where it is.

## Fix

`crates/edit/src/lib.rs`, in both `trim` (ripple mode) and `ripple_trim_group`:

- For a shorter head, the stretch checked on sync-locked tracks is `[cut, cut + d)`, not `[cut - d, cut)`.
  A shorter tail is unchanged (`[end - d, end)`).
- The trimmed clip's own linked partners do not count as "in the way". As before, they are the caller's to
  trim or leave alone (`timeline.trim` puts them in the group; with Linked Selection off they stay put).
  Without this exemption the existing `ripple_trim_group_takes_a_split_edit_along` case refuses, because its
  ungrouped partner on A2 starts at the cut.
- For a head trim, sync-locked tracks ripple from the latest member's start, the picture's cut, whichever
  member was grabbed. Before, grabbing the J cut's early sound checked and shifted from before the cut and was
  refused.
- Unchanged: the final overlap check and `check()`, so a follower with no room still refuses.

## Tests

- `split_edit_ripple_trim_tests::shorter_head_on_a_j_cut_take_shortens_picture_and_sound_together` (engine):
  the J-cut take loses 8 frames from its head through `timeline.trim`. The picture and its early sound keep
  their starts and lose the same 8…

title: Codecs: add clean-room APV (RFC 9924) decoder, encoder, container support, and export presets
author: mweinbach
body:
## Summary

Adds clean-room support for the **APV (Advanced Professional Video, IETF RFC 9924)** video codec across decoding, encoding, container demuxing/muxing, raw `.apv` bitstream playback, and `.mov` export:

- **Clean-room L0 crate (`filmcraft-apv`)**:
  - Implements RFC 9924 (February 2026) access unit / PBU parsing (`aPvF` signature), frame headers, tile grid layout, custom quantization matrices, and metadata PBUs (ITU-T T.35, MDCV, CLL, filler).
  - Supports all 7 standard profiles (`422-10`, `422-12`, `444-10`, `444-12`, `4444-10`, `4444-12`, `400-10`) at 10-bit and 12-bit precision.
  - Even/odd butterfly 1D 8-point IDCT/FDCT decomposition with DC-only block/column fast paths and `rayon` multi-tile / multi-component parallelism.
  - Intra encoder with rate control and ISOBMFF `apvC` (`APVDecoderConfigurationBox`) record builder.
  - Verified **100% bit-exact (`max_diff == 0`)** against FFmpeg (`liboapv` / `apv`) across all profiles, odd dimensions, color spaces, custom Q-matrices, and QP sweep, plus 5,000 mutation/random fuzz iterations under `catch_unwind`.
- **Containers & Media (`filmcraft-isobmff`, `filmcraft-matroska`, `filmcraft-media`, `filmcraft-codecs`)**:
  - ISOBMFF `apv1` sample entry and `apvC` (`APVDecoderConfigurationBox`) demuxing and muxing.
  - Matroska `V_APV` (and VFW `apv1`) demuxing.
  - Standalone `.apv` raw bitstream media source (`ApvSource`) supporting both length-prefixed RFC 9924 §10.1 files and raw `aPvF` streams.
- **Export, Engine & UI (`filmcraft-export`, `filmcraft-engine`, `filmcraft-ui-egui`)**:
  - `Format::Apv` QuickTime `.mov` export (`apv1` + 24-bit PCM audio) with `422-10`, `422-12`, `444-10`, and `444-12` profile selection and HDR metadata signaling (`colr`, `mdcv`, `clli`).
  - Built-in broadcast presets (`APV 422-10` and `APV 422-12`).

title: gpu: upload and composite the alpha plane of Y'CbCr frames
author: dcarnelutti
body:
Supersedes #95, which worked around this by drawing such layers on the CPU. This fixes the cause in the GPU compositor.

## Problem

A ProRes 4444 layer with transparency (a lower-third banner, an outro, a subscribe bar) is drawn opaque in the Program monitor and covers the footage under it. Exporting the same sequence is correct.

The GPU compositor uploaded only the Y, Cb and Cr planes of a `Yuv8`/`Yuv16` frame (the `..` in the `PixelData::Yuv*` arms of `upload` and `prepare_frame`), and the Y'CbCr branch of `sample()` in `composite.wgsl` returned alpha `1.0`. The CPU compositor honours the alpha plane, which is why exports were fine.

I hit it with a ProRes 4444 overlay (`yuva444p12le`) over H.264 footage: with the overlay track enabled the monitor showed black except the bar itself.

## Change

`crates/gpu`:

- Frames with an alpha plane upload it as a fourth texture: `R8Unorm` for `Yuv8`, `R16Float` for `Yuv16` (converted like the other planes, through `prepare_frame` when the plan was prepared beforehand). Frames without one bind the dummy texture.
- `tex_entry(5)` is added to `layer_bgl` and `blend_bgl`, and binding 5 is set at the four places that build layer bind groups (layers, the fx source pass, the blend path, `effect_image`).
- Uniform slot `p3.y` carries the alpha scale (0 = no alpha plane; 1 for 8-bit; `2^bits / (2^bits - 1)` for `Yuv16`, whose f16 codes are `code / 2^bits`).
- `composite.wgsl`: with an alpha plane, `sample()` reads the alpha at full resolution and returns the linear colour premultiplied by it, which is what the rest of the pipeline expects.

## Test

`gpu_draws_yuv_alpha_plane_like_the_cpu` in `crates/gpu/src/tests.rs` composites an alpha ramp (transparent on the left, opaque on the right) over an opaque layer at 8, 10 and 12 bits, on the GPU and with the CPU compositor, and compares them (p99 <= 3, max <= 8). It also checks that the transparent edge shows the background and the opaque edge covers it.

title: NEST4–NEST8: nest toggle, sequences as sources, Reveal in Project, Multi-Camera submenu
author: justjohn12345
body:
Editing with nested sequences: the nest toggle, sequences as sources, Reveal in Project, and the Multi-Camera submenu. One commit per task.

**Stacked on #78 and #82.** The branch merges both, because it touches the clip context menu from #78 and builds on the nest code from #82. Until they merge, the diff here also shows their commits; review the four `NEST4`–`NEST8` commits at the top.

## NEST4: the nest toggle

The Timeline button "Insert and overwrite sequences as nests or individual clips" was drawn always on and did nothing. It now toggles (`sequence.nestSequences`, state `sequences_as_clips`).

- **On (default):** a sequence edits in as one nest, as before.
- **Off:** a sequence edits in as its clips. This follows what Premiere Pro 26.5.2 does: the clips come with their transitions and links, the source's tracks that hold clips go to consecutive tracks from the destination track up (source V1 and V3 land on the destination track and the one above), and missing tracks are added.
- A sequence can go into itself as clips; as a nest it is still refused.
- Multi-camera source sequences stay one clip either way.

It applies wherever a sequence is edited in: drag and drop, `timeline.place`, Source Monitor Insert and Overwrite.

## NEST5: a sequence in the Source Monitor — fixes a bug

Mark In / Mark Out on a sequence loaded in the Source Monitor did nothing: the marks were only stored for media, and the command reported success. They are now the sequence's own In and Out, so Insert and Overwrite edit in the marked part, as a nest or as clips.

Tests also pin Match Frame on a nest: it loads the nested sequence at the frame the nest shows, through a trim and a speed change. That already worked.

title: Nested sequences: rendering fidelity (sizes, speed, effects, captions, waveforms)
author: justjohn12345
body:
Phase 3 of nested-sequence parity with Premiere Pro: how a nest looks and sounds.

**Stacked on #112** (which contains #78 and #82). Only the last three commits are new; review those, and merge after #112.

## What changes

**NEST9 — a nest of another size or frame rate**
- A nested sequence whose frame size differs from the sequence it is in comes in centred at its own size, Scale 100. The clip context menu gains "Fit to frame" and "Fill frame" next to "Scale to Frame Size" (the commands already existed).
- Tests pin a smaller nest, a larger nest (cropped by the frame), a nest at another frame rate, and Fit / Fill / Scale to Frame Size on a nest.

**NEST10 — speed, effects and captions on a nest**
- Sound: a nest's audio went around the path media clips take, so speed, reverse and the clip's audio effects did nothing to it, and a nested sequence at another sample rate was mixed at the outer rate without converting (wrong pitch and length). The nested mix is now read through the same path as a media source: mixed at the nested sequence's own rate, resampled, then through speed, reverse and effects. The nesting depth limit from #82 still applies.
- Captions: the captions of a nested sequence are drawn as part of the nest's picture. The preview cache key of a nest now covers its caption tracks.

**NEST11 — frame plan and waveforms**
- A plain nest (same frame size and colour settings as its parent, nothing on the clip that changes the picture, every layer inside blended normally, not a multicam angle) contributes its own layers to the frame plan, so the GPU composites them instead of receiving one CPU-rendered image. Anything else is planned as one image as before.
- A nest's sound clip gets a waveform: the nested sequence is mixed in the background (under `catch_unwind`), and mixed again when its sound changes; the old waveform stays until the new one is ready.

title: Nested sequences: interchange (AAF compositions, OMF rendered sound, EDL reel AX)
author: justjohn12345
body:
Phase 5 of nested-sequence parity with Premiere Pro: nests in exported and imported timelines. This is the last phase of the plan.

**Stacked on #115** (which is stacked on #113 and #112). Only the last four commits are new; review those, and merge after #115.

## What Premiere Pro 26.5.2 does

I exported a sequence with a nest from Premiere in every interchange format it offers and read the files (they are Premiere's output for a test project; nothing inside the application was read).

| Format | A nested sequence in Premiere's file | FilmCraft before | FilmCraft now |
|---|---|---|---|
| EDL | one event, reel `AX`, the nest's name as clip name | one event, but the reel came from the name (`NESTED_S`) although the report said `AX` | reel `AX` |

**AAF export.** A nested sequence is written as a composition mob, and its clips as source clips that point at it. Nests in nests are followed; a nest used twice is written once. With embedded or consolidated audio, the media of the clips inside a nest is prepared too.

title: Sequence: Add Tracks… opens Premiere's dialog (amount, placement, track type)
author: justjohn12345
body:

title: codecs: MP4/MOV pixel format and alpha come from hvcC, avcC and the ProRes frame header (#103)
author: HEOJUNFO
body:
Fixes #103.

For MP4/MOV, `probe` / `MediaInfo.video` took the pixel format from the codec profile alone. HEVC reported `""`, H.264 High 4:2:2 had no bit depth, and ProRes 4444 reported alpha because of its fourcc.

- **HEVC:** chroma format and bit depth now come from `hvcC`.
- **H.264:** they come from the `avcC` High-profile extension (ISO/IEC 14496-15 §5.3.3), or else from the first SPS. If neither can be read, the format is left empty (unknown) rather than guessed.
- **ProRes:** the first frame header gives the chroma format and alpha (`alpha_channel_type`), the same way the first DNx frame header already does. A 4444 fourcc no longer means alpha.

Labels keep the existing `"YUV 4:2:2 10-bit"` / `"YUVA 4:4:4 12-bit"` style.

| Source (ffmpeg 9.0.2) | ffprobe | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| libx265 yuv420p | yuv420p | `""` | `YUV 4:2:0 8-bit` |
| libx265 yuv420p10le | yuv420p10le | `""` | `YUV 4:2:0 10-bit` |
| libx265 yuv422p10le | yuv422p10le | `""` | `YUV 4:2:2 10-bit` |
| libx264 yuv422p | yuv422p | `YUV 4:2:2` | `YUV 4:2:2 8-bit` |
| libx264 high422 yuv422p10le | yuv422p10le | `YUV 4:2:2` | `YUV 4:2:2 10-bit` |
| prores_ks 4444, no alpha | yuv444p12le | `YUVA 4:4:4 12-bit`, alpha | `YUV 4:4:4 12-bit`, no alpha |
| prores_ks 4444, alpha | yuva444p12le | `YUVA 4:4:4 12-bit`, alpha | `YUVA 4:4:4 12-bit`, alpha |

## Tests
- New unit tests in `mp4.rs`. They fail on `main` and pass here:
  - hvcC 4:2:0/4:2:2 at 8/10-bit

author: justjohn12345
body:
Scrolling the Timeline had three problems. Independent of the other open PRs; based on main.

## What was wrong

1. **Cmd + wheel zoomed**, the same as Option + wheel. egui turns Cmd + wheel into a zoom before the panel sees it.
2. **The plain wheel scrolled sideways.** The tracks could only be scrolled up and down with Shift held.

title: Control: close the connection on input that isn't a request (#119)
author: Luskish
body:
Fixes #119.

The desktop control server answered a line that wasn't JSON with an error, then kept reading. A web page can send an HTTP POST to `127.0.0.1:<port>` with `fetch(..., {mode: "no-cors"})`. The server rejected the request line and headers, then ran the JSON body as a command. So while `--control` was open, any page in the user's browser could drive the app.

This ports the fix LightCraft shipped for the same bug (storytold/lightcraft#94, PR storytold/lightcraft#129), so the two apps' control servers behave the same way:

- Every line must be a JSON object with a string `method`. Anything else (an HTTP request line, other non-JSON text, a JSON array, an object without `method`, invalid UTF-8) gets one error reply, and the server closes the connection. Nothing sent after it on that connection runs.
- A request line longer than 4 MiB is refused without buffering all of it.
- At most 16 connections are served at once. Further connections get an error line and are closed.
- `docs/control-protocol.md` describes the rules.

`filmcraft-cli --bridge` and `mcp --bridge` send one JSON request object per line, so they work unchanged.

This doesn't add authentication (option 2 in the issue). The port is still open to other local processes while it's enabled. PhotoCraft's token handshake (storytold/photocraft#61) could follow in a separate PR if you want it.

**Tests** (`apps/filmcraft/src/control_server.rs`):

- `http_request_closes_before_the_body_runs` replays the issue's browser POST. Before the fix it failed with `nothing may run: ["engine.execute"]`.
- `non_request_json_closes_the_connection`, `a_request_before_junk_still_runs`, `overlong_line_is_refused`, `tcp_connection_is_closed_after_junk` and `extra_connections_are_refused` cover the other rules, and also failed before the fix.

title: Ripple trim: a shorter head after an L cut keeps the earlier sound in place
author: punkhop
body:
Stacked on #104 (J cut): includes its commits; merge #104 first.

## Problem

A ripple trim that shortens a clip's head was refused ("this edit would break sync on a sync-locked track")
when the previous clip's sound runs on past the cut on a sync-locked track (an L cut):

```
V1  a [0,10)          b [10,20)
A1  a's sound [0,13)              (linked to a, runs 3 into b)
```

Ripple-trim b's head by 3: refused, because a's sound crosses the stretch that closes. But a never moves,
so its sound has no reason to move either: it can stay where it is, and the L cut still ends at 13.

## Fix

`crates/edit/src/lib.rs`, `ripple_trim_group`: on a sync-locked track that holds no member of the trimmed
group, an item does not count as "in the way" of a shorter head when it

- starts before the cut,
- is linked to at least one other clip, and every clip it is linked to ends at or before the cut (the
  previous take), and
- is not one of the trimmed clips' own partners (those stay the caller's to trim or leave).

It stays where it is. Everything else is unchanged:

- Unlinked material across the cut (a music bed) still refuses, and so does a clip whose link has no
  partner left, and a linked cutaway whose own picture also reaches past the cut.
- The final overlap check still runs, so later material on that track moving up onto the L cut's sound
  refuses.
- Shorter tails (Edge::Out) are untouched.

## Tests

- `tests::shorter_head_into_an_l_cut_keeps_the_earlier_sound_where_it_is` (edit): the case above is
  accepted, the sound stays at [0,13) and later pictures move up 3. Later material on A1 that would land on

title: Icons: draw straight lines on whole device pixels
author: punkhop
body:
## What was wrong
The panel menu mark (≡) on the active tab was three hand-drawn 1.5 pt lines at fractional positions. At 1x they straddled pixels, and anti-aliasing made the gaps look uneven: 3 px, then 4 px. Every line icon drawn by the icon pen had the same half-pixel blur.

## What changed
- The icon pen (`Pen16` in `crates/ui-egui/src/icons.rs`) draws strokes a whole number of device pixels wide (at least 1). A half pixel rounds down, so 1.25 pt becomes 1 px at 1x and 2 px at 2x.
- Every horizontal or vertical segment snaps onto the pixel grid. So does any segment that runs less than a pixel sideways, since it draws straight anyway. Lines with an odd pixel width sit on pixel centres; ends land on pixel edges.
- Offsets are rounded from the icon's centre, the same way on both sides. Equal steps on the 16 grid stay equal on screen, which gives the menu mark two equal gaps.
- Slanted lines, curves and fills keep their exact positions.
- The tab's menu mark is now `Icon::Hamburger` drawn by the pen (`dock.rs`), replacing its own hand-drawn lines. The Audio Track Mixer's menu mark already used the icon.

## Tests
- `icons::tests::straight_lines_land_on_whole_pixels`: every icon, at 1x and 2x, at four sizes, in a rect off the pixel grid. Every straight stroke must be a whole number of pixels wide, with its middle where that width needs it.
