title: HE-AAC plays at its output rate; AAC export caps the bitrate (#108, parts 1–2)
author: carlitosteso3
body:
Addresses parts 1 and 2 of #108. Part 3 is **not** fixed: I could not reproduce it (see below), so this PR doesn't close the issue.

## 1. Sequence from an HE-AAC clip created at 22050 Hz
The MP4 reader reported the rate from the start of the AudioSpecificConfig, which for HE-AAC is the core rate. Our decoder decodes only the AAC-LC core, so the decoded audio was consistently half the output rate.

- **`filmcraft-aac`:** the decoder records SBR fill elements (`EXT_SBR_DATA` / `EXT_SBR_DATA_CRC`). `Decoder::sbr()` is true for explicit (AOT 5/29) and implicit signalling.
- **`filmcraft-codecs`:**
  - New `aac_output_rate(asc, first_units)` returns the extension rate (explicit), or twice a ≤ 24 kHz core when the first access units carry SBR data (implicit, §1.6.5).
  - The MP4 reader now reports that rate.
  - `PacketDecoder::aac` now uses our decoder for any config it reads, including explicit HE-AAC, which previously went to symphonia. When the stream rate is twice the core rate, it interpolates the core with `Upsample2x`.
- **`Upsample2x`:** a streaming half-band Blackman-windowed-sinc 2× interpolator, 24 taps.
  - Its state carries across packets, so a seek primed with the preceding packet gives the same samples as continuous decoding.
  - Latency is 12 core samples (≈0.5 ms at 22.05 kHz).

**Limitation:** the SBR high band is still not reconstructed. HE-AAC now has the right rate, duration, pitch and level, but no content above the core's Nyquist (≈11 kHz). A real SBR decoder would replace the upsampler and fits a separate PR.

## 2. H.264 export fails with "bitrate out of range"
`aac_factory` asked for the default 320 kbps, which is more than AAC's 6144-bit frame limit allows at 22.05 kHz stereo (6 bits per sample and channel = 264.6 kbps). The bitrate is now capped at that limit instead of failing. Any 22.05 kHz or lower sequence hit this, not only HE-AAC sources.

I don't have an HE-AAC encoder on Windows (`…

title: Audio: mix playback 200 ms ahead so a busy Mac doesn't drop sound
author: punkhop
body:
## Problem

Playing a sequence on a loaded Mac crackles and drops out, at a different spot on every play. Playback
decoded and mixed each device buffer (512 frames, ~10.7 ms at 48 kHz) inside the cpal output callback:
AAC decode, the mixer graph (plan rebuild, rayon `par_iter`, the graph-state cache lock), the source's
audio mutex, and opening a clip's file the first time a cut reaches it. Any stall there missed the device's
deadline. Nothing was buffered ahead, nothing counted underruns.

## Change

- `crates/ui-egui/src/play_ahead.rs` (desktop only): the mix runs on a `filmcraft-audio-mix` thread into a
  single-producer/single-consumer ring of `AtomicU32` slots (no `unsafe`) kept `LEAD_S` = 200 ms ahead. The
  device callback only copies samples; it never decodes, allocates or locks. The first 1024-frame block is
  mixed before the stream starts, so playback opens with sound.
- Underrun: the callback plays silence for the missing frames, counts it, and the mixer skips the same span,
  so sound stays locked to the playhead (which still follows `played_frames`).
- Mixer panic → caught (`catch_unwind`), logged, playback continues silent. The thread stops when the stream
  drops its callback.
- A device with a different channel count than the mix (wider interface, aggregate device, device switched
  since the count was read) plays the shared channels and zeroes the rest.
- `AudioOut::channels()` (default 2; cpal reports the stream config's count).
- `perf.stats` → `playback.audio`: `callbacks`, `underruns`, `missingFrames`, `minLeadMs`.
- The program mix moved unchanged into `pub fn playback_mix(session, seq, rate)` (one fix: a missing sequence
  now zeroes the buffer instead of leaving it unwritten).
- Web: unchanged behavior (no threads); it keeps mixing in its callback.
- Edits made while playing are heard ~200 ms later.

## Tests

- `crates/ui-egui/tests/play_ahead.rs` (own binary: one test panics a mixer on purpose, and the crash hook's
  test reads the process-…

title: Audio: play a sequence on a device at another rate without phase jumps
author: punkhop
body:
Stacked on #131 (audio plays ahead): includes its commits; merge #131 first.

## Problem

When the output device runs at another rate than the sequence (a 44.1 kHz device playing a 48 kHz
sequence), playback converted each device buffer on its own:

- the block's source start was truncated (`s0 = cursor × seq_sr / sr`), so the fractional phase was lost at
  every block boundary: up to a sample of jitter per buffer, heard as a buzz;
- each output sample took the nearest source sample (no interpolation), which aliases;
- each block asked the mixer for `n × seq_sr / sr + 2` frames starting at the truncated `s0`, so the next
  request never continued where the last one ended. The mixer's graph-state cache (keyed on the previous
  request's end) missed on every buffer, rebuilding effect state and preroll each time: more CPU in the audio
  callback, and effect tails restarting.

## Change

- `crates/audio-dsp/src/resample.rs`: `StreamResampler`. Every output sample's source position comes from
  its absolute output frame as an exact rational (`frame × from / to`) and is linearly interpolated, so the
  output is bit-identical however the stream is cut into blocks. Source frames are pulled in contiguous,
  non-overlapping spans (it holds the one or two frames a block boundary needs), so the mixer sees one
  continuous stream. A seek starts it afresh. Output lags the source by one source sample (~21 µs at
  48 kHz). Zero rates are treated as 1 Hz; short or missing channels read as silence.
- `playback_mix` uses it whenever the device rate differs from the sequence rate, and starts it afresh when
  the sequence's rate or channel layout changes while playing. Same-rate playback is untouched.

## Tests (`crates/audio-dsp/src/resample.rs`)

- Output identical when cut into one block, 512-frame blocks, 333-frame blocks and mixed 1/7/512/64 blocks,
  for 48→44.1, 44.1→48, 48→96 and 96→48 kHz.

## Summary

Hardware H.264 + HEVC decoding on Windows through Media Foundation + Direct3D 11 / DXVA, plugged into the existing architecture (`VideoDecoder` factory registry, `HybridDecoder`, the Hardware decoding setting, `perf.stats` counters). Progress on #30 (does not close it).

- New backend `crates/platform/src/media_foundation/`; `register()` / `registered()` / `hardware_decoder_for()` cover Windows, so the desktop app, `filmcraft-cli` / MCP and the bench get it through the same entry points (explicit tests for desktop and CLI).
- H.264 Baseline / Main / High 8-bit, HEVC Main 8-bit, HEVC Main 10, 4:2:0 progressive. Everything else is declined up front and our decoder is used.
- Fallback is the existing `HybridDecoder` (our clean-room decoder, never Windows' software decoding).

## Architecture

```
avcC/hvcC sample -> Annex B -> decoder MFT --DXVA--> NV12 / P010 D3D11 texture
                                                     | staging texture (the one GPU->CPU copy)

```

- The decoder MFT is driven per access unit (no Source Reader: the demuxer already delivers samples). (On this machine `MFTEnumEx(HARDWARE)` returns no H.264/HEVC decoder MFTs; NVIDIA exposes decode through DXVA, not as a hardware MFT.)

title: Hardening: hostile MP4 edit lists and cyclic subclip chains (#66)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #66.

- **codecs** (`crates/codecs/src/mp4.rs`): a resampled MP4 audio read scaled the edit-list offset to the source rate as `audio_offset * src_rate` in i64, which a hostile `media_time` overflows. It's now computed in i128 and clamped, and the window arithmetic downstream saturates.
- **engine** (`crates/engine/src/lib.rs`): `media_duration` recursed through a subclip's parent chain with no bound. It's now a loop capped at 16 hops (`MAX_SUBCLIP_CHAIN`) that returns `None` past that.

Regression tests, both checked to fail without the fix:
- `hostile_audio_edit_offset_never_overflows`: panicked with arithmetic overflow at `mp4.rs:392`.
- `clip_ops_tests::a_cyclic_subclip_chain_has_no_media_duration`: stack overflow, then abort.

`cargo fmt`, `clippy -D warnings` and `cargo test` pass for `filmcraft-codecs` and `filmcraft-engine`.

title: Tests: image-sequence oracle fixtures are written atomically (#125)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #125.

**Cause:** `make_sequence` in `crates/codecs/tests/media_oracle.rs` had ffmpeg write the twelve numbered stills straight into the shared `seq_<ext>` fixture directory, and treated it as ready as soon as `img_0001` and `img_0012` existed. `png_sequence_exact` and `missing_frames_hold_the_previous_frame` both generate `seq_png`, so when they run together one can read PNGs the other is still writing, or two ffmpeg processes rewrite the same files with `-y`. A half-written frame doesn't decode, and the image-sequence source then holds the previous frame (documented behaviour), which is why frame 6 compared equal to frame 3. This bypassed the atomic `testkit::fixtures` contract described in `docs/testing.md`.

**Reproduction:** six parallel test processes on a fresh `FILMCRAFT_FIXTURES_DIR`, 20 rounds. The old code failed **18/120** runs, including the reported `assert_ne!(at(6), at(3))`, plus open-time and hold-assertion variants. The new code failed **0/120**.

**Fix:** ffmpeg writes into a `testkit::fixtures::temp_path` directory, which is renamed into place only when all twelve frames exist (with a `.complete` marker). A racer that loses keeps the winner's copy. The cache directory is now `seq_<ext>_v2`, so a half-written directory left by the old generator is never reused. The missing-frame test's gap copy is now private to the test and removed afterwards. All assertions are unchanged.

title: MCP: render_frame and render_preview leave the playhead where it was (#114)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #114.

`render_frame` and `render_preview` advertise `readOnlyHint: true`, but a call with `seconds` moved the active sequence's playhead to that time, and with Selection Follows Playhead on it also changed the selection. That happened in headless and bridge mode alike.

title: h264enc: 1-pass bitrate modes no longer starve the opening second
author: EthanSuquet
body:
1-pass VBR/CBR priced its one-second virtual history once, at frame 0, from the initial model guess (`ratecontrol.rs`). Instrumented, that virtual cost was about 250× the real per-frame cost, so the first second of every bitrate-mode export was coded far too coarsely (6–9 dB softer).

**Fix:** each virtual frame now costs the running average of the P/B frames coded so far, recomputed every frame. The initial guess is only used until the first P frame.

**Test:** `vbr_opening_second_is_not_starved` in `tests/ffmpeg_oracle.rs` (synthetic 640×360p60 at 2 Mb/s, decoded by ffmpeg):
- Before: `opening 25.02 dB, after 1 s 33.56 dB` (fails).
- After: `opening 32.09 dB, after 1 s 32.98 dB, 1949.9 kbps` (passes; same bitrate).

Frame 0 itself still depends on the initial guess. The other half of #74 (the strict oracle) was fixed in #101.

Ran `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-h264enc --all-targets -- -D warnings`, all h264enc tests and the export tests, all green. Checked on synthetic content only, not the issue's own clip.

Fixes #74

title: automation: a blocking export over the bridge runs as a polled job
author: EthanSuquet
body:
In bridge mode, `file.exportMedia` with `wait: true` was forwarded to the app unchanged (CLI `exec`, MCP `run`). The app encoded on its UI thread and the control channel replied `timeout` after 60 s, while the export carried on and later succeeded. The long-export path with progress and cancel only existed for `Backend::Headless`.

**Fix:**
- New `BridgeClient::execute` starts the export without `wait`, polls `jobs.list` until the job finishes, and returns the same `{job, path, result}` as headless mode.
- The CLI and MCP both use it, and MCP's long-export path (progress notifications and cancel) now runs in bridge mode too.
- `docs/agents.md` is updated to match.

Exports over 60 s now return their result (CLI exit 0, MCP non-error) instead of `app: timeout`. The app keeps showing "Exporting… NN%" and answers other requests meanwhile.

**Tests:** two new tests against a stand-in control channel.
- Before: MCP returns `"text":"app: timeout","isError":true`.
- After: both tests pass, exactly one export is started, and progress notifications arrive.

Ran `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings`, the automation and CLI tests and `cargo xtask layers`, all green.

Not covered:
- This wasn't exercised against the real desktop app; it needs a GUI.
- A raw control-channel client that sends `wait: true` itself still encodes on the UI thread, so #92 stays open for that case.
- On MCP cancel, a relative export path is deleted from the MCP process's working directory, which may differ from the app's.

Fixes #91

title: Windows: zero-copy hardware decode (D3D11 surface to wgpu DX12)
author: SaymonMaster14
body:
**Stacked on #141** (Windows Media Foundation decode): the first two commits of this branch are #141's; review only the last two (`c4b0f40`, `8e68cd3`) until it merges, then I rebase. Progress on #30 (the "zero-copy" item), does not close it.

## Summary

Decoded pictures no longer cross to the CPU on Windows: they stay in GPU memory and the compositor samples the decoder's memory directly. Needs a wgpu **DX12** renderer on the decoder's GPU; otherwise nothing changes (Vulkan, CPU readback as in #141).

## Design (details in `docs/adr/0002-zero-copy-decode-interop.md`, which needs maintainer approval like ADR 0001)

```
MFT --DXVA--> decoder texture --GPU copy (cropped)--> shareable NV12/P010 D3D11 texture (NT handle)
                                                          | OpenSharedHandle (D3D12) + wgpu::hal::dx12, plane-sliced
                                                          v
                          wgpu R8/Rg8 (R16/Rg16 for 10-bit) planes --> compositor kind 3 (luma + interleaved chroma)
```

- `frame`: `PixelData::Gpu(GpuPixels)` over a `GpuSurface` trait (no OS/wgpu types; wasm check passes). `VideoFrame::cpu()` downloads once and caches; `to_linear_f32…`, `to_rgba8`, `luma8`, `rotated` go through it, so code that doesn't know GPU pictures keeps working. `byte_size` counts GPU memory (cache budgets hold). `box_decimated` returns `None` for GPU pictures (the GPU sampler minifies).
- `platform` (`media_foundation::{interop,surface}`): the `unsafe` (shared texture, hal wrap) lives in FFI module `interop` under ADR 0001's rules. D3D11->D3D12 sync is an `ID3D11Query` event wait (GPU only, no pixel copy). `enable_zero_copy(&wgpu::Device)` checks DX12 + same adapter (LUID) and registers the importer; `hw::set_gpu_frames` is the process switch (also cleared when the UI drops the GPU compositor after a GPU error).
- `gpu`: `set_surface_importer`, compositor texture kind 3, import failure falls back to download + upload (logged).

title: Bridge: a blocking export runs as an app job, so it neither times out nor freezes the app (#91, #92)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #91, fixes #92.

**Cause:** `file.exportMedia` with `wait: true` was forwarded to the app unchanged, so the app encoded on its UI thread. While that ran, it showed no progress and answered no other control request (#92). The control server's 60 s reply limit then reported `timeout` for any longer export, which went on and succeeded anyway (#91).

**Fix:** `BridgeClient::execute` (`crates/automation/src/bridge.rs`) starts a blocking export as an app job (`wait: false`) and polls `jobs.list` every 250 ms until it finishes. It returns the same `{job, path, result}` a blocking export does, or `export failed: …`. Both `filmcraft-cli --bridge … exec` and the MCP server's bridge backend use it. MCP `command_run` in bridge mode now also goes through the long-job path, so it gets the same `notifications/progress` and cancellation as headless mode. `docs/agents.md` is updated.

**Tests:**
- Unit tests against a fake control server check that `wait: true` never reaches the app, the export starts exactly once, the result and errors come back, and other commands are forwarded unchanged.
- End to end against the desktop app (`filmcraft --control`): a blocking ProRes export of the demo project through `filmcraft-cli --bridge exec` returned its 642-frame result with exit status 0, and `ui.inspect` on another connection was answered in about 0.05 s throughout the export.

That run took 17 s, so it shows the app stays responsive. The over-60-s case follows from the design: each request is now a short poll.

`clippy -D warnings` and the `filmcraft-automation` tests pass.

title: Playback: a stalled audio device no longer freezes the playhead (#136)
author: carlitosteso3
body:
Refs #136. This is the likely cause rather than a confirmed one: I could only test on Windows, where Play works. @Mystical-17, could you check whether a build with this change plays on your Linux setup, and whether the status bar then says the audio output is not responding? That would confirm it.

## Cause
The playhead follows the audio clock: `advance_playback` uses `AudioOut::played_frames()`, the frames the device callback has consumed. On the desktop, `CpalOut::start` succeeds once the stream is built and `play()` returns. If the device then never calls back, `played_frames()` stays at 0, `elapsed` stays 0, and the playhead never moves. This happens with ALSA when the device is busy, or when the ALSA → PulseAudio/PipeWire bridge doesn't run. Play and Space then do nothing, with no message; cpal's error callback only goes to stderr. That matches #136 (Linux AppImage), and #23 / #106 report ALSA trouble on Linux too.

## Change
- `Playback` notes when the audio clock last moved (`audio_seen`, reset when the preroll ends and audio starts).
- **Stall watchdog:** if the clock stands still for `AUDIO_STALL_S` = 1 s while playing, playback continues on the wall clock from where the audio got to.
  - The stream is stopped, so it can't resume out of sync.
  - A `log::warn!` is written.
  - The status bar says: "Audio output is not responding: playing without sound (check Settings ▸ Audio Hardware)".
- The clock is now read once per frame. A device that plays is unaffected: it keeps driving the clock, with no message.

1 s leaves room for devices that are slow to deliver their first callback, such as Bluetooth, while keeping a broken device from freezing playback for long.

## Tests
New `crates/ui-egui/tests/playback_clock_ui.rs` drives the app with a fake `AudioOut` (kittest harness, 0.25 s steps):
- `a_stalled_audio_device_does_not_freeze_playback`: the stream opens, but the device never consumes. On `main` the playhead stays at 0.00 s after 4 s of simulated playback. …

title: Packaging: the Flatpak can read a project's media wherever it lives (#107)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #107.

The Flatpak manifest granted only `--filesystem=xdg-pictures`, on the premise that the file-chooser and document portals make filesystem access unnecessary. That doesn't hold for a video editor. A `.fcproj` refers to its media by absolute path (`docs/project-files.md`), and the document portal exposes only the file it was handed, not the media beside it. So a project in ~/Videos or ~/Music opened with every clip missing.

The manifest now grants `--filesystem=home` plus the usual external-drive mount points: `/media`, `/run/media` and `/mnt`, where footage often lives. That covers media, project folders, exports and the autosave next to a project. Other video editors on Flathub do much the same. Nothing system-wide is granted, and Open/Save dialogs still use the file-chooser portal. The comment in the manifest explains the choice.

I checked that the manifest still parses with the same `id` and `command`, which packaging-lint asserts. I didn't build a Flatpak here, and the release doesn't build one either.

title: Windows: VP9 + AV1 hardware decode (Media Foundation / DXVA)
author: SaymonMaster14
body:
**Stacked on #141** (Windows Media Foundation decode): everything before the last commit is #141's; review only the last commit (`Windows: VP9 + AV1 hardware decode ...`) until it merges, then I rebase. Progress on #30, does not close it. Independent of the zero-copy draft (#152).

## Summary

VP9 (profiles 0 and 2) and AV1 (main, 8- and 10-bit) hardware decoding on Windows, through the same Media Foundation / Direct3D 11 / DXVA path, `HybridDecoder` fallback, setting and `perf.stats` counters as H.264 / HEVC. 4:2:0 only.

## Design

- `codecs::hw::FrameStreamInfo` (from `vpcC` / `av1C`): profile, bit depth, chroma format, picture size, random-access samples and in-band format changes, with the **colour and size read from the bitstream the way the software decoders do** (`hw_frame::vp9_color` / `av1_color` are now shared by `Vp9Decoder` / `Av1Decoder` and the hardware path, so the two cannot drift). `hw::StreamInfo` (NAL or frame-coded) lets `HybridDecoder` find restart points and parameter changes for any of the four codecs; existing callers compile unchanged (`impl Into<StreamInfo>`).
- `platform::media_foundation::stream`: per codec, which stream the GPU can do (DXVA profile + format + size), the MFT request (subtype, attributes) and the MFT input. H.264 / HEVC go in as Annex B as before; **VP9 frames / superframes and AV1 temporal units go in as they are in the container** (the `av1C` sequence header first after a seek). The MFTs (`VP9VideoExtensionDecoder`, `AV1VideoExtension`) output only shown pictures in presentation order, so hidden alt-ref frames and `show_existing_frame` need no handling.
- VP9 colour/size come from the key frame header at each random-access sample; the MFT's declared picture size (display aperture, since its surfaces are aligned: 640x368 for 640x360) is checked against the stream's, so a decoder that disagrees fails the stream (fallback) instead of cropping or showing padding.

title: Media Browser: probing a file doesn't read it whole (#157)
author: carlitosteso3
body:
Refs #157. This fixes a real disk/memory cost in the Media Browser, but I couldn't reproduce the reporter's exact case with MP4 files, so it may not be the whole story. Details below, and I've asked the reporter about their folder.

## What I measured (Windows 11, v0.2.1 and `main`)
**MP4 is fine.** The probe reads only the index. With 288 MB 1080p files (instrumented `ByteReader` around `open_reader`):
- faststart: 0.2 MB read
- `moov` at the end: 0.2 MB
- fragmented (`frag_keyframe+empty_moov`): 0.1 MB in 194 reads

With 30 such files in Thumbnails view, the app read about 12 MB in total and then stayed idle. List view read nothing, because the default columns need no probe.

**Formats without a reader opener are read whole.** `open_reader` falls back to reading the entire file for the byte openers. Measured with `filmcraft-cli exec mediaBrowser.probe`:

| File | Size | Peak memory before | After this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `camera.avi` (unsupported, so the result is "not media") | 290 MB | **518 MB**, full read | 6 MB |
| `entrevista.wav` (24-bit stereo, 15 min) | 247 MB | **500 MB**, full read | 5 MB |

So a folder of multi-GB AVI, WAV or MP3 files gets read in full, and buffered twice in memory, just to show properties. For AVI that's only to find out it isn't supported.

## Change
- **`filmcraft-media`:** new `reader::open_reader_within(name, reader, reader_openers, extra, max_whole)`. Reader openers are tried first, as before. A file none of them takes is read whole only if it is ≤ `max_whole`; otherwise it is refused with `MediaError::Unsupported` after reading only the 64 KiB sniffing head. `open_reader` is `open_reader_within(.., u64::MAX)`, so its behaviour is unchanged.

title: Graphics: point text and paragraph text, as Premiere has them
author: justjohn12345
body:
Text layers had one kind of handle: every handle stretched the layer away from its opposite side. Premiere has two kinds of text layer, and their handles do different things. This adds both, and the way to switch a layer between them. Independent of other open PRs; based on main.

## What Premiere does

Checked against Premiere Pro 2026 on macOS by driving the app (clicks and drags in the Program monitor, numbers read from Effect Controls):

| | Point text | Paragraph text |
|---|---|---|
| Made with the Type tool by | a click | a drag: the dragged rectangle is the box |
| Lines | only where Return was typed | wrap at the box's width; lines below the box are hidden and the bottom-right handle turns into a red plus |
| Dragging a handle | scales the layer about its anchor point. Every handle, the edge ones too, scales both axes alike; Font Size is untouched | moves that side or corner of the box to the pointer, the opposite side stays; the text re-wraps and Scale is untouched |
| Anchor point of a new layer | left end of the first baseline | the box's top-left corner |

- The anchor point can be dragged; the layer stays where it is (Position and Anchor Point change together). It is picked before anything under it.
- Properties ▸ Text ▸ wrench opens **Text Properties**, whose **Text Layer Type** list switches a layer between Point Text and Paragraph Text. The text stays where it is.

## What this PR does

All of the above:

- **Type tool:** a click still makes point text; a drag on empty picture makes paragraph text in that box. The box of the text being typed into is red.
- **Selection tool handles** depend on the layer: point text scales about its anchor, a paragraph box is resized, a shape stretches away from its opposite side as before.
- **Point-text scale.** Only the pointer's travel along one side of the box counts: along its width for the two side handles, along its height for all the others. Travel `d` away from the anchor scales by `1 + d / r`, where `r` is …

title: Shortcut recorder accepts modifier chords; Add Edit cuts only selected clips (#164, items 1 and 5)
author: carlitosteso3
body:
Refs #164. This covers items **5** (shortcuts with Shift/Ctrl/Alt) and **1** (Add Edit on one track cuts all tracks). The other five items are not addressed here.

## Item 5: no shortcut with Shift, Ctrl or Alt could be recorded
Reproduced on Windows 11 with the v0.2.1 release and a **real keyboard**: in Edit ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts, recording Alt+J shows *"AltLeft can't be used as a shortcut"*.

**Cause.** egui 0.36 reports pressing a modifier key as an `Event::Key` of its own (`ShiftLeft`, `ControlLeft`, `AltLeft`, `SuperLeft` and their right-hand variants) before the key it modifies. `shortcuts_dialog::record` took the first key press, which is the modifier alone. `chord_of` then refused it, because modifiers aren't in `KEYS`.

**Fix.** `record` skips modifier keys on their own (`is_modifier_key`) and records the chord when the modified key arrives, with the modifiers it carries. The synthetic `ui.key` events of the existing tests never include a separate modifier event, which is why `keyboard_shortcuts_dialog_assigns_live_and_cancel_restores` didn't catch this.

Running shortcuts was not affected. With the same real keyboard, the default Shift+1 (Project panel) works in v0.2.1.

**Test:** `scripted::recording_a_shortcut_skips_the_modifier_key_presses` queues what a keyboard sends for Alt+Shift+J (`AltLeft`, `ShiftLeft`, `J`) while recording, then checks `shortcuts.get` lists `Alt+Shift+J`. It fails on `main` and passes with the fix.

`sequence.addEdit` always cut the targeted tracks, which by default are all of them, and ignored the selection. Premiere cuts only the **selected clips** at the playhead when there are any, and the targeted tracks otherwise. `sequence.addEdit` now does the same:

title: Web: Link Media Locate… links the chosen file to the selected missing clip (#111)
author: Luna161
body:
## Summary

Link Media ▸ Locate…, `media.attachProxies` and `media.reconnectFullRes` all
need the chosen file's path back synchronously so they can call the engine
with `item` + `path`. The existing `pick_files` hook imports every chosen
file as a new project item, so on the web build (where the browser picker is
asynchronous and the hook returned `Vec::new()`) the command ran without a
path and the file silently landed as a new project item instead of being
relinked. On native the same hook worked because rfd returns paths
synchronously.

Add a separate `pick_file_for_relink` hook that returns the chosen file's
virtual path synchronously. Native hosts open an rfd dialog; the web host
registers the file in `/files/<name>` via a pending slot and runs
`media.relink` itself when the picker resolves. The three call sites prefer
the new hook and fall back to `pick_files` when the host has not installed
it (so the import flow used by every other dialog stays unchanged).

Fixes #111

## Approach

1. `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs` — new `HostHooks::pick_file_for_relink` field
   (`FnMut(&[&str], Option<RelinkHint>) -> Option<String>`) and a
   `RelinkHint` struct carrying the missing item id + the `media.relink`
   match parameters the caller would have used.
2. `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/media_dialogs.rs` — both call sites
   (`media.attachProxies | media.reconnectFullRes` and Link Media
   `Some("locate")`) prefer `pick_file_for_relink` and fall back to
   `pick_files` when it is unset. The hint is forwarded so the web host can
   run `media.relink` itself with the right item id and match parameters.
3. `apps/filmcraft-web/src/import.rs` — new `pick_for_relink` helper that
   stores a `(item, params)` pair in a thread-local `PENDING_RELINK`
   slot and opens the picker. `take_files` consumes the slot, registers
   the chosen file in `/files/<name>`, and runs `media.relink` on the UI
   thread when it fires.

title: Engine: file.import refreshes the offline-missing list (#110)
author: Luna161
body:
Fixes #110

## Problem

After a web project opened offline, importing the missing file through
the UI re-registered the file at the path the project stored, and the
engine happily reported the item online (`media.status`, `media.findMissing`,
File ▸ Link Media… all showed it back), but the Program monitor kept
rendering the "MEDIA NOT FOUND" slate and the Project panel still
badged the item "Media missing". The user had to either reopen the
project or call `media.relink` per item to clear it.

## Root cause

`file.import` (in `crates/engine/src/commands.rs`) creates new items but
never rebuilt `Session::offline.missing`. The UI reads that list to drive
the slate and the project badge
(`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/project_views.rs::media_badge`), so any
re-imported item the project already listed as missing stayed listed as
missing until `on_open` ran again (reopen) or the caller manually
relinked.

## Fix

One line at the end of `file.import`: call `crate::relink::refresh(s)`
to rebuild `offline.missing` from the current `scan` of the project.
This is the same call `on_open` already uses after a project opens, so
the behaviour is symmetric.

The deeper "stale `SharedSource` cache" layer the reporter observed with
`media.autoRelink` is out of scope for this fix; `autoRelink` updates
the project's path reference but `MediaPool::insert_file` is what
evicts the cached `SharedSource`. That work (calling
`MediaPool::remove(item)` for items whose path now resolves, before
re-inserting) is tracked separately — this PR is the minimum
user-visible fix for the slate/badge symptom.

## Test

`crates/engine/src/relink_tests.rs::reimport_clears_offline_list_after_path_resolves`:
saved project with two clips, delete one of the files, reopen (asserts
`offline.missing` contains the item), recreate the file, run
`file.import`, asserts `offline.missing` no longer contains it and
`media.findMissing` returns 0. The test fails without the fix and
passes with it.

title: Windows: NVENC H.264 hardware encoding for Export (opt-in)
author: SaymonMaster14
body:
**Stacked on #141** (Windows Media Foundation decode): review only the last three commits (NVENC encoder, docs, a doc path) until it merges; I rebase then. Independent of #152 and #162. Progress on #30, does not close it.

## Summary

Hardware H.264 **encoding** on Windows through NVIDIA NVENC, as an opt-in Export encoder. **Export ▸ Hardware Encoding** (`ExportSettings.hardwareEncoding`, also `file.exportMedia` `hardwareEncoding: "off|auto"`) is **off by default**: exports are otherwise byte-identical from run to run, and hardware streams differ.

## Design

- NVENC through the driver's `nvEncodeAPI64.dll`, API **12.1** (works with drivers since 531.x), loaded from System32 at run time (machines without NVIDIA start normally); no CUDA, no SDK to install. The session opens on a D3D11 device on the first NVIDIA adapter.
- The FFI structures are written from NVIDIA's MIT-licensed `nvEncodeAPI.h` and **verified against the C compiler's view of that header**: `src/nvenc/abi_tests.rs` is generated from a C program (built with MSVC) that prints `sizeof` / `alignof` / `offsetof` of every field used, all constants, GUIDs and every function-table slot. (It caught two wrong guesses while writing.) The header itself is not in the repo.
- `unsafe` is confined to `nvenc::{ffi,session}` under ADR 0001's rules (updated); `nvenc/mod.rs` and `export.rs` are safe code.
- Pipeline: RGBA → BT.709 limited 4:2:0 with the **software encoder's own conversion** → NV12 input buffers → NVENC (preset P5, high-quality tuning, CABAC, one B-frame when the profile and GPU allow, IDR at the keyframe distance, VUI BT.709 limited + timing, ring of 8 buffer pairs) → Annex B split into 4-byte length-prefixed samples with the SPS/PPS in the `avcC`; dts = decode index − delay.
- **Fallback**: the factory (registered in front of the software encoder) declines, and the software encoder runs as before, for two-pass VBR, HDR, MXF, interlaced output, sizes outside NVENC's limits, no NVIDIA GPU / old driver. D…

title: platform: opt-in hardware H.264 encoding with VideoToolbox
author: dcarnelutti
body:
Progress on #30 ("GPU export, then hardware encode"); does not close it.

## Summary

Hardware H.264 **encoding** on macOS through VideoToolbox, as an opt-in Export encoder. **Export ▸ Video ▸ Hardware Encoding** (`ExportSettings.hardware_encoding`: `off` | `auto`; `"hardwareEncoding": "off|auto"` in `file.exportMedia`) is **off by default**: exports are otherwise byte-identical from run to run and machine to machine, and a hardware encoder's stream is not.

## Overlap with #180

#180 adds the same opt-in for NVENC on Windows. This PR uses #180's names (the `HardwareEncoding { Off, Auto }` enum, the `"off|auto"` JSON, the Export ▸ Video ▸ Hardware Encoding row, the `export.video.hardwareEncoding` automation id), so the two meet only at small conflicts: the enum, the field, the UI row and a few doc strings. Whichever lands second rebases onto the first and keeps one copy; I will do it if it is mine. The hardware counters of #180 (`perf.stats export.hardware`) are not in this PR.

## Design

- `videotoolbox_encode.rs` (FFI, the one place with `unsafe`, as in ADR 0001; every block has a `// SAFETY:` comment, no panic crosses the callback, safe API): a `VTCompressionSession` created with a hardware encoder **required**, so a machine without one is declined up front. NV12 pixel buffers are filled from planar BT.709 limited-range Y'CbCr made by the software encoder's own conversion (`rgba_to_yuv420_8`), so colours match. The output callback copies each compressed frame (length-prefixed NAL units) into a queue the encoder drains.
- `hardware_encode.rs` (safe code): the `VideoEncoder` adapter and the factory `filmcraft_platform::register()` puts in front of the built-in encoders. `export::register_encoder` ignores a factory registered twice, and `encoder_registered` tells tests and diagnostics.

title: render: composite only what overlays cover, and reuse the float images
author: dcarnelutti
body:
Progress on #30; does not close it. Independent of the other open PRs.

## Summary

The CPU compositor is what export runs. It works on premultiplied linear `f32` images, 33 MB each at 1080p, and every layer was one of them: a ProRes 4444 banner that is transparent except for its bottom 100 rows still cost a whole conversion and a whole mix, and the bottom layer paid for a zero-filled canvas and a pass that mixes it over that canvas. With a fast encoder (#183) the compositor is most of an export: a profile of a 9:29 export with a hardware H.264 encoder put 61–64 % of the busy CPU in compositing, 12 % in zeroing and copying memory, 8–11 % each in the float → 8-bit and RGBA → Y'CbCr conversions and 4–7 % in decoding the ProRes overlays.

**Three changes, each giving the bits the general path gives:**

- **Lazy canvas, opaque first layer taken as the canvas.** The canvas is allocated when a layer needs it; an opaque first layer (a Y'CbCr frame without an alpha plane, opacity 100 %, Normal blend, the size of the output) becomes the canvas instead of being mixed over zeros.
- **Layer rectangles.** A clip of plain media whose frame has an alpha plane is converted and mixed only inside the rectangle where its alpha is not zero: `VideoFrame::alpha_region`, `to_linear_f32_region` and `blend::composite_at` (`composite` is `composite_at` at the origin; Dissolve's pattern follows the pixel's place in the output). A clip with effects, opacity masks, frame blending, colour management or a picture not placed one to one on the output takes the general path, as before.
- **Recycled images.** `filmcraft_frame::pool` keeps idle `f32` images (320 MiB at most). `take_f32_overwritten` hands one back with its old contents, which the conversions overwrite whole (so no zero-fill), and the export pipeline gives each frame's image back after the 8-bit conversion.

title: export: show the estimated time left of a render next to its percentage
author: dcarnelutti
body:
Independent of the other open PRs.

## Summary

Export mode, the status bar and the Progress panel showed "Encoding 37%" and nothing about how long the rest would take. They now say **"37% · 2:05 left"**.

- `Progress::eta()` (new `pace` module) is the time left at the job's speed over the last 15 seconds. Each call is also a reading, so the UI polling on every frame it draws the job feeds it, and none of the places that advance `done` had to change. A trailing window follows the real speed changes of an export (an intro, a banner, plain camera footage) where an average since the start lags; a stall makes the estimate grow instead of freezing it; a long idle start (the loudness pass) is not counted as the job's speed; nothing is shown until a second of readings has progress, and nothing once the job is done or finished. No `unwrap`, no unchecked arithmetic: a `Duration` that cannot hold the value is capped at 100 hours.
- `format_eta`: `45 s`, `2:05`, `1:02:05`, rounded up.
- Shown in the status bar ("Exporting… 37% · 2:05 left", and the `status.job.progress` automation label), in the Export queue (on its own line: the column is narrow and a wrapped "· 15 s left" reads badly) and in the Progress panel.
- The engine adds `etaSeconds` (`null` while unknown) to every job of `jobs.list` and to the encoding items of `export.queue.list`, so agents and scripts read it too; `docs/agents.md` says so.

## Measured

A whole 9:29 export (193 s, Apple M1), asking every 3 s: the first estimate comes after 6 s; from 30 s on, the predicted end of the export is on average 1.1 s early and never more than 14.5 s off (7.5 % of the run). The status bar read "9% · 3:00 left" at 21 s and "97% · 5 s left" at 184 s.

## Tests

- `pace`: a steady job gives the time it has left (and the estimate falls as it goes on); nothing is promised before there is progress to measure; the estimate follows a change of speed within the window; a stall makes it grow; an idle start does not hold it back, and…

title: platform: H.265 (HEVC) export with VideoToolbox
author: dcarnelutti
body:
**Stacked on #183** (hardware H.264 encoding with VideoToolbox): review only the last commit until it merges; I rebase then. Progress on #30; does not close it.

## Summary

Adds the **H.265 (HEVC)** export format: **Export ▸ Format ▸ H.265 (HEVC)**, `"format": "hevc"` (or `h265`) in `file.exportMedia`. HEVC Main, 8-bit 4:2:0, in MP4 (`hvc1`) or QuickTime, with AAC audio, encoded by the macOS hardware encoder through the VideoToolbox wrapper of #183.

There is no built-in H.265 encoder (one in pure Rust is a project of its own, and x265 is GPL), so the format exists only where the OS has a hardware encoder. That changes three things from H.264:

- **Choosing the format is the opt-in**; the `hardware_encoding` setting of #183 / #180 is for H.264. `hardware_encode::hevc_available()` (one small hardware session, created once) is registered with the new `filmcraft_export::register_format_probe`, so `available(Format::Hevc)`, the format list of Export mode and `exportFormats` follow the machine; `Format::has_builtin_encoder` says which formats need such a probe.
- **No fallback encoder.** What the hardware path does not take is an error that names the reason, not a different encoder: two-pass VBR is refused up front ("H.265 export has no two-pass mode"), an HDR sequence exports as SDR, and odd sizes, non-square pixels or a machine without the encoder end in "H.265 (HEVC) encoder not available yet".
- Export mode shows H.264's multiplexer, audio, metadata and bitrate controls for it, without profile, level, two-pass or the hardware checkbox, and says "Encoder: Hardware".

## Design

- `videotoolbox_encode`: the session wrapper creates HEVC sessions too (`VtProfile::HevcMain`; the profile also says which codec). Keyframes are HEVC random access points (NAL types 16–21); the parameter sets are VPS / SPS / PPS; the `hvcC` record in the MP4 sample entry is **the one VideoToolbox writes** (sample description extension atoms), so profile, level and flags are the encoder's own. …

title: Engine: project.selectAll and project.deselectAll for the Project panel (#168)
author: Luna161
body:
Fixes #168 (point 2: "Select All doesn't work" with 161 imported clips).

## Root cause
`edit.selectAll` fills only the timeline clip selection (`state.selection`). No command filled the Project panel's selection (`state.project_selection`), so there was no way to select every imported item at once.

## Fix
- **Engine** (`crates/engine/src/project_panel.rs`): new `project.selectAll` (selects every item in the project) and `project.deselectAll` (clears the Project panel selection). Agents can call them through CLI, MCP and the control channel, e.g. `filmcraft.execute("project.selectAll", {})`.
- **UI** (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`, `handle_shortcuts`): when the Project panel has focus, a fired `edit.selectAll` / `edit.deselectAll` is remapped to the `project.*` command. So Cmd+A / Cmd+Shift+A act on project items when the Project panel is focused, and on timeline clips everywhere else.
- `edit.selectAll` itself is unchanged.

## Not in scope
- No new menu entry. Edit ▸ Select All clicked from the menu still runs `edit.selectAll`, because menu clicks don't go through the focus remap.
- The UI keyboard remap has no automated test. The regression test covers the engine commands.

## Tests
- New: `project_panel_tests::select_all_selects_every_project_item`. With the fix reverted it fails (unknown command); with the fix it passes. It also checks that `edit.selectAll` leaves `project_selection` alone.
- `cargo fmt --check` passes. `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-engine -p filmcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-engine`: 366 passed, 2 failed. Both failures also happen on unmodified `main`:
  - `shortcuts_tests::assign_reassigns_conflicts_and_undoes`: the default keymap has 4 existing conflicts.
  - `export_tests::every_builtin_preset_exports_and_ffprobe_confirms`: the local ffprobe doesn't recognise APV.

title: Graphics: New Layer from File anchors the picture at its own centre
author: ajsongpilot
body:
mise ~/.config/mise/config.toml tools: gh@2.101.0
## Problem

`graphics.newFromFile` resolves the clip's Motion anchor using the **sequence frame size** rather than the **imported picture's size**. For any picture smaller than the frame (a logo or watermark, say), the anchor ends up at the frame centre, e.g. `(960, 540)` for a 4×2 image in a 1080p sequence.

After that, `effects.setParam … motion position=[x,y]` moves the wrong point. The picture lands far from the requested position: a 140 px logo set to `[1190, 650]` in a 1280×720 sequence renders at roughly the centre of the frame.

Repro (headless CLI, v0.2.1):

```jsonl
{"id":"graphics.newFromFile","params":{"path":"/abs/logo.png","time":0,"track":2}}
{"id":"effects.setParam","params":{"clip":<clip>,"effect":"motion","param":"position","value":[1190,650]}}
```

`inspect sequence` shows `anchor = (640, 360)` on the logo clip, and `render --seconds 1` draws the logo near the centre.

## Fix

`place_video_clip` now resolves auto points with the source's own size (`Project::source_size`), falling back to the frame size. Text, shapes and the other graphics that share this helper are frame-sized, so their result doesn't change.

## Tests

- `new_layer_from_file_places_the_image_above` now also asserts that the anchor is the picture's centre. It fails before this change (`left: (960.0, 540.0) right: (2.0, 1.0)`) and passes after it.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-engine --all-targets -D warnings` are clean.
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-engine`: 366 passed, 3 ignored. One failure, `shortcuts_tests::assign_reassigns_conflicts_and_undoes`, also fails on unmodified `main` (86f3375) on Linux, so it is unrelated to this change.

title: Ripple delete names the sync-locked track in the way; playhead snaps to cuts (#164, items 2, 3 and snap)
author: carlitosteso3
body:
Follows #173 on #164 (items 1 and 5).

## Item 2: "Ripple delete doesn't move the tracks"
Reproduced in the demo project: ripple deleting a V1 clip is refused because the music on A2 (and the clip on V2) are sync-locked and sit across the gap. Premiere refuses the same edit, so the behaviour stays; the problem was the message, a generic "this edit would break sync on a sync-locked track" in the status bar, with no hint of which track or what to do.

`EditError::SyncLockConflict` now carries the track's label, so it reads:

> edit failed: this edit would break sync: V2 is sync-locked and has a clip in the way (turn off its sync lock, or lock the track, to make this edit)

Checked in the app: after turning off sync lock on V2 and A2, Shift+Delete removes the clip and V1/A1 close up.

## Item 3: "Cut tool doesn't let me cut anything"
Not reproducible on `main`: clicking a clip with the Razor tool (toolbar or **C**) splits it and its linked audio. The reporter is on the 0.2.1 MSI; I'll ask them in #164 for steps if it still happens on the next build.

title: #199: make Ctrl+C / Ctrl+X / Ctrl+V work on Windows and Linux
author: DWAA1660
body:
Fixes #199.

## Cause
On Windows and Linux, egui-winit doesn't send Ctrl+C, Ctrl+X and Ctrl+V as key presses. It sends `Event::Copy`, `Event::Cut` and `Event::Paste` instead and drops the key press. FilmCraft's shortcut handler only matches key presses, so Copy, Cut, Paste, Paste Insert (Ctrl+Shift+V) and Paste Attributes (Ctrl+Alt+V) only worked from the Edit menu. On Windows, Shift+Delete (Ripple Delete) is reported as Cut and was lost the same way. macOS wasn't affected because the native menu bar handles Cmd+C/V itself.

## What changed
- **`handle_shortcuts`** now turns each clipboard event back into the key press it stands for before matching bindings, keeping the modifiers held: Copy → C, Cut → X, Paste → V when Ctrl is held, and Cut → Delete, Paste → Insert when only Shift is held. This only happens when no text field has keyboard focus, so text fields and the on-canvas title editor still handle copy and paste themselves. The original event is kept for anything else that reads it.
- **Empty system clipboard.** egui-winit sends nothing at all for Ctrl+V when the system clipboard has no text, so Paste could still fail right after copying clips. After Edit ▸ Copy or Cut, the copied clip names now go on the system clipboard, the way other editors put their own data there, so the next Ctrl+V reaches the app.

## Tests
- Unit tests in `lib.rs` (`clipboard_key_tests`) cover the event → key mapping: plain Ctrl+C/X/V, Ctrl+Shift+V and Ctrl+Alt+V, the Windows Shift+Delete and Shift+Insert variants, and leaving other events alone.
- `sequence_ui.rs` has two headless UI tests that send the events the way Windows does:
  - `ctrl_c_and_ctrl_v_copy_and_paste_clips` selects a clip, copies it with Ctrl+C and pastes it with Ctrl+V at the end of the sequence.
  - `ctrl_x_cuts_clips` cuts a clip with Ctrl+X and checks that it leaves the timeline.

  Both tests fail without the fix.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass, …

title: Cmd+C / Cmd+V copy and paste clips on the desktop (#188)
author: carlitosteso3
body:
Fixes #188.

## Cause
It wasn't specific to Graphics: on the desktop, **Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V never copied or pasted any clip from the keyboard**. egui-winit turns the clipboard shortcuts into `Event::Copy` / `Event::Cut` / `Event::Paste` and returns without the key press, so `handle_shortcuts` never saw `Cmd+C` / `Cmd+V`. Also:
- `Event::Paste` is only sent while the **system** clipboard holds text, so with it empty Ctrl+V sends nothing at all.
- On Windows, **Shift+Delete** becomes `Event::Cut` too, so Ripple Delete's shortcut never fired. This is probably item 2 of #164.

The control bridge's `ui.key` injects key events directly, which is why the existing UI tests didn't catch it.

## Fix
- `menus::clipboard_keys`, called from `raw_input_hook`, adds the key press back next to each Copy/Cut/Paste event (Cmd+C/X/V; Shift+Delete / Shift+Insert when Shift is held without Cmd). Text fields still get the event, and `handle_shortcuts` already returns early while one has focus. A key the platform already delivered isn't added twice.
- After `edit.copy` / `edit.cut`, the UI leaves `FilmCraft: N clips` on the system clipboard so the next Ctrl+V arrives.

## Tests
- `ui-egui/sequence_ui`: `copy_paste_events_duplicate_a_graphic_clip` pushes the raw `Copy` / `Paste` events the shell produces; it fails without the fix.
- `engine`: `copy_paste_duplicates_a_graphic_clip`.
- fmt, clippy, layers and wasm pass, and so do the touched crates' tests.

Not yet checked with a real keyboard on the desktop build. Shift+Delete in particular is covered by the mapping but not by a test.

title: Q/W ripple trim only the selected clips' tracks (#164)
author: carlitosteso3
body:
Follows the report on #203 that **Q/W affect all tracks instead of the one being selected** (#164).

## Cause
`trim::to_playhead` trimmed every **targeted** track with a clip under the playhead, and all tracks are targeted by default (as in Premiere). So W on a V1 clip also cut the music on A2 in two and removed a stretch of it.

## Fix
Same rule as Add Edit (#173): with clips selected under the playhead, Q / W / Alt+Q / Alt+W trim only those clips' tracks, plus their linked partners. With nothing selected under the playhead, they use the targeted tracks as before.

## Tests
- `ripple_trim_to_playhead_follows_the_selection`: the selected V1 clip ends at the playhead, its linked sound on A1 is trimmed with it, and the music on A2 is untouched. It fails without the fix: A2 got split.
- The existing `ripple_trim_to_playhead_q_w` still passes, and so do fmt and clippy.
- On Windows the same unrelated engine tests fail locally as on `main` (path separators, `%TEMP%` permissions).

## Not changed
A non-selected track with **sync lock on** can still lose material, because the trim reuses `extract`, which also clears sync-locked tracks. In the demo A2 isn't sync-locked; that rule can follow if it still bites.

title: Speed/Duration opens its dialog; dragging an effect parameter is one undo step (#201)
author: carlitosteso3
body:
Fixes #201.

## 1. Speed/Duration applied 50% at once
The clip menu's **Speed/Duration…** had `{"speed": 50.0}` hard-coded, and there was no dialog. Cmd+R and Clip ▸ Speed/Duration… ran the command with no params, so they applied 100% and did nothing.

It now opens **Clip Speed / Duration** in `clip_dialogs`, using the same params JSON as `clip.speedDuration`:
- speed in %, plus a read-out of the resulting duration that follows the speed
- Reverse Speed
- Ripple Edit, Shifting Trailing Clips
- Time Interpolation: Frame Sampling / Frame Blending / Optical Flow

It is seeded from the selected clip. Automation ids are `speedDuration.*`, documented in the module header. The context menu now goes through `menus::invoke` like every other item.

## 2. Undo after dragging Time Remapping's speed crept back in small steps
`effects.setParam` took one undo step per frame of a drag. This affected every Effect Controls value, not just speed.
- `effects.setParam` takes `merge` / `begin`, the same pattern as `clipMixer.set` and the mask commands. It is built on a new `Session::edit_sequence_as(label, merge, f)`, and `edit_sequence` is unchanged.
- Effect Controls runs its actions through one `run()`: while the mouse button is down, `setParam` is sent with `merge`, and with `begin` on the press. A drag is one undo step; typed values and clicks stay separate steps.

## Tests
- `clip_dialogs_ui::speed_duration_from_the_clip_menu_opens_the_dialog`: right-click → Speed/Duration… opens the dialog without touching the clip, Cancel leaves the clip alone, and OK applies 200% with Frame Blending.
- `engine::tests::dragging_an_effect_parameter_is_one_undo_step`: two drags undo one at a time.
- Checked in the app: dragging Time Remapping ▸ Speed from 100% to 60% and undoing once gives 100%.
- fmt and clippy pass. On Windows the same unrelated engine tests fail locally as on `main` (path separators, `%TEMP%` permissions).

title: Sequence ▸ Sequence Settings… opens its dialog (#172, #198)
author: carlitosteso3
body:
Fixes #172, fixes #198.

## Cause
There was no Sequence Settings dialog. The menu item ran `sequence.settings` with no params, so it changed nothing and only left an empty "Sequence Settings" undo step. To the user, the item did nothing.

- Timebase (`FrameRate::COMMON`)

title: #230: jobs time themselves with web_time, so Create Proxies and mask tracking don't panic on the web
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #230.

## Cause

The web build runs every job synchronously (`if wait || cfg!(target_arch = "wasm32") { run() }`), so a job body executes on wasm32 — where `std::time::Instant::now()` panics with `time not implemented on this platform`. Four job bodies still used the std clock for their "Done in N s" report: `proxies::start_job` (Create Proxies), `masks::track` (mask tracking), and the two preview renderers in `previews.rs`; `project_manager` had the same call in its job. The engine already uses `web_time::Instant` everywhere else (`pump_jobs`, `export_tools`, `scene_detect`, `commands`), which is `std::time::Instant` on native targets and `performance.now()` on the web.

## Fix

- `proxies.rs`, `masks.rs`, `previews.rs` (×2), `project_manager.rs`: `web_time::Instant::now()` instead of `std::time::Instant::now()`. No behaviour change on native targets (`web_time` re-exports std there).
- `autosave.rs`: `Instant`, `SystemTime` and `UNIX_EPOCH` imported from `web_time` as well, so no non-test source in the crate names the std clock any more.
- `wasm_clock_tests.rs`: a regression test that scans the crate's non-test sources and fails on any `std::time::Instant`, so the next job added with a copy-pasted `std::time::Instant::now()` fails `cargo test` instead of killing the web app. A crash reachable only on wasm32 cannot be reproduced by a native unit test, so this guard is the test; plus a smoke test that `web_time::Instant` measures elapsed time.

## Tested

- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-engine wasm_clock proxies masks previews project_manager autosave` — the new guard fails on `upstream/main` (6 hits) and passes here
- `cargo check -p filmcraft-engine --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); reviewed and tested locally.

title: i18n: Spanish for the whole interface, catalog files and a remembered language
author: txiki739
body:
Spanish now covers the whole interface, not only the menus: panels, dialogs, the Settings pages, the Effects and Effect Controls registry, the Keyboard Shortcuts dialog, tooltips and status messages (about 3,400 entries). The interface language is also remembered across restarts. ROADMAP listed dialog/panel coverage as open.

## How it works

- **Catalog files instead of Rust tables.** Translations move to one catalog per language, `crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/<code>.tsv` (`context<TAB>English<TAB>translation`, the format PhotoCraft uses), parsed once into HashMaps. `es.tsv`, `ja.tsv` and `pt-br.tsv` keep every existing entry. The pt-br table from #176 is carried over unchanged and still covers the menus.
- **`tl!("…")` and `tlf!("…{name}", name)`.** UI code wraps its literals. `tlf!` translates a template and then fills named placeholders, so a translation can reorder them. Values are inserted literally, so a file name containing `{n}` is not substituted again.
- **Registry names are translated where they are drawn** (`i18n::t`): effects and their parameters, settings labels, commands, panels, workspaces, labels, export and effect presets, scope and timecode modes. Command ids, automation ids, preference values and project content stay English.
- **The current language is thread-local**, set at the start of each frame from `UiState::language`. Tests that switch language don't affect other tests.

title: fix(web): preserve distinct same-name media imports

title: export: keep alpha in PNG/TIFF sequences (Include Alpha Channel) (#160)
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #160

**Root cause.** `Pipeline::frame` (`crates/export/src/pipeline.rs`) converts every rendered frame with `Image::over_black_rgba8()`, so image sequences are flattened over black before `encode_still` writes them — even though the PNG encoder already writes `Rgba8`. Single-frame Export Frame (`crates/engine/src/keyboard.rs`) uses the straight `to_rgba8()`, which is why one frame keeps transparency and a sequence does not.

**Fix.**
- `ExportSettings.alpha: bool` (`#[serde(default)]`, false = Premiere's default, so saved presets and the MCP schema are unchanged). When set and the format is PNG or TIFF, the pipeline emits straight sRGB RGBA instead of flattening, and `encode_still` keeps the channel in TIFF (it was always converting to RGB; PNG was already RGBA). BMP and every video format ignore the flag. `encode_still` gained an `alpha` parameter; the two other callers (`encode_png`, Export Frame) pass `false`, so their output is byte-identical to before.
- `file.exportMedia` flat parameter `alpha: bool` (`crates/engine/src/export_tools.rs`, schema string in `commands.rs`).
- Export mode → Video: an **Include Alpha Channel** checkbox, shown only for PNG and TIFF sequences (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/export_mode.rs`; the panel uses literal labels, no catalog).

**Tests.** `settings_tests::image_sequences_keep_alpha_when_asked`: a 50 % blue colour matte exported as PNG and TIFF, with and without `alpha` — straight alpha ≈ 128 with full-blue colour when on, opaque and darkened when off; the file must carry an alpha channel when on. `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean on `filmcraft-export`, `filmcraft-engine`, `filmcraft-ui-egui`; their tests pass except three that fail identically on `upstream/main` without this change (`shortcuts_tests::assign_reassigns_conflicts_and_undoes`, `crash::tests::hook_records_and_logs_worker_panics`, `i18n::tests::language_commands_switch_and_persist_without_a_document`).

author: ahmedhosnypro
body:
## What

A source-tree run has no installed `.desktop` entry or hicolor icon for the app id the window sets (`ai.storyteller.filmcraft`), so on Linux the shell (Wayland and X11) falls back to the generic Wayland icon in the taskpanel and the window topbar. Packaging installs both; development did not.

At startup on Linux (`apps/filmcraft/src/dev_icon.rs`, called from `main.rs`), **dev runs only** — a debug build, or a release run with `FILMCRAFT_DEV_DESKTOP_ENTRY=1` (the documented `cargo run --release` flow) — install a user-level entry into `$XDG_DATA_HOME`/`~/.local/share` (`applications/`) plus the embedded 256/512 hicolor PNGs when no entry for the app id exists in any XDG data dir, with `Exec` pointing at the running binary. Never when `APPIMAGE` or `FLATPAK_ID` is set (an AppImage mounts at a fresh `/tmp/.mount_*` each launch; packaged installs ship their own entry and must not write into the profile). A packaged entry in a system dir is never overridden; the user-owned dev copy is rewritten when its `Exec` points at another binary (a dev build moves between checkouts).

- `Exec` is escaped for **both desktop-entry layers** exactly like `packaging/linux/install.sh` (shell layer first, then the file-value layer doubles every backslash, always double-quoted; the module doc points at install.sh so the two stay in sync). Paths with `=`, `%` or control characters are rejected instead of written.
- The stale check parses the first `Exec` argument through both layers and **compares it exactly** — `/a/filmcraft-old` is not ours.

body:
## Why

The desktop app never installs a logger, so every `log::warn!` / `log::error!` in the workspace (around 40 of them) is discarded, and a launch from a desktop menu or the Dock has no terminal to show the `eprintln!` start-up messages either. Help ▸ Reveal Log Files already opens `<data dir>/Logs`, but only crash logs ever land there: the warnings that explain what went wrong before a crash, or a problem that never crashes (hardware decoding unavailable, auto-save disabled, a failed recovery), are lost.

We ran into this in the sister project PhotoCraft (storytold/photocraft#1143): a window that stayed empty on Linux took an hour of `WAYLAND_DEBUG` and `gdb` to understand, while the app had already logged the relevant decision to nowhere.

## What

`apps/filmcraft/src/logging.rs`, no new dependency (just `log`):

- **Two sinks:** standard error and `<data dir>/Logs/filmcraft.log`, next to the crash logs, so Help ▸ Reveal Log Files shows it. The directory follows the existing order: `--data-dir`, `FILMCRAFT_DATA_DIR`, then the platform default.
- **Rotation:** each launch moves the previous log to `filmcraft.1.log` (and that one to `.2`), so the log of a run that crashed survives the next start.
- **Bounded:** the file stops at 16 MiB with one note; records logged before the file is attached are buffered (max 512, with a "N earlier lines dropped" note).
- **Levels:** `info` for `filmcraft*` targets, `warn` for everything else. `RUST_LOG` replaces this with env_logger-style directives; a trailing `*` matches a prefix.
- **Never crash:** no `unwrap`/`expect`/indexing; an unusable directory or a failed write keeps standard error only; lock poisoning is handled.
- **Audio:** the realtime callbacks (`audio.rs`, `audio_in.rs`, the play-ahead reader) do not log; the logger holds its lock only for one `write_all` of an already formatted line, and standard error is written outside the lock.

`main.rs`: the logger is installed first (before `crash::install`), the file is…

title: #220: Unlink leaves only the right-clicked clip selected
author: MrCloudy2
body:
Fixes #220.

## What was wrong

Unlink from the timeline clip menu did clear the link on the picture and its sound, but both clips stayed selected. They had been selected together *because* they were linked, and nothing changed the selection afterwards. Clicking a clip that is already selected keeps the selection, so dragging the picture straight after Unlink still dragged the sound with it, and Unlink looked like it had done nothing. Deselecting and clicking the picture again did move it alone.

## What it does now

After **Unlink** from the clip's right-click menu, only the clip that was right-clicked stays selected, so it can be dragged away from its former partner straight away. **Link** leaves the selection as it was. The `clip.link` command itself is unchanged; Clip ▸ Unlink from the menu bar and Cmd+L don't have a right-clicked clip and behave as before.

The change is in `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/timeline.rs` only: the right-clicked clip is remembered while its menu is open, and after `clip.link` reports `linked: false` the selection is set to that clip through `timeline.select`.

## Tests

- `crates/ui-egui/tests/unlink_ui.rs` (headless, real input path): right-click the picture → Unlink → both links are cleared and only the picture is selected → drag the picture: it moves and the sound stays put. Also Unlink from the sound keeps the sound selected, and Link from the menu keeps both selected. Both tests fail without the fix.
- Real app on Linux (`--control 9876`): right-click Ocean_Sunset.mp4 on V1 → Unlink → selection `[picture]`, links `None` → drag: picture start moved, sound start stayed `0`; checked on a screenshot. Also tried by hand.

The change is platform-independent egui logic (no `cfg`), so Windows and macOS take the same path; tested on Linux only.

## Gates (Linux, Rust 1.95.0)

- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask assets`, `cargo xtask wasm`: pass.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --release -- -D warnings`: fails…

title: engine: project.delete takes explicit bin ids without a Project-panel selection (#244)
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #244

## Root cause

`Session::enabled_for` already lets a caller that names its targets skip the selection: the enablement check is re-run with the named ids standing in for `project_selection`. But `commands::named_items` only accepted ids that are project *items* (`project.item(id).is_some()`), while `project.delete`'s `items` also take bin ids — the Project panel's selection holds both in one id space (`project.select` accepts them, and the issue's repro deletes four bins). With nothing selected, a call naming only bins fell back to the selection's verdict: `select an item in the Project panel`.

## Fix

`named_items` counts a named bin as a target too, except the project's own top bin, which no command acts on. Nothing else changes: an id of nothing still does not stand in for a selection, menu enablement still follows the selection, and the selections are left untouched.

## Tests

`explicit_targets_tests::project_delete_takes_explicit_bins_and_items_without_a_selection`: with an empty Project-panel selection, `project.delete` deletes an empty bin, a bin holding a clip, and a plain item, each by id alone; the root bin id and an unknown id are still refused with the selection's message; the selection stays empty, `is_enabled` stays false, and two undos restore the project. Fails before the fix at the first delete (`Disabled`).

`cargo test -p filmcraft-engine` passes apart from `shortcuts_tests::assign_reassigns_conflicts_and_undoes`, which also fails on untouched `main` (built-in preset conflicts on Cmd+9 / Cmd+Shift+M / Cmd+T) and is unrelated. `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are green.

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); reviewed and tested locally.

title: Playback: fall back to a working output device when the ALSA default cannot be opened
author: ahmedhosnypro
body:
Refs #23, #106. Reproduced and diagnosed on Linux (PipeWire, one sound card at index 1, no card 0).

## Cause

On this machine the ALSA `default` PCM was broken: the distro's `99-pipewire-default.conf` symlink (PipeWire's `pcm.!default { type pipewire }` override) was missing from `/etc/alsa/conf.d`, so plain `default` fell through to the legacy chain (`defaults.pcm.card 0`) and card 0 does not exist. Stock `aplay -D default` reproduced the exact `cannot find card '0'` → `Unknown PCM default` chain from #23/#106, while `aplay -D pipewire` played; other apps work because they speak PipeWire/Pulse native APIs — cpal is what opens the ALSA `default` PCM.

With the default unopenable, `CpalOut::new()` got no config (48 kHz/2 defaults) and `start()` failed at the device/config step: playback ran on the wall clock without sound, and the only hint was cpal's stderr ALSA trace.

## Change

- `output_device` picks, in order: the device named in the settings, the host default (now required to actually open), then the first enumerated output device that can — with a `log::warn!` naming the fallback. `start`, `devices` and `configure` all go through it.
- A new defaulted `AudioOut::note()` method surfaces a hardware note in the status bar, read on the first frame (`apply_prefs`) and when playback starts (`start_audio`): "Audio hardware: the default output device cannot be opened; using '…'". When no device can open at all, `CpalOut::new()` reports "No audio output device found: playing without sound (check Settings ▸ Audio Hardware)".
- Caveat: cpal 0.16 enumerates per-card `plughw:N` devices (direct kernel path, bypassing PipeWire) and its public API cannot open an arbitrary PCM name like `pipewire`; so the fallback fixes "no sound at all", but on a broken-`default` machine the robust sound path remains restoring the ALSA config (the missing symlink here).

title: control: Ctrl+ chords through ui.key fire shortcuts off macOS (#245)
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #245

## Root cause

Key bindings are stored as `Cmd+…` and `menus::parse_shortcut` turns them into `egui::Modifiers { command: true }`; egui's `cmd_ctrl_matches` then requires `command` on the pressed modifiers. A physical Ctrl press off macOS carries it (egui-winit sets `command = ctrl` there), but `ui.key` built its synthetic event from the same `parse_shortcut`, which mapped `"Ctrl"` to `ctrl` alone — so an injected `Ctrl+Z` matched no binding while `Cmd+Z` did. `ui.click` / `ui.drag` modifiers (`{"ctrl": true}`) had the same gap.

## Fix

- `parse_shortcut` (`crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs`): off macOS `Ctrl` and `Cmd` are one key (what the engine's `Chord::effective` already says), so both parse to `command`. Patterns stay permissive (they never require `ctrl`), so events carrying only `command` — e.g. the `Modifiers::COMMAND` the sequence UI tests send with clipboard events — keep matching. On a Mac the two stay distinct keys, as before.
- `control.rs`: a new `as_pressed` mirrors egui-winit for synthesised input — off macOS a press of either Ctrl or Cmd carries both `ctrl` and `command`. `ui.key` and the shared `modifiers()` helper (click/drag/scroll) go through it.
- `docs/control-protocol.md`: one note that `Ctrl+K` is the same key as `Cmd+K` off macOS.

## Tests

- `menus::parse_shortcut_tests::ctrl_and_cmd_are_one_key_off_macos` (unit, both platforms): off macOS `Ctrl+Z` and `Cmd+Z` parse identically and are matched by the physical modifiers and by a bare `COMMAND`; on macOS they remain two keys that do not match each other; a bare key never stands in for the chord.
- `keyboard_ui::ctrl_chords_fire_shortcuts_off_macos` (kittest harness, `cfg(not(macos))`): `Ctrl+Right` nudges the selected clip one frame and `Ctrl+Z` undoes it, the same via `{"key":"Right","ctrl":true}`, and a bare `Z` does nothing. Fails before the fix at the first nudge.

title: shortcuts: Delete clears the selected timeline clips (#243)
author: wstock
body:
Fixes the Delete-key part of #243 (typing Vietnamese diacritics, the other half of that issue, is not addressed here).

## Root cause
On Windows and Linux keyboards the key labelled **Delete** is the forward-delete key (`Delete` in FilmCraft's notation; the Mac "delete" key is `Backspace`). In FilmCraft Default it was bound only to `project.delete` (Project ▸ Clear, application-wide — its registry default), while `edit.clear` had `Backspace`. One FilmCraft panel shortcut in `shortcut_presets::FILMCRAFT_PANEL`: `("edit.clear", "Delete", "Timeline")`, as Premiere has it. title: macOS DMG: branded window background and icon layout
author: XusBadia
body:
## What

The macOS DMG opened as a plain white Finder window. It now opens like this:

![FilmCraft DMG window in Finder](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/XusBadia/filmcraft/dmg-preview/finder.png)

The icon's figure as a cover on the FilmCraft colour field, FilmCraft.app and the `Applications` link side by side on Paper, and a small FilmCraft-specific touch: the arrow and the mono line under the title come from the app's craft. Ink, Paper and the app colour only; Inter and JetBrains Mono.

## How

Same approach as PhotoCraft's and VectorCraft's, which have landed (storytold/photocraft#1201, storytold/vectorcraft#493):

- `packaging/macos/dmg/background.svg`: the source. Its text is outlined, so rendering it needs no fonts, and the figure is an `<image>` of the existing icon in `assets/app-icon/`.
- `background.tiff`: 1x 660×400 + 2x 1320×800 in one HiDPI TIFF (16-colour palette, Deflate, sRGB; 106 KB). No paper grain: noise doesn't compress, and this keeps the binary small.
- `dmg-layout.DS_Store`: Finder's view settings (window 660×400 content, icon size 128, FilmCraft.app at (326, 205), Applications at (574, 205), the background). It's named so it isn't mistaken for, or ignored like, a Finder-generated `.DS_Store`.
- `generate.py`: writes both from the SVG on any OS (`pip install 'pillow>=12' ds_store==1.3.3 mac_alias==2.2.3`, resvg on PATH). The output is byte-for-byte reproducible and carries nothing from the machine that ran it: no paths, users, disk names or volume UUIDs.
- `package.sh` copies the TIFF and the layout into the staging folder. The image is still built with `hdiutil makehybrid`, and nothing extra runs in the signing job.

## One behaviour change: the volume name drops the version

`.DS_Store` points at the background through an alias that includes the volume name. With `FilmCraft <version>` Finder kept the window and icon positions but lost the background (tested). So the mounted volume is now called `FilmCraft`; the DMG file name still carries …

title: #197, #193: web recovery retries failed snapshot writes and keeps skipped snapshots dirty
author: carlitosteso3
body:
Fixes #197, fixes #193.

## Cause
The web app's OPFS recovery snapshot (`apps/filmcraft-web`) had two problems:
- **#197:** `opfs::write` never reported failures, and `Autosave` recorded the revision as snapshotted before the write ran. A failed write was only retried after the next edit.
- **#193:** the first tick of a clean session wrote `{"dirty": false}` to the meta. Starting with `?norecover` or `?fresh` therefore marked a snapshot that was never reopened as clean, and it was lost.

## Fix
- The decision of when to snapshot or mark clean moves to a pure module, `recovery_policy`, so it is tested natively even though the crate is wasm32-only.
- Failed writes (snapshot or clean meta) are retried after the 5 s interval, without another edit.
- The meta is marked clean only to retire a snapshot **this session** wrote. A snapshot left by an earlier session and skipped with `?norecover` / `?fresh` stays dirty.
- `opfs::write_then` reports whether a queued write landed; writes coalesced into a newer one report the newer one's result. Snapshot and meta are reported as a pair: either failing retries both.

## Tests
`tests/recovery_policy.rs` (6 tests):
- a failed snapshot write is retried after the interval with no edit, and not before
- a stale failure for an older revision is ignored
- a clean start never marks an unconsumed snapshot clean (#193)
- saving retires this session's snapshot
- a failed clean write is retried
- an edit during the clean write keeps the meta dirty

Also checked: fmt and `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -- -D warnings` pass.

title: fix: Ctrl+ chords now trigger shortcuts on Windows/Linux
author: mjohnson7cd
body:
## Fixes #245

## Problem

On Windows/Linux, \`ui.key\` with a \`Ctrl+…\` chord (e.g. \`{"key":"Ctrl+Z"}\`) through the control channel or MCP \`ui_key\` tool does nothing. \`Cmd+Z\` works. A physical Ctrl+Z is unaffected (egui-winit sets \`command\` for Ctrl off macOS), so this only affects injected/synthetic keys.

## Root Cause

\`parse_shortcut\` (\`crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs:515\`) maps \`"Ctrl"\` to \`egui::Modifiers { ctrl: true, command: false }\`. Bindings are stored as \`Cmd+…\` (which becomes \`command: true\`). A real Ctrl press on Windows/Linux sets both \`ctrl\` and \`command\`, but the synthetic event only had \`ctrl\`, so no binding matched.

The \`modifiers()\` helper in \`control.rs:68\` had the same gap: it set \`ctrl\` without \`command\` off macOS.

## Fix

The engine's \`Chord::parse\` (\`crates/engine/src/shortcuts.rs:277\`) already handles this correctly per platform; this brings the UI-layer parsers in line.

## Testing

- \`cargo build --release -p filmcraft\` compiles clean on Linux (CachyOS, kernel 7.2.9, Rust 1.99.0)

## Files changed

- \`crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs\` — \`parse_shortcut\` now sets \`command = true\` on non-macOS for \`Ctrl\` modifier
- \`crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs\` — \`modifiers()\` now sets \`command = true\` when \`ctrl\` is true on non-macOS

title: fix: project.delete accepts explicit items without UI selection
author: mjohnson7cd
body:
## Fixes #244

## Problem

\`project.delete\` ignores its explicit \`items\` parameter when nothing is selected in the Project panel. It fails with \`command 'project.delete' is not available right now: select an item in the Project panel\`, even though the body handles \`items\` correctly. Agents driving the app through the control channel or MCP cannot delete by id without first faking a UI selection.

## Root Cause

\`crates/engine/src/commands.rs:2361\` registers \`project.delete\` with the \`has_project_selection\` enabled-check, which only looks at \`s.state.project_selection\`. The enabled-check runs before the body, so the explicit \`items\` param never gets used, even though the body already falls back to the selection only when \`items\` is absent.

## Fix

- Changed the enabled-check from \`has_project_selection\` to \`always\`
- Added a body-level check: if both \`items\` param and \`project_selection\` are empty, return \`EngineError::Other\` with a helpful message

This preserves the UI behavior (Delete key still works when items are selected) while allowing agents to delete by explicit id without a UI selection.

## Testing

- \`cargo build --release -p filmcraft\` compiles clean on Linux (CachyOS, kernel 7.2.9, Rust 1.99.0)
- Existing UI delete behavior unchanged (Delete key with selection still works)

## Files changed

- \`crates/engine/src/commands.rs\` — \`project.delete\` enabled-check changed to \`always\`, added empty-items guard in body
