title: Issue #545: captions.list with a track that names no caption track is an error
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Fixes #545.

`captions.list` resolved `track` with `track_param`, but an unresolved selector became `None`, which the filter treated the same as an omitted `track`. A missing numeric id (e.g. `1009`) or a label past the last track (`C3` with two tracks) therefore returned every caption track with success.

### What changes
- When `track` is given and names no caption track, `captions.list` now fails with `captions.list: no such caption track`. This matches `captions.export`, `captions.setTrack`, `captions.setStyle`, `captions.deleteTrack` and `captions.add`, which already reject an unknown track.
- Omitting `track` still lists every track. Valid ids and `C1` / `C2`… labels still return just their track.
- `docs/captions.md`: the `captions.list` row notes that an unknown `track` is an error.

### Tests
- `caption_list_track_filter_never_falls_back_to_every_track` (`crates/engine/src/captions_tests.rs`) creates two caption tracks and checks that each id and each label returns only its own track, and that a missing id, `C3`, `C0` and `"nope"` are errors. It fails on `main` (the missing id returns both tracks) and passes with this change.

### Gates (macOS arm64)
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask assets` and `cargo xtask wasm` all pass.
- `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`: 2277 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `filmcraft-matroska` `oracle::mjpeg_ac3` (ffprobe packet duration 32 vs 8), an ffmpeg-oracle test in a crate this PR doesn't touch. It fails the same way on an untouched `main` (see #446).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(export): Selection as Project exports a selected bin's contents (#536)
author: maxm11
body:
## Summary

Selecting a nonempty bin in the Project panel and running File ▸ Export ▸ Selection as FilmCraft Project reported success (`ok:true`, `items:[bin]`) while writing a project with an empty item map and root. The same happened passing the bin id directly in `items`, and a mixed request `[bin, item]` reported the bin even though it was absent from the output.

Root cause: `closure()` kept the bin id (bins and items share one id space, but a bin is not an item), and `project_subset()` then pruned every real item because none were kept.

## Fix

`closure()` now expands a named **non-root** bin to every item it holds (recursing into sub-bins), then follows those items' dependencies — exactly the precedent set by `project.delete` (`crates/engine/src/commands.rs:2534`). Only ids naming a real item enter the keep set, so the reported `items` and the saved project always agree. The project's top bin is still excluded (#244), since no command acts on it.

`export_selection` now returns an actionable error when the target has no exportable items (e.g. an empty bin) instead of writing an empty project.

## Tests

`export_selection_project_of_a_bin_exports_its_contents` (regression): selecting the demo Footage bin exports exactly its six items; a mixed bin+item request reports no bin; an empty bin errors without writing a file.

Verified end-to-end with the CLI reproduction from the issue — selected-bin, explicit-bin and mixed cases now save/reopen `[5,6,7,8,9,10]` with a populated root, while the direct-contents and sequence controls are unchanged and the source project is untouched.

Gates: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p filmcraft-engine --lib` (429 passed) all green.

Closes #536

title: Roll: reversed clips take the cut from the opposite source end (#526)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #526.

`roll()` changed the source ranges of reversed clips as if they played forward. It now follows the same reverse rules as `trim()`:

- Reversed left clip: moving the cut later extends its tail on the timeline, which in reverse is the start of its source range, so `source_in` goes down by the delta (like `trim` on the Out edge).
- Reversed right clip: the cut eats its head on the timeline, which in reverse is the end of its source range, so `source_in` stays the same (like `trim` on the In edge).
- The media-limit clamps also swap for reversed clips. A reversed left clip is limited by the media before its source In, and a reversed right clip is limited by the media after its source Out. Without this swap a reversed left clip could roll past the start of its media.

Forward clips behave as before.

Test: `roll_reversed_clips_keeps_media_mapping` is the issue's case: two reversed 30-frame clips with source In 20 and 50, rolled by +10. The left clip becomes [0,40) with source [10,50), and the right clip becomes [40,60) with source [50,70). On main the test gets [20,60) and [60,80), so it fails there.

title: fix(edit): reversed trims use the media handle their playback direction consumes (#527)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #527.

`clamp_trim()` limited trims on reversed clips as if they played forward. But `trim()` already moves the source range the reverse way: a reversed In edge grows `source_out`, and a reversed Out edge lowers `source_in`. So the limits and the edit did not match. The limits now match the edit:

- Reversed In edge: an extension is limited by the media after `source_out`. With no media length (stills and similar), there is no limit, the same as a forward Out edge.
- Reversed Out edge: an extension is limited by the media before `source_in`, which is the head handle.

Forward clips and frame holds behave as before. `ripple_trim_group()` and the engine's `timeline.trim` both go through `clamp_trim()`, so they get the fix too.

Test: `reversed_trim_uses_the_handle_its_playback_direction_consumes` reverses a clip with source [5,15) on 1000-frame media. An Out extension of +20 is clamped to +5 and gives source [0,15). An In extension of -10 is then accepted in full and gives [0,25). On main the first step is not clamped to +5: it allows +20, which would put `source_in` before the media start. The second step is clamped to 0. So the test fails on main.

title: Trim: extend each selected edit point to the playhead by its own distance (#528)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #528.

`trim.extendToPlayhead` worked out one delta from the first selected edit point (`playhead - first edit time`) and used it for every selected point. When the selected points were at different times, only the first one ended at the playhead. In the issue's repro, the Out point at frame 80 moved 35 frames later to frame 115, when it should have moved back to frame 65.

Now each point gets its own delta, `playhead - edit_time(point)`, read from the sequence when the trim loop reaches that point. That way, if an earlier trim already moved a point (through a linked partner, for example), it isn't moved a second time. `trim_all_raw` takes a per-point delta closure for this. The other callers (`trim_all` for nudges, and dynamic J/K/L trimming) pass a constant delta, so they behave exactly as before. The Trim Monitor shift counter still adds the primary point's applied movement, as it did before.

Test: `extend_to_playhead_moves_each_unequal_out_point_to_the_playhead` in `trim_tests.rs`. It selects the Out points of a V1 clip and the V2 overlay in the demo project. The two clips overlap but end at different times. It puts the playhead inside the overlap, runs `trim.extendToPlayhead` and checks that both clips now end at the playhead. Without the fix, the second clip ends at a different time.

title: Linked slip: clamp to one shared delta so picture and sound stay aligned (#529)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #529.

`timeline.slip` slipped each linked partner on its own, and `edit::slip` clamps each clip to its own media range. When the partners have different durations, one partner can reach the media end before the other does. That partner stopped and the other one kept going, so picture and sound got out of sync. In the issue's fixture, a +30 frame slip moved sound by 20 frames and picture by 0.

Now the handler trial-slips each linked clip on a clone of the sequence, keeps the smallest allowed delta, and then slips all partners by that delta. `timeline.slide` and linked `timeline.trim` already work this way.

Test: `linked_slip_keeps_picture_and_sound_aligned_at_unequal_media_limits` builds the fixture from the issue (4 s offline clip, picture trimmed to 80 frames, sound left at 60 frames). It checks that the +30 slip leaves both source Ins at frame 20, and that a -10 slip then moves both to frame 10. Without the fix, the first assertion fails because sound moves to frame 40.

Not in this PR: the keyboard slip helper (`slip_selection` in `keyboard.rs`), which the issue also mentions, still clamps each clip on its own. It scales the delta by each clip's speed, so a shared delta there needs its own change. I can open a follow-up if you want one.

title: Frame-held Regular In trim stops at the previous clip instead of overlapping it (#530)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #530.

In `clamp_trim`, a frame-held clip replaced the whole In-edge lower bound with `Tick::MIN`. That removed the source-head limit, which is correct for a hold, but it also removed the Regular-mode limit at the previous clip. A held extension past the previous clip was not clamped, so the edit failed with an overlap error. A non-held clip gets the same request clamped to the free space.

Now a held clip in Regular mode is clamped to the gap before the previous clip, and still ignores the source head. Ripple mode with a hold keeps no lower limit, as before. Non-held clips are unchanged.

Test: `held_regular_in_trim_stops_at_previous_clip` gives a held clip a 5-frame gap and asks for a 20-frame extension. The trim now returns -5 frames. A second request with no space left returns zero. On main the first trim fails with the overlap error.

title: Export settings: accept camelCase for nested snake_case fields (#531)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #531.

`settings_from_params` serializes the current `ExportSettings` to JSON, deep-merges the caller's `settings` object into it, and deserializes the result. A few nested structs (`AudioSettings`, `LoudnessNormalization`, `ExportEffects` and its overlays) serialize their fields in snake_case. So a documented camelCase key like `audio.sampleRate` or `effects.loudness.targetLufs` was added as a second key next to the snake_case default. Serde then ignored the camelCase key, and the export silently used the default (48000 Hz, -23 LUFS).

The fix is in `merge`. When a patch key is not in the base object but its snake_case spelling is, the value is merged into the snake_case key. Keys that already match are unchanged, so snake_case input, top-level camelCase input and the serialized format all behave as before.

Test: `nested_camel_case_settings_are_honoured` resolves a WAV export with `audio.sampleRate: 96000` and `effects.loudness.targetLufs: -16`. It checks that `output.sampleRate` is 96000, that the resolved settings carry both values, and that the result is the same as with the snake_case spelling. Without the fix, `settings.audio.sample_rate` stays `null` and the test fails.

title: Queue move: saturate a huge relative offset instead of overflowing (#532)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #532.

`export.queue.move` computed the target index as `i as i64 + by` before clamping, so a `by` near `i64::MAX` overflowed and the command failed with a generic internal error in debug builds. The addition now uses `saturating_add`, so an extreme offset lands on the existing `clamp(0, n - 1)` and moves the item to the end (or the start for a large negative offset), matching what an out-of-range absolute `to` already does. Small relative moves and absolute moves are unchanged.

Added a unit test that moves the middle of three queued items by `i64::MAX` and then by `i64::MIN` and checks the resulting order.

title: Forced relink and Replace Footage keep the new file's properties (#534)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #534.

When a forced `media.relink` (and `media.replaceFootage`, which forces) gets past a failed cheap check such as the fingerprint, `check_candidate` returns before opening the file. So the candidate has no `info`. `relink()` then opened the file only to check that it could be read, threw the source away, and `apply` kept the old file's duration, size and frame rate on the item. The stale info was also saved with the project.

Now, when the check left no source, `relink()` keeps the file it opens and puts the file's `info` on the candidate. `apply` then stores the new file's properties, as it already does for a relink that passes the checks. A non-forced relink still refuses a mismatch.

Test: `forced_relink_takes_the_new_files_properties` force-relinks to a replacement at twice the size and checks that the item reports the new width. It fails without the fix.

title: Project Manager: keep every parent of a nested subclip when collecting (#535)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #535.

`used_ranges` only marked the immediate parent of a subclip as used. A project loaded from disk can hold a subclip whose parent is another subclip, so with `excludeUnused: true` the root media item was dropped from the copy and no media file was collected. The copied project then had a subclip pointing at a missing item.

`used_ranges` now walks the whole parent chain of a subclip, up to the media item, and marks each link as used. The walk stops after 16 steps, the same limit as `Project::resolve_media`, so a cyclic chain cannot loop forever. Nothing else changes: the range bookkeeping still uses the immediate parent, as before.

Test: `nested_subclip_keeps_its_whole_parent_chain_used` builds a media -> inner subclip -> outer subclip chain, puts the outer subclip on the timeline, and checks that all three items are in the used set. Without the fix, the media item is missing.

title: CLI: a closed stderr no longer panics with exit 101 (#537)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #537.

`eprintln!` panics when writing to stderr fails, so with a stderr pipe whose reader has exited, `filmcraft-cli` ended with status 101 instead of the documented 2 (usage error), 1 (command failure) or 0 (finished export).

All stderr diagnostics in `apps/filmcraft-cli/src/main.rs` now go through a small `diag` helper that writes the line and ignores a write error: `usage`, `fail`, the export and render completion messages, and the "can't write to stdout" message. The exit statuses are now the same with a closed stderr as with a writable one. Stdout handling (#285 / #297) does not change.

Test: `a_failing_diagnostic_stream_does_not_panic` sends a diagnostic to a writer that always returns `BrokenPipe` and checks that a normal writer still gets the line.

title: CLI export: forward a lone --start or --end so the engine reports the missing bound (#538)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #538.

`filmcraft-cli export` only forwarded `--start` / `--end` when both flags were present, so a lone bound was silently dropped and the whole sequence was exported with exit 0. The CLI now sets `range: custom` and forwards whichever bound was given, so the engine's custom-range check returns its usual `custom range: need start` / `need end` error and nothing is written. A complete pair and the no-bound default behave as before. This also covers `--range custom --start s`, which used to report the wrong missing bound because the supplied one was not forwarded.

The forwarding moved into a small `set_custom_bounds` helper, with a unit test covering a lone start, a lone end and no bounds.

title: CLI render: report the real reason for an invalid scale instead of no sequence (#539)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #539.

`filmcraft-cli render` called `Session::render_program`, which returns `Option` and drops the reason, so every failure was printed as `no sequence`, even an open sequence rendered with `--scale 0`, `-1` or `NaN`.

The command now calls `Session::try_render_program_at(scale, playhead)` (the same render, with the same options) through a small helper and prints its error. As a result:

- an invalid scale reports `render scale 0 must be finite and positive`
- a session with no sequence still reports `no active sequence`
- a valid scale such as `0.5` renders the same way as before

The new test `render_reports_the_real_reason` covers all three cases: the no-sequence message, the finite-and-positive message for 0, -1 and NaN on a 16x16 sequence, and the 8x8 result at scale 0.5.

title: Parametric Equalizer: use the full EQ so master gain, bands 1/2/4/5 and pass filters reach the audio (#540)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #540.

`audio_fx::mapping` had an explicit `"parametric_eq"` arm that sent Parametric Equalizer to the three-band `simple_eq` DSP. That arm forwarded only the low shelf, Band 3 and the high shelf. It came before the `DIRECT` fallback, so the existing `("parametric_eq", "parametric_eq_full", 0.1)` entry was never used. Master Gain, Bands 1, 2, 4 and 5, High Pass and Low Pass were saved but did nothing to the audio.

The fix removes that arm. Parametric Equalizer now goes through the `DIRECT` entry to `parametric_eq_full`, which takes every project parameter by the same id. The existing `direct_mappings_match_dsp_parameters` test already checks that the ids, ranges and defaults match. The low shelf, Band 3 and high shelf use the same ids as before, so existing projects and the Essential Sound presets keep their settings. The `simple_eq` project effect still uses its own mapping.

Other changes: the On switches and Q values of the shelves now also take effect. Pre-roll for a new chain is now the direct-mapping value (0.12 s) instead of 0.05 s.

Test: `parametric_eq_applies_every_control` configures the effect through `configured()` and reads `response_db(1000.0)`. It checks Master Gain at -30 dB, Bands 1/2/4/5 at 1 kHz / -24 dB, High Pass at 10 kHz and Low Pass at 100 Hz. On main the effect configures `simple_eq`, which ignores these controls, so the test fails there.

title: Audio Gain: measure the peak of the audio stream each clip plays (#541)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #541.

`clip_peaks` read every clip's source with `src.audio(...)`, and that always reads container stream 0. A clip placed from the second audio stream of a multi-stream file therefore got the first stream's peak. `clip.audioPeak` reported the wrong value, and `normalizeAll` / `normalizeMax` computed the wrong gain from it.

Now `clip_peaks` reads `src.audio_stream(it.audio_stream, ...)`, the same call the renderer uses for the clip's sound (`crates/render/src/audio.rs`). Clips on stream 0 work as before.

`clip_peaks` is now `pub(crate)` so the test can call it.

Test: `clip_peaks_measure_the_stream_the_clip_plays` places a two-stream item (a bars-and-tone generator whose info lists a second stream that the source does not have). The stream-0 clip measures about -20 dBFS and the stream-1 clip measures silence. Without the fix, both clips report -20 dBFS and the test fails.

title: masks.addVertex: clamp oversized index on animated paths, reject empty paths instead of panicking (#543)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #543.

On a mask path with two or more keyframes, `masks.addVertex` first inserted a midpoint vertex into every keyframe and then computed the target index from the already grown path. With `after` past the last vertex, that index was one past the end, so the assignment panicked (`the len is 5 but the index is 5`). On an animated path whose keyframes have no vertices, `path.vertices.len() - 1` underflowed.

Now the index is clamped against the vertex count before any insertion, so an oversized `after` appends the vertex at the end, the same as static and one-keyframe paths already do. An animated path with no vertices returns a parameter error ("the animated mask path has no vertices to insert after"), and the edit leaves the mask unchanged. Static and one-keyframe paths, including empty ones, behave as before.

Test: `add_vertex_on_animated_path_clamps_oversized_index_and_rejects_empty_path` builds a two-keyframe polygon mask and adds a vertex with `after: 100`; it now has 5 vertices. It then builds a two-keyframe empty open path and checks that `addVertex` returns the parameter error (not the generic internal-error response) and the path stays empty, and that a static empty path still takes its first vertex. Without the fix, the first two cases panic.

title: MCC export: end each ancillary packet with its checksum byte so FFmpeg reads the captions (#544)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #544.

`build_cdp` wrote the ancillary prefix (`61 01 <count>`) and the CDP, but no SMPTE ST 291 checksum byte after the user data words. FFmpeg's MCC demuxer expects that byte, so it read zero caption packets from our exports.

`build_cdp` now appends the checksum: the low 8 bits of the sum of DID, SDID, data count and the CDP bytes. Our own reader already bounds the CDP by its declared length, so import of these files is unchanged.

Test: `cdp_structure_and_checksum` now checks the 77-byte packet length and the trailing checksum byte; it fails on main (76 bytes, no checksum).

title: Text panel: word navigation ignores a selection the transcript no longer has (#546)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #546.

`text_panel` read `app.ui.transcript_sel` as-is. When the sequence transcript shrinks while the Text panel is open (e.g. `transcript.extract` over the control channel), the stored selection still holds the old word indices, so `prevWord` computed `to = 4` on a 3-word transcript and `words[to]` panicked (caught by the UI guard).

The keyboard path now drops a selection that is out of range and falls back to the word at the playhead, the same as when no word is selected. The drawing code in `panels/text.rs` already treats an out-of-range selection as no selection (`transcript_sel.filter(...)`), so navigation now matches what the panel shows.

Test: `transcript_selection_tests::prev_word_after_the_transcript_shrank_under_the_selection_does_not_panic` in `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/keyboard.rs`. It sets a 4-word transcript on the demo project, selects word 3, extracts words 0 to 1 through the engine, then runs `textPanel.prevWord`. Before this change it panics with an index out of bounds. With the change it returns a selection inside the 2-word transcript.

title: Slide: keep reversed neighbours' source ranges correct (#548)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #548.

`slide` trimmed its neighbours as if they always played forward. A reversed clip shows its source Out first, so a change to its Out edge moves `source_in`, and a change to its In edge leaves `source_in` where it is. This is how `trim` already handles the two edges.

Now `slide` does the same:
- A reversed left neighbour that grows or shrinks at its Out edge has its `source_in` moved by the same media amount. Its content at the timeline positions that stay does not change.
- A reversed right neighbour keeps its `source_in` when its In edge moves.
- The media-handle clamps also take the reverse direction into account. A reversed left neighbour can grow only by the media before its `source_in`. A reversed right neighbour can grow only by the media after its source Out. This means a slide cannot push `source_in` below the start of the media.

Forward neighbours work as before.

With the issue's input (three reversed 30-frame clips at source In 20, 50 and 70, middle clip slid +10 frames), the result is now left [0,40) src [10,50), middle [40,70) src [50,80), right [70,90) src [70,90).

Test: `slide_keeps_reversed_neighbours_content` reproduces that case. It fails without the fix (left neighbour source In 20, right neighbour 80).

title: timeline, monitors: drag the current-time timecode to scrub, click to type a time
author: ReReddo
body:
Closes #554.

The big blue timecode in the Timeline and the current-time timecodes of the Program and Source monitors were display-only. All three now work the same way:

- **Drag** left or right to scrub that panel's playhead: 1 frame per point, Shift for 10. It stops at the start (for the Source monitor, the clip's start). The pointer is hidden while dragging and put back where the drag began.
- **Click** to type a time. The whole value is selected, so typing replaces it. Enter or clicking elsewhere goes to the typed time, Escape cancels. Left/Right on the selected value start from its last digit.
- Typed input goes through the existing `parse_timecode`, so `01:02:03:04`, `1000` (10 s) and relative `+15` / `-1.00` all work. An invalid time is reported in the status bar and the playhead stays where it was.

**Changes**

- `crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs`: new `timecode_field`, replacing the unused `timecode_label` stub.
- `panels/timeline.rs`, `panels/monitor.rs`: the three readouts use it. The Timeline and Program monitor dispatch `playhead.set`, the Source monitor `source.setPlayhead`. Automation ids are unchanged (`timeline.timecode`, `program.timecode`, `source.timecode`).
- No engine changes.

Two egui details worth knowing for review:

- Focus is requested by the text field itself, on its first frame. Requesting it before the field exists left the accessibility tree focused on a missing node, which panicked in `accesskit_consumer`.
- Focus is requested only until the field has it. `request_focus` resets the field's focus-lock filter, so calling it every frame let the arrow keys move focus out of the field, which committed the edit. `widgets::hot_number` still requests focus every frame, so its fields may have the same arrow-key problem; I left it out of this PR.

**Testing**

- New `crates/ui-egui/tests/timecode_ui.rs` (5 tests): dragging scrubs and stops at the start, typing replaces the value, relative input, Escape cancels, an invalid time is reported witho…

title: Project panel: dragging one of several selected items places them all, back to back, in one undo step
author: aw4e
body:
## What

Dragging one of several selected Project panel items onto the Timeline places all of them, back to back, as one undo step.

- The first item lands at the drop point and each next one where the previous one ends. Insert mode (Cmd/Ctrl) works the same way.
- Dropping on an empty Timeline creates the sequence from the first item and places the rest after it, also as one undo step.
- The drag ghost reads "N items" when the selection is dragged.
- Dragging an item that is not in the selection still places only that item.

## How

This follows the review: the placement is an engine command, so agents and the CLI can use it, and one undo step.

- `timeline.place` takes `items: [...]` as well as `item`. They are placed back to back; if one fails, none is placed. `sourceIn` and `duration` still need a single `item`.
- `file.newSequence` takes `fromItems: [...]` the same way.
- New `Session::edit_group` runs several edits as one undo step and rolls back if any of them fails.
- The UI (Timeline drop, empty Timeline) calls these commands and reports errors in the status line.
- Based on top of #517.

title: Hardening: an AAF weak-reference collection with a zero key size can't exhaust memory
author: haranishi
body:
An `.aaf` whose weak-reference vector/set index declares a key size of 0 made the importer loop `count` times (a `u32` from the file, up to 4.29 billion), pushing one empty key per turn. With a key size of 0 every `idx.get(9 + k * 0..9 + (k + 1) * 0)` succeeds, so nothing ever stopped the loop. A 2.5 KB file (its index stream is 9 bytes) could ask for about 100 GB (the allocation failure aborts the process) or hang the import for minutes. The strong-collection branches are bounded by the index length, and the MXF reader already returns early on a zero key size (`klv.rs`, `batch_of`); the weak branch had neither.

## What changes

- `crates/interchange/src/aaf/store.rs`: reject `count > 0 && size == 0` ("zero-size weak collection key"), and require, with checked arithmetic, that `9 + count * size` fits in the index stream before the loop starts. The iteration count is then bounded by the real stream length. For key sizes of 1 or more, the new bound is exactly what the old loop needed, so those files are read as before. A non-empty collection with key size 0, which the old code read as empty keys that nothing uses, is now an error (keys are AUIDs; the writer in `write.rs` emits 16-byte keys).
- `crates/interchange/src/aaf/hostile_tests.rs` (new, registered in `aaf/mod.rs`): the tests below. It is a new file rather than `tests.rs` so it stays clear of #419.

## Tests

- `zero_size_weak_collection_keys_are_an_error` fails before the fix ("read 1000000 empty keys instead of an error") and passes after; it covers the vector and the set form. A million keys show the problem cheaply; the real input asks for 4.29 billion.
- `weak_collection_count_beyond_the_index_is_an_error`: `count = u32::MAX` with a short index is an error (already true before the fix; it documents the bound).
- `weak_collections_within_the_index_are_read`: an empty collection and a two-key collection still read.

title: CFB: bound the DIFAT and FAT chain walks by the file's own size
author: haranishi
body:
`CompoundFile::open` runs whenever a file with the compound-file signature is opened, including when the AAF importer only sniffs a file (`aaf::sniff`). Two of its loop guards were derived from numbers the file controls:

1. **DIFAT walk.** The guard was `seen > n_difat.max(1) + max_sectors`, where `n_difat` is the header's `u32`. A DIFAT sector that names no FAT sector and points to itself therefore kept the loop going for up to about 4.3 billion passes, each reading a sector: about 14-16 s here for `n_difat = 100,000,000` and minutes for `u32::MAX`, from a 1 KB file.
2. **Sector chains.** `read_chain` stopped after `fat.len()` steps. The FAT is the concatenation of the sectors that the header and the DIFAT name, and one FAT sector can be named many times, so `fat.len()` can be 109 × sector_size / 4 entries. A chain that loops back on itself (the directory and the mini FAT are read with no size limit) then appended a whole sector per entry: a 457 MB buffer from a 450 KB file with 4 KB sectors, and about 117 GB (a process abort) from a ~7 MB file with 64 KB sectors.

## What changes

- `crates/cfb/src/read.rs`: the DIFAT walk stops after `max_sectors` passes instead of `n_difat + max_sectors` (the header's count is no longer trusted for the bound, and is no longer read); `read_chain` stops after `data.len() / sector_size + 1` steps instead of `fat.len()`. Neither chain can have more sectors than the file holds, so valid files are unaffected. The "chain loops" errors now name the bound (`… more than 111 sectors in a 450560-byte file`); nothing else in the repository matched the old texts. `read_mini_chain` is bounded by the stream size, which `open` already checks against the file length.

## Tests

- `difat_self_loop_fails_fast`: a 1 KB file with a self-pointing DIFAT sector and `n_difat = 100,000,000`. The test asserts the error that names the bound (3 sectors for this file). Before the fix the walk ran for about 14-16 s before failing with the old message; after i…

title: Give each picture its own link to the sound that overlaps it
author: vbasky
body:
Fixes #507.

Linking several cut pairs put every selected clip on one link. Selecting any one of them then selected the whole run.

A selection with more than one picture and at least one sound now keeps one link per picture, together with the selected sound that overlaps it. The same media wins over a longer overlap from another clip. A picture with no overlapping sound stays as it is, and so does sound that overlaps none of the pictures. One picture, or pictures with no sound selected, still share a single link, including two pictures on one track.

The first call on clips that are already linked still unlinks them. Undo, redo, and save/reopen keep the pairs.

title: Keyboard slip: clamp linked clips by one shared delta (#529)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Follow-up to #561 (issue #529).

#561 fixed `timeline.slip`, but the keyboard slip commands (`timeline.slipLeft`, `slipRight`, `slipLeft5`, `slipRight5`, Cmd+Alt+(Shift+)Left/Right) go through `slip_selection` in `crates/engine/src/keyboard.rs`, which still slipped each clip on its own. When a linked picture and sound clip had different media handles, slipping past the shorter handle stopped one clip at its media end while the other kept moving, so picture and sound drifted out of sync.

Changes:
- Moved the shared clamp from the `timeline.slip` command into `pub(crate) fn slip_together` in `commands.rs`. It probes each clip's slip on a copy of the sequence, takes the most constrained one, and slips every clip by the same fraction of its own media delta. `slip_selection` computes a media delta per clip (it scales by clip speed), so the helper scales the deltas instead of taking one tick value; for `timeline.slip`, where every delta is equal, this gives the same result as #561.
- `timeline.slip` and `slip_selection` both call `slip_together`.
- `slip_selection` groups the selected clips by link and calls `slip_together` once per group, so only linked partners are clamped together. Unlinked clips, and every clip when linked selection is off, slip on their own as before (the same rule `timeline.slip` follows through `with_links`).

Test: `keyboard_slip_keeps_linked_clips_in_sync_past_the_shorter_handle` places a linked pair, gives the picture 10 frames of tail handle and the sound 20, and presses Slip Left Five Frames three times. Before this change the picture stopped at +10 frames and the sound reached +15. Now both stop at +10. The test then turns linked selection off and checks that the sound slips on its own again.

title: Reject unknown mcp options instead of silently ignoring them (#476)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #476.

`filmcraft-cli mcp` accepted any `--x` option and ignored it. So `mcp --automation-read-root DIR` (PhotoCraft's confinement flag) started a server with no sandbox and no warning.

Now `mcp` accepts only the options it uses: `--bridge`, `--project`, `--demo` and `--data-dir`. Any other option stops it before the server starts:

```
filmcraft-cli: unknown mcp option `--automation-read-root`
Run `filmcraft-cli help` for usage.
```

The exit code is 2. That is what `filmcraft-cli` already uses for usage errors (`usage()`, e.g. an unknown subcommand). designcraft-cli rejects unknown `mcp` options in the same way.

- `Args::unknown_opt(allowed)` returns the first option that is not in the list. The unit test covers `--automation-read-root X`, an `--x=value` typo, and a valid set of options.
- `docs/agents.md` now says that the MCP server takes no other options and has no folder-confinement flags.

The change is limited to `mcp`, which the issue is about. The other subcommands still ignore unknown flags.

title: Audio Clip Mixer: click the dB readout to type a volume (#481)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #481.

The dB value under each Audio Clip Mixer strip was a plain painted label, so the clip volume could only be changed with the fader. It now uses the same `widgets::hot_number` control as the Audio Track Mixer's readout: click it to type a value (Enter applies, clamped to the fader range `FADER_MIN_DB..FADER_MAX_DB`), or drag it to scrub.

The new value goes through the strip's existing `set`/`release` helpers, so it behaves like a fader move: `clipMixer.set` on the clip under the playhead (honouring the strip's Write Keyframes toggle), or `clipMixer.touch`/`clipMixer.release` during an automation pass. When no clip is under the playhead the readout stays dimmed as before and ignores input. The automation id `clipMixer.<track>.value` now covers the control's actual rect, as in the track mixer.

Test: `mixer_ui::clip_mixer_db_value_can_be_typed` clicks `clipMixer.A1.value`, types `-20`, presses Enter and checks the clip's volume level is -20 dB. It fails on main (the label does not react to clicks).

title: #402: WebM transparency (VP9 alpha in BlockAdditions)
author: liangforstudy
body: Part of #402 (WebM; APNG follows in a separate PR). ## What and why A WebM VP9 track with `AlphaMode` 1 stores its alpha as a second, independently coded VP9 stream in each block's `BlockAdditional` (`BlockAddID` 1). The Matroska reader detected `AlphaMode` (`has_alpha` was true) but never read the additions, so transparent areas rendered black. - **matroska:** `BlockAdditions` in BlockGroups are parsed; the `BlockAdditional` with ID 1 of an unlaced block is kept as `Sample::addition` and read with `MkvFile::read_sample_addition`. - **codecs:** a WebM VP9 track with `AlphaMode` and additions gets an `AlphaDecoder` (`webm_alpha.rs`). It decodes each sample's alpha frame with a second software VP9 decoder and attaches its luma plane (full range, converted to the picture's bit depth; RGB profiles get the A channel) as the frame's alpha. - After a seek, the alpha decoder resynchronises from the nearest alpha key frame (the alpha stream's key frames need not match the colour ones). - Colour pictures are held until their alpha picture is out: the two decoders can return pictures after different calls (frame threading), which made a first version drop the alpha of the last frame before a key frame ~40% of the time. - Best effort: a missing or undecodable alpha frame leaves that picture opaque and never fails the colour decode. ## How it was tested - New `tests::vp9_webm_alpha_layer_matches_libvpx`: an ffmpeg-made `yuva420p` WebM whose alpha changes every frame; frames requested out of order (seeks across key frames) and then forward must match ffmpeg's **libvpx** decode exactly, colour and alpha (ffmpeg's native VP9 decoder ignores the alpha layer). **Fails without the fix** (`no alpha plane`). Passed 200/200 runs, four in parallel. - `set_alpha` unit tests: 8-bit, 10-bit and RGBA pictures; a mismatched or truncate…

title: Export: CRF (constant quality) for H.264
author: JordyUSA
body:
## What

Adds a **CRF (constant quality)** option to Bitrate Encoding for H.264 exports. The built-in encoder already had `RateControl::Crf`, but export only ever used CBR or VBR.

- **Export panel:** "CRF (constant quality)" shows a **Quality (CRF)** slider (0–51, default 23) instead of the Target and Maximum Bitrate fields. It's greyed out for H.265, which has no software encoder.
- **Settings:** `BitrateMode::Crf` plus `ExportSettings::crf`. Presets saved earlier load with CRF 23 and keep their mode. A CRF outside 0–51, or not a number, is rejected by `validate()`.
- **`file.exportMedia`:** takes `crf` (on its own it switches to CRF mode) and `bitrateMode: "crf"`.
- **Hardware encoders:** VideoToolbox and NVENC decline CRF, so the built-in encoder runs.
- Spanish and Japanese translations for the two new labels.

## Level for CRF streams (h264enc)

With no bitrate cap, the level used to be picked from the frame size and rate alone. A CRF 0 export of 1080p30 camera footage averaged **105 Mb/s with a 147 Mb/s peak** but was labelled **High@L4**, whose limit is 25 Mb/s. The encoder now sizes the level for an estimated worst case: 3 bits per pixel at CRF 0, halving every 6 steps. So 1080p30 at CRF 0 gets **5.1**, and at the default CRF 23 stays at **4.0**. Checked on a real export: the 1080p23.976 demo at CRF 0 now reads `High@L5` in MediaInfo.

## Settings note in the stream

The user_data_unregistered SEI the encoder already wrote now also lists the settings, x264-style, under FilmCraft's own UUID:


title: #260: file dialogs on Linux no longer stop the app (GNOME "not responding")
author: MrCloudy2
body:
Fixes #260.

## What was wrong

Every native file dialog (Import, Open, Save As, Export… destinations, preset import/export, Link Media, Browse… buttons: 34 call sites) called a synchronous host hook such as `pick_files` and used the path right away. On Linux, rfd shows the dialog through the XDG desktop portal and waits for it on the UI thread, so the frame loop stops for as long as the dialog is open: nothing repaints, control-channel requests aren't answered, and GNOME offers to force-quit the window after about five seconds of unanswered pings.

Measured on KDE Wayland (xdg-desktop-portal-kde) with File ▸ Import open: before the dialog a control request is answered in 6 ms; while it is open, **no answer at all** (6 s timeout).

## What it does now

This follows the approach suggested in the issue: ask for a dialog with a continuation, run the dialog off the UI thread, and apply the result when it arrives.

- **`crates/ui-egui/src/native_dialogs.rs` (new):** `FileDialog` (open files / one file / project, save project, save as, folder, relink) and two entry points:
  - `FilmcraftApp::pick(dialog, then)` for menu and control-channel commands. With the synchronous pickers, `then` runs at once and its result is the command's result, so agents, MCP and tests see exactly what they saw before. With a runner the command answers `{"dialog": "open"}`.
  - `FilmcraftApp::pick_ui(dialog, then)` for a panel's buttons. `then` always runs at the start of a later frame, before the panels draw: a panel works on a copy of its state and writes it back at the end of the frame, which would otherwise overwrite the path. It writes into the dialog's stored state (`app.ui.…` or the egui temporary); if the user has closed that dialog meanwhile, the path goes nowhere.

  One dialog is open at a time. Asking for another is refused with "A file dialog is already open" (status line / command error; Spanish entry added). A dialog whose host thread ends without an answer counts as cancelled.
- …

title: Export: never crash on WAV/AIFF over 4 GiB; stream PCM to disk
author: JordyUSA
body:
## The crash

`pcm::write_wav` and `write_aiff` stored sizes in `u32` with unchecked arithmetic (`interleaved.len() as u32 * bps`, `20 + fmt_len + data_len`). Once the audio passes 4 GiB, a debug build panics on overflow and a release build writes a wrapped, corrupt header. That's after about 41 minutes of 24-bit 5.1 at 96 kHz, or about 4 hours of 24-bit stereo at 48 kHz. The whole file was also built in a `Vec` first, so a 4 GiB WAV needed more than 4 GiB of RAM.

## The fix

- **WAV over 4 GiB → RF64** (EBU Tech 3306): `RF64` with size `0xFFFFFFFF`, a `ds64` chunk carrying the 64-bit RIFF size, data size and sample count, and a `data` chunk sized `0xFFFFFFFF`. Anything up to 4 GiB is still plain `RIFF`, byte for byte.
- **AIFF over 4 GiB is refused:** AIFF has no 64-bit form. The export fails before anything is written, with a message that names WAV instead.
- **Streaming:** `pcm::header` builds the header from the known frame count, then `pcm::encode` writes the samples one second per chunk through the existing `Out` (a file, or memory for an `OutputSink`). Memory stays flat, and progress now advances per second of audio.
- **Pad byte:** odd-sized data chunks (e.g. 24-bit mono with an odd frame count) now get the pad byte RIFF and AIFF require, and it's counted in the container size.
- **Hostile values:** a frame count, channel count or sample rate that overflows any size now produces an `Unsupported` error instead of a panic.

`write_wav` / `write_aiff` are kept as whole-file helpers on top of `header` + `encode` and now return `Result`. Inside the workspace they were only used by export.

## Tests

- `wav_past_4_gib_is_rf64`: header layout for an hour of 24-bit 5.1 at 96 kHz (6.2 GB).
- `wav_up_to_4_gib_stays_riff`: the largest file that stays plain RIFF, and that one more frame switches to RF64.
- `aiff_past_4_gib_is_refused_not_wrapped`, `hostile_sizes_are_errors`, `odd_data_chunks_are_padded`.
- `ffprobe_reads_rf64_duration`: writes a 5-hour RF64 header plus…

title: Escape cancels a drag in progress: drag-and-drop, value drags, color pickers and dialogs
author: ReReddo
body:
Closes #580.

egui ends a drag when Escape is pressed, and FilmCraft treated that as a release, so the drag was committed wherever the pointer was. Now Escape while a mouse button is held takes the drag back and leaves everything as it was before the press. I tried to apply this everywhere a drag can happen, so it behaves the same across the app.

**Commit 1: drag-and-drop**

- Timeline: clip moves, trims, rolls, slips, slides, stretches, caption blocks and automation keyframes. The clips stay put and stay selected.
- Items carried between panels (a clip or sequence from the Project panel, Source monitor drags, effects, presets, graphics templates): the payload is cleared. `panels::cancel_drag` / `drag_cancelled` keep a cancelled drag from starting again until the button comes up.
- Freeform card moves go back.
- Media Browser drags, which import when the drag starts, take the import back.

**Commit 2: value drags, color pickers and dialogs**

- Value drags in panels (hot numbers, sliders and color pickers in Effect Controls, Properties, Lumetri and elsewhere). The engine gets `Session::undo_mark()` / `revert_to(mark)`. The app marks the history at the start of the frame a press begins and reverts to the mark on Escape. `revert_to` drops those steps without putting them on the redo stack. The mark is taken at the start of the frame because the color picker's 2D slider changes the value on the press frame itself.

title: Windows: draw with the newest driver when one GPU is listed through two Vulkan drivers
author: JeremyYao
body:
## Problem

On a PC whose GPUs were installed from different driver packages, FilmCraft dies on launch with
`STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION` (`0xc0000005`) before the window appears. Seen on an ASUS ROG G513QY
(Ryzen 9 5900HX integrated Radeon on AMD's 2021 package, Radeon RX 6800M on the 2026 package).

Each package registers its own Vulkan ICD, so the loader lists the RX 6800M twice: first through the
2021 `amdvlk64.dll` (Vulkan 1.2), then through the 2026 one (Vulkan 1.4). wgpu's default
`request_adapter` takes the first discrete adapter, which is the stale entry, and drawing through it
crashes inside the driver with no Rust frame on the stack (the panic hook and `catch_unwind` never
see it; Windows writes a dump to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\CrashDumps`).

## Fix

`apps/filmcraft/src/graphics.rs` installs an egui-wgpu `native_adapter_selector`:

- keeps wgpu's own ranking between different GPUs (device type for `WGPU_POWER_PREF`, then
  enumeration order), so machines with one driver per GPU get exactly the choice they got before;
- among entries that are one physical GPU (same backend, vendor and device id, and bus id when both
  drivers report one; adapters without ids are never merged), prefers the entry exposing the most
  wgpu features, i.e. the newer driver;
- skips adapters that cannot draw to the window, and returns an error (the existing "could not start
  its window" dialog) instead of panicking when none can;
- logs every candidate, a warning naming the duplicated GPU and its drivers, and the choice;
- `WGPU_ADAPTER_NAME` (part of the adapter's name, backend or driver text, any case) picks an
  adapter by hand, so two same-named entries can be told apart.

Nothing is tied to a GPU model, driver version or machine. The README's Windows troubleshooting
section documents the duplicate-driver case and the override.

## Tests

The choice is a pure function over plain candidate data, so it has GPU-free unit tests in the same
file (11 tests, 45 in the crate):

- the exact ada…

title: feat: Add Russian (ru) localization

title: Export: FLAC (clean-room encoder; .flac files and FLAC audio in MP4/MOV)
author: JordyUSA
body:
> **Depends on #606.** This branch is built on the PCM streaming fix, because FLAC export reuses its chunked writer. Until #606 merges, this PR also shows that commit (`2e21c44`). Review the last two commits.

## What

- **`filmcraft-flac`**: a new L0 crate, a clean-room FLAC encoder written from [RFC 9639](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9639). It depends only on `filmcraft-bitstream` and `thiserror`, has no `unsafe`, and builds for wasm. No libFLAC or FFmpeg code was read; ffmpeg is used only as a test oracle.
  - Subframes: constant, verbatim, fixed predictors (order 0–4) and LPC up to order 12 (Levinson–Durbin on Tukey(0.5)-windowed autocorrelation, quantised coefficients with error feedback), whichever is smallest.
  - Residuals: partitioned Rice codes. Stereo: left/side, side/right or mid/side per frame.
  - Integrity: CRC-8 and CRC-16, plus a STREAMINFO MD5 using our own RFC 1321 implementation.
  - Levels 0–8, all lossless. 1–8 channels, 8–24 bit, any sample rate.
- **Export, audio only:** a new `FLAC` format writes `.flac` at 16 or 24 bit. Like WAV/AIFF it streams one second at a time, and STREAMINFO is rewritten at the end with frame sizes, total samples and MD5. There's a new preset, "FLAC 48 kHz 24-bit".
- **Export, FLAC audio in MP4 and QuickTime:** stored as `fLaC` + `dfLa`, one frame per sample. The short last frame gets its true duration, so the audio is exactly as long as the range.
  - `dfLa` is replaced before the `moov` is written, via a new `Mp4Writer::set_sample_entry`, so it carries the final STREAMINFO.
  - Two new `AudioEncoder` methods support this: `flush_timed` and `final_sample_entry`. Their defaults keep AAC unchanged.
  - MXF stays PCM.
- **UI and commands:**
  - Audio Format gains **FLAC (lossless)**: MP4 offers AAC or FLAC; MOV offers AAC, PCM or FLAC.
  - A **Compression Level** control (default 5) appears when FLAC is chosen.
  - `file.exportMedia` accepts `format: "flac"`, `audioCodec` and `flacLevel`.
  - Spanish and Japanese s…

title: timeline, project panel: paste images and copied files from the system clipboard
author: ReReddo
body:
Closes #611.

Ctrl+V only pasted clips copied inside FilmCraft. Now it also pastes what other apps put on the clipboard:

- **Images** (a screenshot, an image copied in a browser or an image editor) are saved as `Pasted Image <n>.png` and imported.
- **Files** copied in Explorer / Finder (video, audio, images) are imported.
- **Timeline:** they are placed at the playhead, end to end, **without overwriting anything**. Each clip goes on the first free track from the targeted one outward (up for video, down for audio). When every track is busy there, a new track is added, so an image pasted over footage sits above it as an overlay.
- **Ctrl+Shift+V** (Paste Insert) inserts them on the targeted tracks instead, pushing later clips right, as with clips.
- **Project panel:** Ctrl+V imports into the shown bin and places nothing.
- **Undo** takes the whole paste back in one step, including the import and any track it added. The playhead moves to the end, as after Paste.
- **Whichever was copied last wins.** Copying clips already puts their names on the system clipboard as text (#199), so media on the clipboard was copied after them. Without media, Paste pastes the copied clips as before.

**Changes**

- `crates/engine/src/paste_media.rs` (new): `edit.pasteMedia {paths, insert, place, bin}` imports and places. `save_pasted_image` writes the PNG where voice-over takes and narrations go, through `voiceover::media_dir` (from #278): Project Settings ▸ Scratch Disks ▸ Captured Audio and Video, else next to the project file, else the data directory for an unsaved project. title: Let a bin be cleared from its context menu, the trash button, the panel menu and Delete (#587)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #587.

A bin could not be removed from the Project panel. The engine already handles it: `project.delete` with `{"items": [binId]}` removes a named bin and everything in it. The UI just never sent the bin's id.

- **Bin right-click menu:** now has **Clear**. It sends `project.delete` with `{"items": [bin]}`, the same way the item context menu's Clear does.
- **Trash button (panel footer), panel menu ▸ Delete, and Backspace/Delete with the Project panel focused:** a new helper, `clear_params`, picks what to send. If items are selected, it sends `{}`, so the selection is cleared as before. If no items are selected but a bin is, it sends `{"items": [bin]}`. If nothing is selected, the footer still shows "Select items to clear" and the menu entry stays disabled. Clicking a bin clears the item selection, so this fallback covers exactly the "I clicked a bin" case.
- The keyboard fallback runs only while the Project panel has focus. Delete is also an app-wide binding for `project.delete`, and pressing it while another panel is focused should not delete the bin that was clicked earlier.

Test: `clear_falls_back_to_the_selected_bin` covers the three cases of `clear_params`. The engine side (deleting a bin by id) is already covered by `explicit_targets_tests` and `project_tools_tests`.

title: Space out browser downloads so image-sequence exports are not dropped (#378)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #378.

**Cause.** On the web build, every file the app writes goes through `fs::set_on_write` -> `fs::download`. That function clicked a hidden Blob anchor at once, for each file. An image-sequence export (PNG/TIFF/BMP, one file per frame) wrote all its frames in one go. That fired 20 anchor clicks in the same instant, and Chrome dropped about half of them. This matches the reporter's control: the same bytes clicked 125 ms apart all arrived.

**Fix.**
- New pure module `download_pacing.rs` (same pattern as `recovery_policy.rs`). `Pacer::reserve(now)` gives each download a slot at least `GAP_MS` (125 ms) after the previous one and returns how long to wait. A download after a quiet period is not delayed.
- `fs::download` still creates the Blob URL and anchor right away. The append + click now runs in the existing `spawn_local` task after the delay. The Blob URL is still revoked 60 s after the click (it used to be 60 s after the call). A failed append is logged as `download <name>: ...`, like the caller's message.
- Only the web download path changes. Native export writes straight to disk and is not affected.

**Tests.** `apps/filmcraft-web/tests/download_pacing.rs` runs natively, like `tests/recovery_policy.rs`:
- `burst_of_downloads_is_spaced_out`: 20 downloads requested at the same instant get delays 0, 125, ..., 2375 ms.
- `download_after_a_pause_is_immediate`: a later, single download is not delayed.

I did not run this in a browser.

title: Media: Automatically refresh growing files works (and catches re-renders)
author: KattKnight
body:
## What this does

**Settings ▸ Media ▸ Automatically refresh growing files** and *Refresh growing files every* were listed but not wired. They now work, and they cover the other common case as well: a render written over the file a clip uses.

That's the After Effects → Premiere round trip, done the file way: re-render a comp in EffectCraft and the FilmCraft timeline shows the new version.

### How it works

- **Checking:**
  - The desktop app stamps each file media item's file (size and modification time).
  - It does this every *Refresh growing files every* seconds (default 60), **and** as soon as its window comes back to the front. So switching back after a render picks it up at once.
  - The stamps are taken on a worker thread.
- **Refreshing:** a changed file is opened again, the way import opens it. The item then gets:
  - the new `MediaInfo` (a longer duration, another frame size);
  - a new identity, so relinking compares against the new file;
  - a fresh source in the media pool. The old source still indexes the file as it was, and could decode garbage from the new bytes.
- **Not an edit:** the view refreshes through `bump_view`, so there's no undo step and a clean project isn't marked modified. The file changed, not the edit.
- **Files not ready yet:** a file that can't be opened yet keeps its old stamp, so the next look tries again. A file seen for the first time is only remembered.
- **New command:** `media.refreshChanged` runs one look (CLI, MCP). Both Settings rows are now marked wired.

## Tests

- **New tests:** `media_watch_tests` has 3 tests:
  - A movie re-rendered as another scene at twice the length (`make_movie`) shows the new picture (PSNR > 40 dB against a fresh import), the new length and the new identity, with no undo step and not dirty.
  - A half-written movie is retried.
  - The background look works.
- **Live check:** `effectcraft-cli` rendered a red 1 s comp to H.264. The built FilmCraft app imported it and made a sequence from it.

title: #374: trim preview keeps the waveform in place instead of squeezing it
author: JordyUSA
body:
Refs #374 (item 13: *"When shortening an audio clip, the waveform squishes down as the length is decreased, making it impossible to tell where to let go"*). It addresses only that item, so it doesn't close the issue.

## The bug

While a clip edge is dragged, `preview_drag` gives the clip's new start and duration, but `draw_clip` was still handed the **untrimmed** `TrackItem`. `draw_waveform` maps each pixel to `it.start + it.duration × fraction`, so the clip's whole original source range was spread over the shorter (or longer) box. The waveform squeezed, and the sound under the pointer moved as you dragged. That made it hard to trim to the point where music starts after a quiet intro. On release the real edit applied and the waveform jumped back.

## The fix

- Trim and roll previews now produce the **edited item** (`edited: HashMap<ClipId, TrackItem>`), and the clip is drawn from it. Every timeline time the clip still covers shows the same media, and the waveform is cut off at the moving edge. Video thumbnails show the new first frame for the same reason.
- The per-item update in `trim` and `ripple_trim_group` is factored into **`filmcraft_edit::move_edge`**, which the preview also uses. Preview and edit therefore agree for speed-changed, reversed and frame-held clips, and the behaviour of both trims is unchanged.
- **Rate Stretch** still squeezes on purpose, since it really fits the same media into a new length.
- `preview_drag` loses its unused `_layout` parameter.

## Verification

- `edit`: `moving_an_edge_keeps_the_media_under_the_timeline` covers speed 1/2/0.5, reversed, reversed ×2 and frame-held clips, In and Out edges, in both directions. The media at every remaining timeline time is unchanged, and the result equals the real `trim`.
- `ui-egui` (`trim_preview_tests`): on the demo project, trimming Ambient_Score.wav's In/Out edges and rolling an A1 cut keep the media in place, with the preview positions unchanged. A Rate Stretch still draws from the origin…

title: codecs: H.264 High 10 and High 4:2:2 decoding, bit-exact
author: 4papuce
body:
Closes #626  

## Summary

`filmcraft-h264` now decodes **8- to 10-bit 4:2:0 and 4:2:2** streams (Baseline / Main / High /
High 10 / High 4:2:2) bit-exactly — including Panasonic Lumix 4K `H264_422_LongGOP` camera
material — and outputs them through `filmcraft-codecs` as `Yuv16` / `Chroma::C422`. 8-bit 4:2:0
behaviour and performance are unchanged; hardware decode (VA-API) still declines the new formats
and falls back to software.

## Implementation (ITU-T H.264, edition 04/2017; spec text only, no decoder sources read)

- **Sample pipeline** (`picture.rs`): planes are `u16` for every bit depth (the `filmcraft-hevc`
  pattern), 8-bit streams narrowed at output (`Plane::U8` / `Plane::U16`).
- **Bit depth**: residual scaling on the effective QP (`QP′ = QP + QpBdOffset`, 7-38/8-312),
  `Clip1Y/Clip1C` in reconstruction, weighted-prediction offsets scaled in the weight derivation
  (8-291/8-292/8-296/8-297), deblocking thresholds scaled by `1 << (BitDepth-8)` with the tables
  indexed on raw QPY/QPC (8.7.2.2), I_PCM `u(BitDepth)` samples (7.3.5), QPY wrap over
  `52 + QpBdOffsetY`.
- **4:2:2 chroma**: 2x4 chroma DC transform with the scan-order remap (8-305) and `qPDC = qP + 3`
  scaling (8-327..8-329); CAVLC `nC = -2` and CABAC ctxBlockCat 3 with `NumC8x8 = 2`
  (`ctxIdxInc = Min(levelListIdx / NumC8x8, 2)`, 9-22); whole-block 8x16 intra chroma prediction
  (8.3.4, Plane with `yCF = 4`); chroma motion with `mvCLX = mvLX` and `yFracC = (mv & 3) << 1`
  (8-221/8-222, 8-231..8-234); deblocking chroma edges `yE = 0, 4, 8, 12` filtered regardless of
  `transform_size_8x8_flag` (8.7 / Figure 8-10), block scan `x = (idx % 2) * 4, y = (idx / 2) * 4`
  (6.4.7).
- **Output** (`filmcraft-codecs`): `PixelData::Yuv16` with `Chroma::C422` / `bits`, mirrors the
  HEVC converter; `set_plane_allocator` gains the u16 twin.

## Tests

- New oracle fixtures (`tests/conformance.rs`): `high10_cabac`, `high10_cavlc_8x8`,
  `high10_weightb`, `high422_cabac`, `high422_cavlc`, `high422_intra`, …

title: ui: reject software rasterizers for GPU compositing and say so
author: 4papuce
body:
Fixes #632 

## Problem

When wgpu falls back to a software rasterizer (llvmpipe / SwiftShader / softpipe — containers and
VMs without GPU device access, missing drivers), `set_wgpu` accepted it as the GPU compositor
(llvmpipe satisfies the `Rgba16Float` checks), so the preview quietly composited through WGSL on a
CPU rasterizer: GPU usage 0 %, CPU 100 %, laggy playback, no visible explanation.

## Change

- `filmcraft-ui-egui`: new `software_rasterizer(&AdapterInfo)` detects CPU rasterizers
  (`device_type == Cpu`, or llvmpipe / SwiftShader / softpipe in the name); `gpu_compositor_unsupported`
  rejects them first, so the monitors use the native CPU compositor, which renders the same frames
  faster than wgpu-on-llvmpipe.
- `set_wgpu` now puts the reason in the status bar ("GPU acceleration is unavailable; preview
  renders on the CPU (software rasterizer (llvmpipe, Cpu))") in addition to the log line, so the
  symptom is self-explanatory instead of looking like a renderer bug.
- New `tl!` string with Spanish, Japanese and Simplified Chinese translations (the enforced
  complete catalogs).

## Tests

- `gpu_fallback_tests::software_rasterizers_are_detected`: llvmpipe/Cpu, a real GPU name reporting
  `DeviceType::Cpu`, SwiftShader, and softpipe are detected; an AMD discrete GPU and Apple
  integrated GPU are not.
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-ui-egui`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets
  -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask assets` pass.
- Verified live on a machine whose sandbox hides `/dev/dri`: before, the app logged
  "Software rasterizer detected ... llvmpipe" and composited on it; after, it logs
  "GPU compositor disabled (software rasterizer (llvmpipe (LLVM …), Cpu)); compositing on the CPU"

title: Linux: default to XWayland for file drag-and-drop on Wayland desktops
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
### Rationale & History

Under Wayland sessions, dragging and dropping video clips, audio tracks, and project files from desktop file managers onto FilmCraft showed a "no" (prohibited) cursor and drops did not function.

This occurs because `eframe 0.36.2` depends on `winit 0.30.13`. In `winit 0.30`, Wayland drag-and-drop was not implemented ([winit#1881](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/issues/1881)). Native Wayland drag-and-drop was added for `winit 0.31` in [winit#4571](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4571) (merged July 2026, tagged in `0.31.0-beta.3`). However, updating to `winit 0.31` directly is blocked by breaking event loop API changes until upstream `eframe` adds support.

On X11 / XWayland, drag-and-drop is fully supported in `winit 0.30`. This pull request adopts the established pattern from `designcraft` and `deckcraft` by Brandon Thomas:
1. Adds `winit = { version = "0.30", default-features = false, features = ["x11"] }` under `cfg(all(unix, not(target_os = "macos")))`.
2. Extends `agent_event_loop` to provide an event loop builder hook: when an X server is reachable (`DISPLAY` is set) and `FILMCRAFT_WAYLAND` is not set, configures `EventLoopBuilderExtX11::with_x11()` to route through XWayland so file drops work out of the box on standard Wayland desktop sessions.
3. Allows users desiring pure native Wayland to opt out and preserve the native Wayland backend by setting `FILMCRAFT_WAYLAND=1`.

### Verification
Verified local compilation and dependency resolution with `cargo check -p filmcraft` on Linux (0 errors, 0 warnings).

title: macOS: open projects from Finder, the Dock and `open -a`
author: LloydNicholson
body:
## Problem
- **Finder never offers FilmCraft.** FilmCraft exports the `.fcproj` type but declares no `CFBundleDocumentTypes`, so Finder doesn't offer it for a project, in Open With or on double-click.
- **`open -a` doesn't open anything.** `open -a FilmCraft p.fcproj` starts the app without opening the project. LaunchServices sends the path as a `kAEOpenDocuments` Apple event, which winit 0.30 doesn't handle.

## Fix
- **`packaging/macos/Info.plist.in`:** FilmCraft owns `ai.storyteller.filmcraft.project` (`.fcproj`).

title: Project panel: double-click anywhere empty in Icon view opens Import
author: JordyUSA
body:
## The bug

Double-clicking empty space in the Project panel opens Import, but it stopped working once the project had something in it. The way it was found: placing audio in the timeline adds the audio clip (and its sequence) to the Project panel, and then double-clicking the blank space did nothing.

**Cause:** in Icon view each row of cards is laid out as a hover-only strip (`allocate_exact_size(…, Sense::hover())`). The only click-sensing empty space was `empty_space`, the strip *under* the last row. With an empty project, that strip is the whole panel. Once there are cards, most of the visible blank space sits beside or between them, and that space ignored clicks.

I found no existing issue or PR for this.

## The fix

`empty_background` registers a click-sensing area over the visible Icon view (`ui.clip_rect()`) **before** the cards. egui gives later widgets priority, so cards keep their own clicks, drags and double-clicks, and everything else lands on the background. It shares its handlers with the bottom strip through `empty_interactions`: click deselects, double-click imports, right-click opens the panel menu. List view rows already span the full width, and Freeform already has a full-canvas background, so neither needed changes.

## Tests

Both tests use real pointer input at 60 fps (two press/release pairs a frame apart), with `hooks.pick_files` counting how often Import opens:

- `double_click_empty_area_imports_with_a_project_loaded`: an empty project's empty area, then the gap between the demo project's first two bins and the space right of the last bin in the row. A double-click *on* a bin still opens the bin, not Import.

title: MP4: read the start timecode from a Sony rtmd track when there is no tmcd
author: maxm11
body:
Fixes #460.

Sony XAVC cameras (FX3, a6400, …) keep a clip's start timecode in an `rtmd` (real-time metadata) data track instead of a QuickTime `tmcd` track. FilmCraft only looked for `tmcd`, so `probe` reported `start_timecode: null` and timecode sync could not use the footage.

## Change

When no `tmcd` track provides a start timecode, read it from the first `rtmd` sample and expose it as `MediaInfo::start_timecode`. Sony stores the fields as raw decimal bytes in the sample's fixed header — hours, minutes, seconds, a drop-frame flag, then frames — which is exactly the block ffmpeg reads for the `timecode` tag of an `rtmd` stream. The frame count is derived with `filmcraft_time::fields_to_frames` using the video frame rate and the drop-frame flag, matching how a `tmcd` start frame is treated. The parse is defensive (missing/short sample → `None`, no panic).

The layout is proprietary and undocumented, so it was derived from real footage rather than a specification; the offset was verified byte-by-byte against ffprobe's `timecode` tag (setting the flag byte toggles `:`→`;`, and patching the hour/minute/second/frame bytes changes the reported string).

## Tests

- `crates/codecs/tests/mp4_rtmd.rs`: a hand-built MP4 with a video track and an `rtmd` track exercises the whole probe path (start timecode `781234` = `03:37:00:34` at 59.94), plus a too-short-sample case.
- Unit test for the field reader, including the drop-frame flag and short input.

Verified on a real a6400 XAVC file: `filmcraft-cli probe` now reports `"start_timecode": 781234` where ffprobe reports `timecode=03:37:00:34`.

All new code is in the codecs  layer; no public API in `isobmff` changed.

title: perf(export): index the bin tree once in closure() (#536 follow-up)
author: maxm11
body:
Follow-up to the P2 finding on #557 (now merged as 913b45c).

## Problem

`closure()` told bins apart from items with `p.root.find_bin(bin)` for **every queued id**. `Bin::find_bin` walks the whole tree when the id is an item, so exporting N items from a flat N-item project did O(N²) work even when no bins were selected (measured ~2.38 ms → ~823 ms for 40,000 flat items, ~346×).

## Fix

Walk the bin tree **once** up front, recording the set of bin ids and each bin's direct children. Then:
- membership in the bin set replaces the per-id `find_bin` traversal, and
- a named bin expands from the indexed children (BFS over sub-bins) instead of a second `all_items` walk per bin.

`closure()` is now O(N log N) over the items plus entries touched, with identical results (the keep set is a `BTreeSet`). The bin semantics from #557 are unchanged: a non-root bin contributes its items and their dependencies, the top bin is excluded (#244), and only real item ids are returned.

## Verification

- `export_selection_project_of_a_bin_exports_its_contents` and `export_selection_project_and_ale` pass.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

title: fix: prevent duplicate file imports (tier 1 only) (#356)
author: mjohnson7cd
body:
Fixes #356  
Replaces #438 with simplified tier-1-only implementation per maintainer feedback.

## Summary
Prevents importing the same file multiple times using canonical path comparison (tier 1 only). Optimized for performance on large projects with network storage.

## The Problem
Users dragging folders couldn't detect duplicates, causing lag when the same file was imported multiple times with different path spellings (`./file` vs `/absolute/path` vs symlinks).

## Solution: Tier 1 Only (Canonical Path)

Per @echelon's feedback, this implements **only tier 1** - no Services extensions, no file identity, no media identity.

### Implementation Details:

**find_duplicate_item() helper:**
- Filename filter first (fast string comparison)
- Lazy canonicalization only on filename matches
- Avoids stat-ing thousands of items on every import
- Returns `Option<ItemId>` on duplicate

**Result structure:**
- `duplicates`: `[{path, item}]` separate from `errors`
- Toast: "N file(s) already in the project"

### Performance:
- Network storage: only items with matching filenames are canonicalized
- Project with 1000 clips importing 1 file: ~1 canonicalization instead of 1000
- Scales well to large projects

## Changes
- 2 files: `commands.rs` (+59 lines), `tests.rs` (+46 lines)
- Total: +91 lines (vs +1,002 in previous PR)
- Single helper function, no new modules
- Test: `duplicate_file_import_detection` covers absolute + relative paths

## Testing
✅ Test passes: duplicate detection via absolute path, relative path (`./`)  
✅ Compiles cleanly  
✅ No settings_tests modifications needed

## What was dropped from #438:
- Tiers 2 & 3 (file identity, media identity)
- `Services::canonical_path`/`file_identity` trait methods
- `FileIdentity` type
- `import_duplicates.rs` module (634 lines)
- settings_tests workarounds

This is the minimal fix requested - tier 1 alone fixes #356 as reported.

title: #598: import AVI files (clean-room AVI / OpenDML demuxer)
author: JordyUSA
body:
Closes #598.

## What

AVI files now import, play and probe, through `file.import`, the Import dialog and the Media Browser.

**`filmcraft-avi`** is a new L0 crate, written from Microsoft's AVI RIFF reference and OpenDML 1.02. It has no dependencies, no `unsafe`, and builds for wasm. No libavformat or other AVI implementation was read; ffmpeg and ffprobe are used only as test oracles.
- **Headers:** `avih`, plus per stream `strh`, `strf` (`BITMAPINFOHEADER`, `WAVEFORMATEX` / `WAVEFORMATEXTENSIBLE`) and `strn`.
- **Index, best available first:** the OpenDML `indx` super index → `ix##` standard indexes (field indexes included); else `idx1` (relative to `movi` or absolute), plus a scan of the `RIFF AVIX` extensions it can't see; else a scan of `movi`, where keyframes are unknown and reported as such.
- **Robustness:** sizes are clamped to the file, so a cut-off recording opens with what was saved. `rec ` lists nest at most 3 deep, and tables are bounded by what the file could hold.

**`AviSource`** (`filmcraft-codecs`):
- **Video:** Motion JPEG, H.264 and HEVC (Annex B, our decoders), plus uncompressed BGR24 / BGRX32 / YUY2 / UYVY / I420 / YV12 / NV12 / grey through a new `RawVideoDecoder`. Empty "drop frame" chunks hold the previous picture.
- **B-frames:** AVI has no timestamps, so H.264 with B-frames is stored in decode order. Display order comes from picture order counts (reusing `mxf::avc_presentation_order`), and pictures keep their slots. A quick look at the first 300 frames decides whether the stream reorders at all, so reading every frame's header is only done for streams that need it.
- **Fine time bases:** ffmpeg copying an MP4's 1/600 time base gives 600 slots/s with a picture in every 20th. FilmCraft reports the rate the pictures play at (30 fps), not 600.
- **Audio:** PCM (integer and float) straight from chunks. MP3 / MP2 and AC-3 frames, which AVI chunks needn't follow, are found again across chunks with a new `filmcraft_mpegts::frame_bytes` helper.
- *…

title: #591: named clips that cannot stand in for a selection say why
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #591.

## Problem
Commands that take `clips` / `clip` (e.g. `clip.speedDuration`, `edit.rippleDelete`, `clip.enable`) answered **"no clips selected"** whenever the named ids were not clips of the active sequence. Over MCP or the control channel, that reads as if the explicit ids were ignored. Since 6de389c, integer clip ids of the active sequence already work. The reporter's cases all fail for other reasons, and the message hid which one:

- a clip id of **another sequence**, e.g. taken from `sequence.inspect {"item": …}` or after importing a timeline;
- an id that is **no clip at all**: `sequence.inspect` returns track `id`s, project `item`s and `link`s next to each item's `clip`;

`Session::enabled_for` changes only the error text. It does not change whether a command is enabled. When the selection check fails and the caller named clips under a key the command documents, but none of them is a clip of the active sequence, the reason names the first one:

- `clip 29 is in sequence "Demo", not the active one: open it first with sequence.open {"item":21}`
- `no clip 5 in the active sequence (clip ids are the `clip` numbers of the items in sequence.inspect)`
- `"29" is not a clip id (clip ids are the `clip` numbers of the items in sequence.inspect)`

Such calls are still refused. A call that names nothing (menus, shortcuts, `{}` or `"clips": []`) keeps the selection's own reason, and no open sequence still reports `no sequence is open`.

title: #456: Select All in the Project panel takes only the shown bin
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes point 3 of #456 (Part of #456; points 1, 2 and 4 are not covered here).

## Problem
With the Project panel focused, Cmd+A / Ctrl+A was rewritten to `project.selectAll`, and that selected every key of `project.items`. Items in closed bins, and items outside the bin tab being shown, ended up selected too.

## Fix
- `project.selectAll` takes two optional params, `{"bin":binId?,"expanded":[binId]?}`, listed in its params so CLI/MCP can see them.
  - `bin`: select only that bin's direct (listed) items.
  - `expanded`: sub-bins twirled open in List view. Their items are on screen, so they count, the way Premiere's List view behaves. A bin only counts if every bin above it is open as well. The walk is iterative, so deeply nested bins from a hostile project can't overflow the stack.
  - An unknown, negative or non-numeric `bin`, or an `expanded` that isn't a list of ids, returns an error and leaves the selection alone. Without `bin` (or with `bin: null`), the command selects the whole project as before.
- The UI's Select All in the Project panel now passes the shown instance's bin (the main panel's bin or the active tab's) and, in List view only, the open bins. While a search filters the panel, it selects exactly the rows shown (`project.select`), so hidden rows are never selected.

title: #412: select a single keyframe in Effect Controls
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes point 4 of #412 (Part of #412).

## Problem
In Effect Controls, the keyframe lane highlighted a keyframe when its time equalled the playhead (`k.time == mt`). Clicking a keyframe moves the playhead to it, so every parameter's keyframe at that frame lit up, not just the one clicked.

## Fix
- New serde UI state `UiState::keyframe_selection: Vec<KeyframeRef>` (clip, effect index, param, optional mask, media time). The engine has no keyframe-selection concept, so it lives with the other panel state; a `Vec` leaves room for marquee/modifier selection later (points 1–2, not implemented here).
- A click (or drag start) on a lane keyframe selects exactly that keyframe and still moves the playhead as before; the highlight reads the selection instead of the playhead.
- A dragged keyframe stays selected at its new time. References to keyframes that no longer exist (deleted, undone) or to clips no longer shown are dropped each frame via bounds-checked lookups, no panics.
- Agent-drivable: readable via `ui.inspect` → `ui.keyframe_selection`, settable via `ui.set {"keyframeSelection": [...]}` (documented in `docs/control-protocol.md`).
- Works for mask parameter rows too (they share `param_row`).

title: #642: open Help/About links in the system browser on the desktop
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #642.

## Problem
Every link in the app (Help menu incl. "Report an Issue…", About dialog, header Discord button, Import screen, Settings and Keyboard help) goes through `links::open` → `egui::Context::open_url`. The workspace builds eframe with `default-features = false` and the desktop app does not enable eframe's `links` feature, so egui-winit only logs `Cannot open url - feature links not enabled`. Nothing opens, on Linux, Windows or macOS alike.

## Fix
Same approach as PhotoCraft: a host hook instead of relying on egui's `links` feature.
- `HostHooks::open_url: Option<Box<dyn FnMut(&str) -> Result<(), String>>>` (next to `open_path`).
- `links::open(app, ctx, url)` calls the hook; when it is unset or returns an error it logs and falls back to `ctx.open_url`, so the web build keeps opening a new tab.
- The desktop app sets the hook to `open::that_detached` ([`open`](https://crates.io/crates/open) 5, MIT; pulls in `is-wsl` / `is-docker`, both MIT). The detached variant never blocks the UI thread, even when a launcher waits for the browser to exit.
- The dependency lives only in `apps/filmcraft` (L5), so layering is unchanged and nothing below L5 gains a dependency.

## Tests
`links::tests::links_open_through_the_host_hook`: every Help-menu link command reaches the hook with its URL, `links::open` does too, and a failing hook falls back to `ctx.open_url`.

## Gates
