title: Trim MP3 encoder delay when decoding audio files (#1137)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1137.

`AudioFileSource::decode` probed audio files with `FormatOptions::default()`. In symphonia 0.5 `enable_gapless` is off by default, so the MP3 reader ignored the LAME/Xing tag and never set `trim_start`/`trim_end` on packets. Every tagged MP3 kept 1105 extra samples (576 encoder delay + 529 decoder delay) at the start and played about 25 ms late.

The probe now uses `FormatOptions { enable_gapless: true, ..FormatOptions::default() }`, the same setting SoundCraft uses in `crates/audio-io/src/symph.rs`.

This is the only symphonia probe in the codebase. The audio of video imports goes through FilmCraft's own MP4/MKV demuxers and is decoded packet by packet, so this flag does not apply there.

As the issue says, MP3 clips in existing projects will start about 25 ms earlier after this change. That may be worth a release note.

Test: `gapless_tests::mp3_encoder_delay_is_trimmed` builds a small silent mono 44.1 kHz MP3 in memory. It has an Info frame with a LAME tag (encoder delay 576, no padding, valid tag CRC) and ten audio frames. The test checks that decoding gives `10 * 1152 - 1105` samples. Without the fix it gives the full `10 * 1152`.

title: Hot-text number fields select the whole value when clicked (#1126)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1126.

Clicking a blue hot-text value (position, scale, rotation, opacity and the other parameters in Effect Controls and Properties, plus Lumetri, Essential Graphics and the mixer, which use the same widget) opened the edit field with only a caret, so you had to clear the old number before typing. Now the whole value is selected once the field has focus, so typing replaces it, as in Premiere.

`hot_number` in `crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs` now does what `timecode_field` already does: the click sets a select-all flag, the edit field gets a fixed id, and once the field has focus its whole text is selected. egui drops a selection made before the field has focus, so the selection waits until then. The repaint is requested only while the field is waiting for focus and on the frame the selection is made, as in `timecode_field`, so an open field does not repaint all the time.

Test: `widgets::tests::clicking_a_hot_number_selects_its_whole_value` clicks a hot number showing `123.5` and checks that the edit field's selection covers all 5 characters. Without the fix it fails, because the field has no selection.

title: Timeline: dragging a clip above the top track or below the last one adds a new track (#1104)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1104.

Dragging clips inside the timeline into the empty space above the top video track (or below the last audio track) did nothing, while dropping media from the Project panel there already created a new track (#483). Now the clip move does the same, like Premiere.

**What changed**
- `timeline.move` accepts `"track":"new"` on a move. One track is added after the last track of each kind the `"new"` clips come from (video and/or audio), the clips move onto it, and adding the track plus the move is one undo step. If the move fails, the new track is removed again. This follows `place_on_new_tracks` (#483): same `add_tracks` call and the same undo merge and rollback.
- Timeline UI: while dragging clips from a single track past the last track of the same kind, the pointer hits the same `new_track_at` band that the media drop uses. The band shows an outline where the clips will land, and on release the moves are sent with `"track":"new"`. Drags of clips from several tracks keep the old behaviour.
- The `timeline.move` params help text lists `"new"`.

**Test**
`move_to_new_track_adds_it_in_one_undo_step` (engine): a clip moved with `"track":"new"` ends up alone on a new top video track, in one undo step; undo restores the sequence exactly; a failing move leaves no track and no undo entry behind. Without the fix, `"new"` is not a track id, so the move returns an error and the test fails.

title: Release workflow: pass the Azure signing secrets
author: echelon
body:
Since this repo's `release.yml` moved to `storytold/craft-common-actions`, it has passed the Apple and `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE*` secrets to the shared workflow, but not the six `AZURE_*` secrets that Azure Trusted Signing uses.

The shared workflow's signing jobs run in this repo's `release` environment and read the values from there, but only for names the caller lists. So the next release would have built **unsigned** Windows MSIs and portable zips, with only a warning. craft-launcher 0.3.1 did exactly this, and storytold/craft-launcher#174 fixed it with this same change.

This adds the six names. All twelve secrets are already set in this repo's `release` environment. storytold/craft-common-actions#3 makes release builds fail outright if signing secrets are missing, and fixes the riscv64 `--formats` call. This PR should land first.

`actionlint` passes.

title: Gate the control server behind a per-run token (#163)
author: bfenty
body:
# Gate the control server behind a per-run token (#163)

Second half of #163. The bind address is already loopback-only and #119 closed the
HTTP-smuggling hole, but any local process (or a web page smuggling a line through a
browser) that reaches the port can still run engine/UI commands. This adds the
authentication the issue asks for.

## How it works

- At startup the app creates a `Token`: `FILMCRAFT_CONTROL_TOKEN` if set, otherwise 16
  random bytes from `getrandom` (32 hex chars). If the OS RNG fails the server refuses
  requests rather than inventing a weak token.
- The token is written to `control.token` in the app's data directory, mode 0600, so the
  CLI bridge can find it (same directory the logs/autosaves already live in).
- Every connection must open with `{"token": "…"}` before any request runs. The compare is
  constant-time. A missing or wrong token gets one error reply naming the problem (never
  echoing the expected token) and the connection closes. Blank lines before the token are
  tolerated; everything else that isn't the token line is rejected like any non-request,
  so the #119 HTTP probe still dies on the first line.
- `BridgeClient` (CLI + MCP bridge) resolves the token from the env var or the file and
  performs the handshake on connect; a rejected token is a clear error telling the user to
  set `FILMCRAFT_CONTROL_TOKEN`.
- Docs updated: `control-protocol.md` ("The port has no authentication" is gone) and the
  `agents.md` minimal client now shows the handshake.

## Tests

`control_server.rs`: new gated tests — request without token runs nothing; wrong token runs
nothing and the reply doesn't echo the expected token; right token then requests run in
order; the #119 HTTP probe is rejected as a non-token line; env-value precedence/trimming;
generated tokens are 32 hex chars and differ per run. Existing ungated tests unchanged
(`serve_lines` is now a thin wrapper, so the #119 coverage still exercises the same parser).

`bridge.rs`: `fake_app`…

title: feat(codecs): scale decoded-frame GOP budget with host physical RAM
author: AnarchByte0
body:
### Summary
This PR automatically scales the process-wide decoded frame budget for GOP caching based on total available system physical RAM.

- Adds \set_frame_budget\ and \ctive_frame_budget\ helpers in \crates/codecs\ to allow dynamically sizing cache memory limits.
- Detects host memory at initialization via \GlobalMemoryStatusEx\ on Windows and \/proc/meminfo\ on Linux in \crates/platform\.
- Scales GOP budget from default 1.0 GiB up to 2.5 GiB (for 32 GiB systems) and 5.0 GiB (for 64+ GiB systems), significantly improving playback and scrubbing performance on high-framerate (120/144 fps) timelines.
- Cleanly scoped without unrelated dependencies.

title: feat(av1enc): clean-room pure-Rust baseline AV1 software encoder
author: AnarchByte0
body:
### Summary
This PR introduces \crates/av1enc\, a clean-room pure-Rust baseline AV1 software encoder conforming to the AOMedia AV1 Specification v1.0.0.

### Highlights
- **Inter-Frame Prediction (P-Frames) & Zero-Motion Skip**: P-frame coding with zero-motion inter skip checks against reference frames, reducing file size by 7–10x compared to pure intra keyframe encoding.
- **In-Loop CDEF Filter**: Complete in-loop Constrained Directional Enhancement Filter (CDEF) with directional search, primary/secondary damping, and configurable filter strengths to eliminate block artifacts.
- **Dynamic Scene Cut Detection**: Automatic scene transition detector based on mean absolute frame difference thresholds; automatically places I-frames on timeline cuts.
- **I/P-Frame QP Offset**: Dynamic quantization offset between intra and inter frames, preserving high fidelity on keyframe anchors while efficiently compressing temporal residuals.
- **Vectorized Math (Chunked SIMD SAD)**: Auto-vectorized 16-byte chunk calculations (\s_chunks::<16>()\) lowering into native SIMD vector instructions under Safe Rust (\unsafe_code = 'forbid'\).
- **Parallel Row Analysis via Rayon**: Superblock row analysis runs in parallel across all CPU cores before serial arithmetic entropy bitstream packing.
- **Intra Prediction**: DC, Vertical, Horizontal, Smooth, and Paeth prediction modes with flat-block early termination.
- **Rate Control**: Constant Quality (CRF), direct Qindex, and adaptive 1-pass CBR / VBR with bit-reservoir tracking.
- **Safety**: Fully safe pure-Rust implementation adhering strictly to FilmCraft's zero-panic standard (\Result<T, E>\).

### Validation & Benchmarks
- \cargo test -p filmcraft-av1enc\: all unit tests + full MP4 mux and decode round-trip pass.
- Benchmark suite (\	ests/benchmarks.rs\): real-world encoding benchmarks across 720p, 1080p, and 4K.
- \cargo clippy -p filmcraft-av1enc --all-targets -- -D warnings\: passes cleanly (0 warnings).
- \cargo fmt --check\: clean.

title: #1124: ⌘D / ⇧⌘D apply transitions to the selected clips or edit points
author: n-delic
body:
Fixes #1124.

## What changes

Apply Video Transition (⌘D / Ctrl+D) and Apply Audio Transition (⇧⌘D) worked only at an edit point under the playhead. As in Premiere:

title: Trim MP3 encoder delay so imports play in time (#1137)
author: bfenty
body:
## Problem (#1137)

MP3 imports play ~25 ms late: LAME records its encoder delay/padding in the LAME tag, and symphonia only trims those samples when `enable_gapless` is on. `AudioFileSource::decode` used `FormatOptions::default()`, so every decoded MP3 carried ~576 leading samples of silence and every click landed late against a ffmpeg-decoded reference.

## Fix

One behavior change in `crates/codecs/src/audio.rs`: set `enable_gapless = true` on the probe options. Symphonia then trims the recorded delay/padding, matching ffmpeg default behavior.

## Test

New `crates/codecs/tests/mp3_gapless.rs`: builds a 4 s WAV with single-sample clicks at exactly 1.000/2.000/3.000 s, encodes it with LAME (cached fixture, same pattern as the other oracle tests), decodes through the public `MediaSource::audio` API, and asserts each click lands within 2 samples of ffmpeg's own decode. Red on main (click at 44100 decoded at 45205 — the 1105-sample encoder delay), green with the fix.

Note: `opus_mkv_mono_speechlike_16k` fails identically on unmodified main (verified via stash), so it is unrelated to this change.

title: clips: Maintain Audio Pitch for sped-up clips (follows #1146 / #959)
author: wzachmorris
body:
Closes nothing on its own; follows up #959 / #1146 with the per-clip half.

#1146 keeps the pitch while **shuttling**. This adds the same for a **clip** whose speed was changed: Clip ▸ Speed/Duration gains **Maintain Audio Pitch** (`clip.speedDuration {maintainPitch}`, on by default), so a voice at 115 % stays a voice, in playback and export alike.

**What this does**

- `filmcraft-audio-dsp` gains `stretch::Stretcher`, a pull-based WSOLA time stretch (24 ms Hann grains, half-hop overlap, ±9 ms waveform-similarity search). Tempo changes, pitch stays; speeds clamp to 1/64..64 and 0 / NaN / ∞ fall back to identity. (Separate from #1146's phase-vocoder shift: this stretches a single clip's source on demand inside the mixer, where the pitch shifter would need a second resampling pass per clip.)
- `TrackItem::maintain_pitch` (serde default, old projects load unchanged); the Speed/Duration dialog checkbox; `sequence.inspect` reports it; i18n rows for es and zh-cn.
- **Where the stream state lives** (the flagged design point, reworked after review): the mixer is stateless per block and renders tracks in parallel, but a time stretch carries its grain chain between blocks. There is no process-wide static now. `render::audio::StretchPool` is owned by the reader's `LiveMix`, the object playback already passes into `mix_graph`; it keeps one stream per clip with the position it continues from. A block starting there takes the stream, whichever rayon thread mixes the track, and puts it back. A seek starts a new one; two readers (playback beside an export) never share a stream. Export's `AudioOut` and the preview renderer each own a `LiveMix` now. A caller with no `LiveMix` (`mix_sequence`: analysis, waveforms, tests) gets the clip resampled as before, so nothing can observe a chopped stream.

**Tests**

- `audio-dsp`: steady level stays steady; a tone's zero-crossing rate stays put while the source is consumed at speed; hostile speeds are identity; block size does not change the …

title: Enable Linux HEVC NVENC export and stabilize audio mixing
author: turkawa
body:
## Summary

This PR enables HEVC (H.265) NVENC hardware export on 64-bit Linux and addresses intermittent export hangs observed when audio mixing and GPU rendering run concurrently.

### Changes
- Enable Linux HEVC NVENC capability detection and encoder initialization.
- Allow the HEVC NVENC encoder factory to run on Linux.
- Change audio track mixing from parallel to sequential iteration to avoid the observed export stalls.

### Testing
Tested on PikaOS Linux with an NVIDIA RTX 2060 SUPER.

- HEVC NVENC export produces valid H.265 video.
- GPU compositing enabled.
- Audio enabled.
- Three consecutive exports completed successfully after the audio mixing change.
- Export overlap remains enabled.

### Notes
The intermittent hangs appeared related to concurrent audio mixing and GPU export work. Sequential audio mixing resolved the issue in my tests, although the underlying synchronization problem has not been conclusively identified.

The audio mixing change affects all platforms, so feedback on a more targeted solution is welcome.

title: ui: add Label submenu to the Timeline marker menu (#1143)
author: bfenty
body:
Right-clicking a marker on the Timeline ruler offered only "Clear Selected Marker" / "Clear Markers" — there was no way to change a marker's colour from the Timeline. The clip menu's `edit.label` targets clips, not markers, so it silently did nothing for markers (as noted in the issue).

The marker menu now carries a **Label** submenu listing the 16 label colours (current one ticked), which edits the right-clicked marker through `markers.edit` — the only command that changes a marker's colour. The right-click already parks the playhead on the marker (`timeline.rs`, marker-menu open path), which is how the menu identifies its target.

Adds a headless kittest regression (`crates/ui-egui/tests/marker_menu_ui.rs`): open demo project → add a range marker → right-click its pentagon → open Label → pick a colour → assert the marker's colour changed.

Tested: `cargo test -p filmcraft-ui-egui --test marker_menu_ui --test edit_point_menu_ui --test panels_ui --test menus_ui` — all pass.

title: Transition edge drags keep their alignment
author: gyroninja
body:
Dragging an end of a transition used to trim only that end, which broke the alignment: a Center at Cut transition drifted off its cut and turned into Custom Start the first time it was resized, and the cut-side end of a Start or End at Cut transition could be dragged off the cut entirely. The trim cursor appeared over every end, even a pinned one where the drag did nothing.

Now an end drag resizes the transition the way its alignment says: Center at Cut keeps its midpoint on the cut (pulling the right end out also pulls the left end out the same amount), Start at Cut keeps its start on the cut and End at Cut its end, and Custom Start trims just the grabbed end. Only dragging its middle slides a transition over the cut into Custom Start. The Timeline and Effect Controls show the trim cursor only on ends that can actually move, so a pinned end no longer looks like a handle.

title: Captions: preserve fractional TTML tick offsets
author: webdevtodayjason
body:
TTML and DFXP imports dropped the fractional part of tick offsets. With `ttp:tickRate="10"`, `begin="1.5t"` placed the caption at 0.1 seconds instead of 0.15 seconds. TTML allows a fraction on every offset metric (`time-count fraction? metric`), including `t`.

The tick branch now converts the whole decimal value before dividing by the tick rate, the same way the h, m, s and ms branches already do. Malformed or overflowing fractions are rejected instead of being read as the integer part. The default tick rate (1, or frameRate times subFrameRate when a frame rate is given) is unchanged.

The first commit adds my entry to `contributors/people.toml`.

How it was tested:

- The new regression test fails on current main (`Tick(25401600000)` instead of `Tick(38102400000)`) and passes with the fix. It covers TTML and DFXP import at tickRate 10, a 3 Hz tick rate, and malformed or overflowing fractional offsets.
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-captions`: 64 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask assets` and `cargo xtask wasm`: pass.
- `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`: nine tests that need a GPU or the optional Japanese craft font could not run here and fail the same way on current main without them; everything else passes.

title: Help menu: say where each item goes; keep the address when no browser opens
author: liangforstudy
body:
From the Help menu you couldn't tell which items open the web browser, which address they go to, or what happens otherwise.

- Hovering a link item (Join the ArtCraft Discord, ArtCraft Website, FilmCraft on getartcraft.com, FilmCraft on GitHub, Report an Issue, FilmCraft Help) shows **"Opens in your web browser: <address>"**, the same hint the About dialog's link buttons already give.
- The other Help items say what they do instead: Reveal Log Files "Saves this session's log and shows it in your file manager.", System Compatibility Report "Shows a report on this computer.", About FilmCraft "Shows the version, community links and credits in a FilmCraft window."
- When the host can't open a browser, the click used to be only logged (the native `ctx.open_url` fallback is a no-op, #642). Now a **"Couldn't open your web browser"** dialog shows the reason and the address in a read-only field you can select from, with a Copy button. It stays until Close or Escape, so the address is still there after switching to another window. A status-bar message would clear itself after 8 seconds, and a copy to the clipboard can fail silently (egui only logs it), so neither keeps the address on its own.

The dialog's state is `ui.failedLink` (`{url, error}`, serde like the rest of `UiState`); automation ids `failedLink.url`, `failedLink.copy`, `failedLink.close`. New strings have Spanish, Simplified Chinese and Japanese translations (required by the i18n tests).

**Tests:**
- `links::tests::help_menu_items_say_where_they_go`: every Help menu item has a hint; links name their address and say "web browser", the other items don't.
- `links_open_through_the_host_hook`: a failing opener now leaves the address and the reason in `ui.failedLink`.
- `links::tests::failed_link_dialog_keeps_the_address_until_closed`: the dialog shows the address, Copy copies it, idle frames don't close it, Close does.

**Checked** (Windows 11): `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-ui-egui --all-targets …

title: ui: paused, a playhead jump outside the view scrolls the Timeline to it (#1188)
author: bfenty
body:
Home / End moved the playhead but not the Timeline view, so while paused the playhead jumped off-screen (the auto-scroll block only ran `if app.playback.playing`).

**Fix:** when paused and no drag is running, a playhead that *moved* to a position outside the visible window moves the view to it (instant jump, same style as the playing-follow block). A playhead that did not move never moves the view, so a scroll the user set stays put; paused scrubbing is excluded via the existing drag guard. Because Home/End, next/prev-edit, timecode entry, and scripted `playhead.set` all funnel through the same state change, they all get the behavior for free.

**Tests** (`crates/ui-egui/tests/playhead_scroll_ui.rs`, headless kittest):
- End → view follows, playhead lands at the right edge (or the scroll limit); Home → both back at the head
- frame-stepping past the right edge keeps the playhead visible
- a still playhead leaves the user's manual scroll alone

Negative control: all three tests fail without the patch block (e.g. "the playhead stayed in view: 1095.7 px of 729.7").

Note for maintainers: the paused block intentionally ignores the `follow` / `auto_scroll` prefs (Premiere's Home/End always jump the view too). Easy to gate on `follow` if you'd rather.

title: i18n(es): fix mistranslations and terms, add 4 missing rows
author: diegozpy
body:
Review of the Spanish interface catalog (`crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/es.tsv`): 4 rows added, 38 changed. Only that file changes.

**Missing (4)**
*Settings*, *Hide Others*, *Hide FilmCraft* (the macOS app menu) and the hardware-decoding explanation in Preferences had no Spanish row; other catalogs have them.

**Mistranslations**
- *Scratch Disks* said «discos de memoria virtual» (virtual memory); they are «discos de trabajo» (three rows).
- *Create Sidecar File* said «archivo adjunto» (attachment); it is «archivo complementario».
- *Metadata & Timecode Burn-in* said «Impresión» (printing); it is «Incrustación».
- *Legal Range Squeeze* said «rango de vídeo»; it is «rango legal» (and the header writes *video* without an accent).
- *Grab bag* said «Mosaico»; it is «Miscelánea».
- *Show/Join Through Edits* said «ediciones pasantes»; they are «cortes continuos».
- *Trim Backward/Forward Many* said «Recortar muchos…»; they trim several frames («Recortar varios fotogramas…»). *Trim Edit* is a mode, «Edición de recorte», like *Roll Edit*.
- *Nudge Selected Object … by one/five* lost the unit («…cinco hacia abajo»); the nudge moves the position by pixels, so «cinco píxeles», «un píxel» (eight rows).
- *Butt cap* said «Extremo cuadrado» (a square cap); it is «Extremo plano». *Camera Shake* said «Movimiento de cámara» (camera movement); it is «Vibración de cámara». *British Stack* (an amp) said «Pila británica».

**Consistency**
- *Render* is «procesar» everywhere, as the header says; three GPU/software rendering rows said «renderizar».
- *View Preset* uses «ajuste preestablecido» like every other preset; *More transport controls* matches *Show Transport Controls*; *Match Playhead* reads «Igualar al cabezal»; *Focus* is «Enfoque», like *Focus Point*.
- Grammar: the count messages put the participle after the noun («{n} grupo(s) de clips sincronizado(s)»), the missing-media message agrees with `clip(s)`, and «Estilo de blanqueo omitido» gets its «de».

title: Export: 32-bit integer and 32-bit float audio
author: JordyUSA
body:
## Summary

Adds 32-bit integer and 32-bit float PCM audio export. The Sample Size selector now lists 16 bit, 24 bit, 32 bit and 32 bit float the same way Audio Format does: every option is shown, and the ones the chosen codec/container can't store are greyed out with the reason on hover.

## What each format supports

| Format | 16 | 24 | 32 | 32 float |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| WAV | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ (`WAVE_FORMAT_IEEE_FLOAT`, EXTENSIBLE above 2 channels, with `fact` chunk) |
| AIFF | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ (AIFF-C `fl32`) |
| QuickTime PCM (ProRes, DNxHR, …) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ (`lpcm` with the float flag) |
| MXF | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | greyed out |
| FLAC (`.flac`, MOV, MP4) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | greyed out |
| MP4 (AAC) | no change | | | |

## Changes

- **Engine:** `AudioSettings` gains `float`; `bits` accepts 16, 24 or 32. A new `SampleFormat` (Int16 / Int24 / Int32 / Float32) and `ExportSettings::supports_sample_format` decide what each codec and container can store. `validate` refuses float without 32 bits, and float in FLAC or MXF.
- **Float keeps the mix unclipped:** peaks above 0 dBFS survive in 32-bit float. 16 and 24-bit output is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- **FLAC encoder:** now takes 8–32 bits. At 32 bits, stereo is coded as independent channels (a side channel would need 33 bits), and the sample-range check no longer overflows.
- **UI (Export mode):** Sample Size shows all four sizes, greys out the unsupported ones and explains why on hover. A size that stops being available (for example, float after switching Audio Format to FLAC) falls back to 32-bit integer. Strings are added for es, fr, pt-br, id, ja and zh-cn.
- **CLI / control channel / presets:** accept `"audio": {"bits": 32, "float": true}`. Unsupported combinations are rejected with an error message.

## Design note: FLAC 32-bit header

32-bit FLAC frames point back to STREAMINFO for their bit depth instead of using RFC 9639's dedicated 32-bit code. symphonia 0.5 (FilmCraft's own FLAC import) rejects that code as reserved, s…

title: Linux: VA-API H.264 export encoding (AMD / Intel), on main's `vaapi` module (#30)
author: LloydNicholson
body:
## Summary

On Linux, Export ▸ Hardware encoding now uses the GPU's media engine through **VA-API** for H.264 on AMD, Intel and other Mesa / vendor drivers that expose an H.264 `EncSlice` entrypoint, or `EncSliceLP` (the low-power encoder Intel's iHD driver offers on Iris Xe, UHD 620 and others; 567febde by @ZpdyGonzales, tested on both). Until now the only Linux hardware encoder was NVENC, so AMD and Intel machines always encoded on the CPU.

This is the "VA-API encode" part of #408, split out and ported onto main's existing `crates/platform/src/vaapi/` module as @echelon asked in https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/pull/408#issuecomment-6114599196. There's no second FFI layer and no new dependency: it uses the same runtime-loaded libva table and the decoders' shared display. The encoder logic is @mutombopr's (credited as co-author on the commits that port it). I asked on #408 before opening this (https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/pull/408#issuecomment-6118390434); if @mutombopr would rather resubmit it themselves, I'm happy to close this in favour of theirs.

- `vaapi/va.rs`: `encode_caps(profile)` (rate-control modes and max picture size via `vaGetConfigAttributes` on `EncSlice`; no new libva symbol), and `EncodeSession` (config, context, input + 2 reconstructed surfaces, coded buffer, a cached NV12 upload image).

title: GPU export: 4:2:0 frames straight from the GPU (colour conversion on the GPU) (#30)
author: LloydNicholson
body:
## Summary

With GPU Rendering on, export frames are composited on the GPU and then read back as **linear float RGBA** (8 bytes a pixel). On the CPU they're converted to 8-bit sRGB (`Image::over_black_rgba8`) and then to 4:2:0 (`rgba_to_yuv420_8`). In a 4K export with hardware encoding those two conversions were ~75 % of the remaining CPU time.

This PR adds a GPU path that produces the encoder's input directly:

- **`crates/gpu/src/yuv.wgsl` / `yuv.rs`:** a compute pass converts the Rgba16Float accumulator to 8-bit BT.709 limited 4:2:0. It uses the **same 4096-entry table and index** as `linear_to_srgb_u8` and the **same formulas, accumulation order and rounding** as `rgba_to_yuv420_8`. Only the planes are read back (1.5 bytes a pixel). Each invocation owns whole output words (8×2 pixels), so there are no write races. The pipeline is built in a validation error scope, so a device that rejects it converts on the CPU instead of retiring GPU export rendering.
- **`GpuCompositor::render_export_yuv420` / `ExportRenderer::render_yuv420`** return a `filmcraft_frame::VideoFrame` (`Yuv8`, `C420`, BT.709 limited).
- **`filmcraft-export`** (all additive, default off):
  - `FrameRenderer::render_yuv420` (default `None`).
  - `VideoEncoder::takes_yuv420` / `encode_yuv420` (default `false` / `Unsupported`).
  - The built-in H.264 encoder takes the planes through `filmcraft_h264enc::YuvFrame`.
  - `Pipeline::yuv_eligible` / `frame_yuv`, and a `Frame` enum in the job.
- **Eligibility:** the path is used only when nothing after compositing would change the picture: no letterbox, pillarbox or resample into the frame size, no image, name or timecode overlay, video limiter off, not HDR, no alpha, and an encoder that takes 4:2:0. A size change the render scale makes on its own (e.g. half size) is fine. Any frame the renderer declines (a transition, a CPU-planned frame, a failed read-back) takes the RGBA path as before, so a stream can mix both.
- **Memory:** frames count as RGBA in the…

body:

title: codecs: start an edited MP4 at its first presented picture (#1276)
author: bfenty
body:
## Problem

An MP4 whose video edit list starts with an empty edit (a start offset — e.g. `-output_ts_offset 0.0533`) rendered every picture one frame early. At sequence time 2.1042 s in a 24 fps Sequence From Clip, Filmcraft showed frame 49 where ffprobe presents frame 50.

## Root cause

`rebase_unedited_video` (#714) shifts a file so its first presented picture lands at time zero, but only ran when the video track had **no** edit list. With a leading empty edit, the first presentation is `min pts + edit_offset` > 0 all the same — the video lookup in `video_at` just never applied that start, so sequence time 0 mapped to file time 0 and every frame landed ~53 ms early.

## Fix

Lift the edit-list gate on the #714 rebase: any video track whose first presentation is after zero rebases, video and audio together, by the earliest start among them (unchanged mechanics). An edit that skips into the media yields a non-positive start and still does nothing; edit-list cuts are untouched.

## Test (red → green)

`crates/codecs/tests/empty_edit_offset.rs` uses the issue's exact ffmpeg generator — `testsrc` prints each frame's own generation time, so the rendered picture identifies itself — and asserts the picture at sequence 2.1042 s is the frame ffprobe presents there (compared against ffmpeg's own decode).

- **Red** on `main`: `must be ffmpeg's presented frame 50, got frame Some(49)`
- **Green** with the patch
- Negative control: reverting the patch makes it red again
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-codecs --lib`: 98 passed (the one failure, `opus_mkv_mono_speechlike_16k`, fails identically on `main`)
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean

Closes #1276

title: fix(ui): open the context menu on macOS Ctrl+Click
author: gyroninja
body:
On macOS, AppKit delivers Ctrl+Click to the winit view as a primary mouse press carrying the Control modifier — rightMouseDown only fires for a real right button or a two-finger trackpad click. winit 0.30 (button 0 → Left) and egui-winit 0.36 (Left → PointerButton::Primary) pass it through untouched, so egui's secondary_clicked() never fires and no context menu opens.

Context menus subscribe to egui's secondary click, so the translation is done once at the input boundary, as the platform convention requires: winit deliberately leaves Ctrl+Click handling to the application (rust-windowing/winit#4469, wontfix), and macOS apps translate it themselves (Firefox does the same in nsCocoaWindow.mm).

raw_input_hook runs before egui begins its pass, when pointer click state is computed — the only seam where a rewritten event has the right effect. Primary presses carrying the Control modifier become Secondary presses; the press and its release are paired so releasing Control mid-click still closes as a context click and never leaks a stray primary click, and a plain press or PointerGone clears any stale pairing. Real right clicks and other buttons pass through unchanged; Windows and Linux keep Ctrl+Click as a selection modifier, and control-channel/automation input is exempt.

Unit tests cover the transformation through egui's real pointer state: a rewritten Ctrl+Click makes pointer.secondary_clicked() true, plain clicks are untouched, and a stale pairing cannot corrupt the next click.

title: fix(media): drop .y4m and .ale from the import lists (#1292)
author: mroxso
body:
## What
Fixes #1292.

Two extensions were offered for import but could never be imported:

- `.y4m` was in `VIDEO_EXTENSIONS` (`crates/media/src/lib.rs`), but no opener reads YUV4MPEG2 — the only `y4m` references in the tree were as a vpxenc intermediate in codecs tests.
- `.ale` was in `PROJECT_EXTENSIONS` (`crates/engine/src/media_browser.rs`), but FilmCraft only writes ALE (`file.exportAle`); nothing reads it back (the `interchange::ale` parser is used by the export round-trip tests only).

Both failed at import with `unsupported media: …: unrecognised format`.

Following the issue's fallback option ("drop them from the lists so users aren't offered files that always fail"), this removes them from the lists. File ▸ Import, the Media Browser filter and `mediaBrowser.extensions()` all derive from these lists, so the fix applies everywhere at once. ALE **export** is untouched.

If/when a Y4M reader or an ALE importer lands, the extensions can be added back.

## Test
New regression test `media_browser_tests::unopenable_formats_are_not_offered`: `.y4m`/`.ale` get no kind, are absent from the extension list and `is_importable`, while `.mov`/`.edl` stay listed. All 11 media-browser tests pass; `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy` clean on the touched crates.

title: codecs: import raw ADTS .aac files (#1291)
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Fixes #1291.

Raw ADTS `.aac` files are offered by File ▸ Import and the Media Browser, and Export ▸ AAC Audio writes them (#814), but importing one always failed with `unrecognised format`: `audio::opener` only accepted `mp3 | mp2 | flac | ogg | oga | aif | aiff | aifc`.

**Change** (`crates/codecs/src/audio.rs`)
- `aac` is accepted by the standalone-audio opener, and `AudioFileSource` decodes an ADTS stream with our AAC decoder (ISO/IEC 13818-7 §6.2). It reads frame after frame from the first header (after an ID3v2 tag) and resyncs past damaged bytes. Frames with a different configuration from the first are skipped, and a frame that fails to decode keeps its duration as silence. HE-AAC is upsampled to its output rate via the existing `aac_output_rate`, and the existing `adts_split` / `PacketDecoder::aac` do the decoding.
- Standalone audio is decoded into memory, so the ADTS path stops with an actionable error ("remux it to .m4a") past 2³⁰ samples (4 GiB, ~3 h of 48 kHz stereo) instead of allocating without bound.
- The ID3v2 skip from the `.mp2` path is now a shared `id3v2_len` helper (no behaviour change).

**Tested** (Fedora 44, KDE Plasma, RX 9060 XT)
- New `crates/codecs/tests/adts_file.rs`: a stereo tone encoded by our own AAC encoder with ADTS output imports with the right rate, channels, duration and level. It failed before the change with `unrecognised format`. Also truncated, bit-flipped, zero-length and over-long frames, run under `catch_unwind`.
- By hand with `filmcraft-cli`: an ffmpeg-made ADTS file probes as AAC/ADTS 48 kHz, and a `.aac` exported by FilmCraft itself now imports (`"errors":[]`).
- Gates: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask assets` pass. `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`: 3257 passed, 0 failed. The `filmcraft-gpu` lib test binary segfaulted inside the RADV Vulkan driver (Mesa 26.3-devel), as it intermittently does on unmodified `main` on this machine. I…

title: Import YUV4MPEG2 (.y4m) video; stop offering .ale for import (#1292)
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Fixes #1292.

Two file types were offered for import but could never be imported.

**`.y4m`: now read** (`crates/codecs/src/y4m.rs`)
- `y4m` was in `VIDEO_EXTENSIONS`, and `docs/file-format-parity.md` already lists Y4M as read, but no opener existed. `Y4mSource` is written from the format's public documentation (the `yuv4mpeg(5)` manual page):
  - The `W` / `H` / `F` / `A` / `I` / `C` / `X` stream header, and `FRAME` lines carrying their own parameters.
  - Formats: 8-bit 4:2:0 (`420jpeg` / `420paldv` / `420mpeg2`), 4:2:2, 4:4:4, `444alpha` and `mono` as `Yuv8`; 9–16-bit little-endian (`420p10`, `422p12`, `mono16`, …) as `Yuv16`.
  - `XCOLORRANGE=FULL` and the pixel aspect ratio are read.
- Frames are indexed once from their header lines and read on demand. It's registered as both an opener and a reader opener, so a multi-gigabyte file isn't loaded whole.
- Sizes, rates and offsets are checked, and frames are capped at 2²⁸ pixels. 4:1:1 and unknown colour spaces give an "unsupported" error.

**`.ale`: no longer offered** (`crates/engine/src/media_browser.rs`)
- The Media Browser listed `.ale` among project files, but FilmCraft only writes ALE (File ▸ Export ▸ Avid Log Exchange). Premiere doesn't import it either, and the parity doc lists it as write-only. So importing one from the browser always failed. It's now left out of `PROJECT_EXTENSIONS`. I went with this rather than adding an ALE importer because the parity doc lists ALE as write-only; happy to switch if you'd rather import ALE as clips.

**Tested** (Fedora 44, KDE Plasma, RX 9060 XT)
- New `crates/codecs/tests/y4m_file.rs` covers:
  - 4:2:0 frame by frame; 10-bit 4:2:2 with frame-line parameters, 4:3 pixels and full range; mono; the reader-opener path.
  - Truncated, bit-flipped and hostile headers (huge, zero or missing size, `F0:0`, `F25:0`, `C411`, unknown `C`) under `catch_unwind`.
  - An ffmpeg oracle: 8-bit 4:2:0 and 10-bit 4:2:2 files from `-f yuv4mpegpipe` (with ffmpeg's `XYSCSS` extension) equal ff…

title: media: decode uncompressed and PackBits YCbCr TIFF stills (#1293)
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Fixes #1293.

TIFFs stored as YCbCr (PhotometricInterpretation 6) without JPEG compression failed with `does not support the color type Unknown(24)`, because the image crate reads YCbCr only inside JPEG compression. ffmpeg writes these whenever the source is YUV, so an ordinary frame grab (`ffmpeg -i clip.mp4 -frames:v 1 grab.tiff`) or an ffmpeg-made TIFF sequence couldn't be imported.

**Change** (`crates/media/src/still/ycbcr_tiff.rs`, called from `still::decode_raster`)
- Decodes uncompressed and PackBits YCbCr TIFFs from TIFF 6.0 (§21 YCbCr images, §20 ReferenceBlackWhite, §9 PackBits), reading the directory with filmcraft-dng's TIFF parser:
  - 8-bit chunky data units with subsampling 1, 2 or 4 each way; the image is padded to whole data units, and the padding is dropped.
  - Converted with the file's YCbCrCoefficients and ReferenceBlackWhite, falling back to the §21 defaults.
  - Chroma is repeated across each data unit.
- Every size, offset and count is checked, and the picture is capped at 2²⁸ pixels. Separate planes, tiles and other bit depths give an "unsupported" error.
- JPEG-compressed YCbCr TIFFs and RGB TIFFs still go to the image crate, unchanged.

**Tested** (Fedora 44, KDE Plasma, RX 9060 XT)
- New `crates/media/tests/tiff_ycbcr.rs`:
  - Hand-built files: data-unit placement at 4:2:0; video-range reference levels with PackBits at 4:4:4; a 3×3 image at 2×2, which isn't a whole number of data units. These failed before the change with the `Unknown(24)` error.
  - Truncated, bit-flipped and hostile files (65535×65535, zero subsampling, a PackBits run past the strip) under `catch_unwind`.
  - An ffmpeg oracle: ffmpeg-written 4:2:0, 4:2:2 and 4:4:4 TIFFs (95×63, PackBits) against ffmpeg's own RGB decode, every channel of every pixel within 6. The difference comes from chroma upsampling, nearest versus interpolated.
- Unit test for PackBits literals, runs, no-ops and output capping.
- By hand with `filmcraft-cli probe`: the TIFFs from the issue, includin…

title: codecs: MP4 frames stamped just after the frame grid show on their own frame
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1282.

The frame shown at a time is the last one starting at or before it, so when a phone stamps its frames a millisecond after the grid, a sequence frame asked at its exact start gets the picture before. The MP4 lookup already rounds the request to the track timescale (the #73 fix, as WebM does since #83), but that only covers timestamps quantised to a coarse timescale: at 90 kHz a millisecond is 90 units, so rounding the request doesn't reach the frame.

So `Mp4Source` now snaps the video sample times back onto the frame grid when opening a file, but only for a file that is a constant rate gone slightly off. The grid starts at the first picture and steps by the nominal frame duration. The file is snapped only if every picture is less than a quarter of a frame from its grid point and no two pictures share a grid point; otherwise it's treated as variable frame rate and nothing moves. A picture one unit off is left where it is, since that can't be told from timescale rounding. Only the video sample times change: the audio, the first picture and the reported duration stay the same. Happy to adjust the threshold.

The audio question at the end of the issue (does the audio stay in sync with the late picture) is not addressed here.

Validation (macOS, Apple silicon), new tests in `rounded_pts_tests.rs`:
- `mp4_with_frames_1ms_after_the_grid_shows_every_frame_once` (90 kHz, frames 1 ms late, 7 rates): fails on main (`30 fps, frames 90/90000 s late: 1 of 90 frames never shown [89]…, 1 shown twice [0]…`, same at every rate), passes here.
- `mp4_with_frames_on_the_grid_shows_every_frame_once` and `mp4_variable_rate_and_on_grid_frame_times_stay_put` (alternating 1/30 and 1/20 s, a 0.4-frame shift, a 1/5-frame stutter, two frames one and five units after the same grid point, 59.94 fps with truncated stamps): pass on main and here, frame for frame.
- Removing the quarter-frame check, the shared-grid-point check or the one-unit allowance each makes the last test fail.
- …

title: Fix Linux HEVC NVENC heap corruption and probe lifecycle
author: turkawa
body:
## Summary

Restores Linux HEVC (H.265) NVENC hardware encoding and fixes the probe lifecycle associated with intermittent CLI heap corruption.

- Re-enables Linux HEVC NVENC export and HEVC/HDR capability detection.
- Moves asynchronous HEVC probing to GUI startup, keeping background probing out of CLI initialization.
- Tracks and joins the probe thread before GUI graphics shutdown.
- Enables Linux HEVC NVENC integration tests.

## Verification

- Release GUI and CLI builds successful.
- HEVC NVENC integration tests: **4/4 passed**.
- Valgrind integration tests: **4/4 passed**.
- No invalid heap reads, writes, frees, or mismatched frees detected.
- **0 bytes definitely lost** under Valgrind.
- **20 consecutive CLI HEVC exports passed**, without crashes or hangs.
- FFprobe confirmed HEVC video and AAC audio in exported files.

Valgrind reported uninitialized-value warnings, including NVIDIA driver library warnings, but no heap-corruption errors.

## Separate known issue

GUI HEVC export with audio mixing and "Composite on GPU when available" can hang at approximately 4%. Thread backtraces were captured. This audio-mixing/export synchronization issue will be investigated separately.

title: Stop H.264 export hanging in the YUV conversion
author: vbasky
body:
Fixes #1329.

H.264 export overlaps the next batch on the global Rayon pool, and the colour conversion started another parallel iterator on that same pool. The scope thread then waited in `rgba_to_yuv420_8` while every worker slept, so the export sat at 0% CPU. Conversion now runs on the current thread when that thread is already a pool worker. The same path covers the HDR float conversion.

Refs #1283, which hangs in the same overlap.

title: fix(shortcuts): Clear and reassign also drop a command's panel copy of its key (part of #1333)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #1333.

New Bin has Cmd+B twice in FilmCraft Default: application-wide and again in the Project panel (`FILMCRAFT_PANEL`). The editor's Clear sends panel Application and a reassignment replaces keys in the current context only, so the Project panel copy of Cmd+B survived both, and with the Project panel focused Cmd+B still made a bin. A panel binding on the same key as one of the command's application keys is now treated as a copy of it: Clear in Application and replacing the application shortcut take it along. A panel key of its own, like History ▸ Left for Undo, is left alone. Same idea as the Cmd+W pair from #832, just not limited to Close.

This doesn't touch the recorder sometimes registering only "B" instead of Cmd+B; that looks like a separate cause, so I left it for its own fix.

Validation:
- `clear_new_bin_frees_cmd_b_in_the_project_panel_too`: fails on main (the Project panel keeps Cmd+B on New Bin), passes here; also checks the saved set after a reload
- `reassigning_new_bin_moves_its_project_panel_key_too`: fails on main (`[("Cmd+B", Some("Project")), ("Cmd+Alt+B", None)]`), passes here
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-engine --lib shortcuts_tests`, `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

author: marcoarnulfo

Fixes #1341.

The Program monitor drew the selected mask's outline and handles whenever a mask was selected, without looking at the clip selection, so after clicking another clip (or empty timeline) they stayed on screen. The mask overlay now draws only while the mask's clip is selected, the same rule the Motion/Transform box already follows. The mask itself stays selected, so its handles come back when you reselect the clip; happy to switch to clearing the mask selection in `timeline.select` instead if you prefer that.

Validation:
- `masks_ui::mask_handles_follow_the_clip_selection`: fails on main (`no handles with [32] selected`), passes here

title: render: Sharpen stays visible at reduced playback resolution
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1351.

Sharpen's blur radius is `px_scale.max(0.35)`, so at 1/2 playback resolution it asks `gaussian_boxes` for sigma 0.5 (0.35 at 1/4). The three-box approximation rounds anything below ~0.58 to three radius-0 boxes, the "blurred" copy equals the original, and the unsharp mask adds nothing. Paused Resolution defaults to Full, which is why the paused frame was sharpened and playback was not. The floor is now 0.6, the smallest sigma that still gives a non-empty kernel; at Full (and anything down to 0.6) the boxes are identical to before. Happy to switch to a different floor or to fix this inside `gaussian_boxes` instead, but that would also change small-radius Gaussian/Camera blurs, so I kept it to Sharpen.

Validation:
- `crates/render/tests/sharpen_preview_res.rs`: fails on main (at px_scale 0.5 the edge pixel stays 0.25), passes here; the Full-resolution case pins the values rendered before the fix
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-render --test sharpen_preview_res`, `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-render --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: perf(av1): optimize decoder allocations, zero-fill elimination and DC transforms
author: AnarchByte0
body:
### Summary
This PR optimizes the pure-Rust software AV1 decoder (\ ilmcraft-av1\):
1. **Zero-copy frame delivery**: \Slot::wait_take()\ moves the owned \Picture\ buffer instead of cloning the shared \Arc\, eliminating redundant 25+ MB buffer copies per frame at 4K.
2. **Buffer recycling without zero-fill**: \Plane::try_clone()\ and \FrameBuf::try_clone()\ reuse pre-allocated memory buffers directly without intermediate zeroing passes when writing CDEF and restoration filter stages.
3. **DC fast-path for inverse transforms**: transforms for pure DC residual blocks (\DCT_DCT\) bypass full matrix multiplication and perform flat DC expansion directly.

### Performance Results (AMD Ryzen 9 9900X3D, 16 threads)
- 1080p 8-bit GOP: 124 fps ➔ **133 fps** (+7%)
- 1080p 10-bit GOP: 118 fps ➔ **130 fps** (+10%)
- 1080p 8 tiles: 165 fps ➔ **175 fps** (+6%)

### Conformance & Verification
- \cargo test -p filmcraft-av1\: all 12 unittests + conformance vectors pass bit-exact.
- \cargo clippy -p filmcraft-av1 --all-targets -- -D warnings\: clean (0 warnings).
- \cargo fmt --check\: clean.

title: WIN-03: Make AVI oracle file reads portable
author: jahvari
body:
## Summary

- Replace the AVI oracle's unconditional Unix-only file API with safe standard-library seek/read operations.
- Hold one mutex across seek and read so concurrent readers get the requested offset.
- Add a small synthetic regression for exact/nonmonotonic offsets, EOF, extreme offsets, empty reads and shared concurrent reads.

Only `crates/avi/tests/ffmpeg_oracle.rs` changes. No dependencies, unsafe, shipped code or assets are added. The existing greater-than-1-GB oracle remains ignored.

## Validation

- Before the repair, Windows compilation failed with E0433 in the test helper.
- After the repair, the synthetic regression and existing AVI table oracle passed: 2 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored.
- Strict full-workspace/all-targets release Clippy passed.
- Full default `cargo xtask ci` passed: 3,305 tests passed, 0 failed, 45 ignored; fmt, strict release Clippy, release tests, layers, 69 asset attributions and 49 WASM crates passed.

title: fix(masks): Delete / Backspace and Cmd+Z take back the last pen point while drawing
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1345.

The pen draft (`app.ui.mask_pen`) lives outside the undo history, and the global shortcuts run before the panels draw, so while drawing Cmd+Z reverted the previous project edit and Delete / Backspace (Clear) removed the clip being masked, with the draft left as it was. A small `masks::pen_take_back` now runs in `handle_shortcuts` right after the dynamic-trim Esc, the same way that one is intercepted: while a draft is open it consumes Delete / Backspace (left to a focused text field) and Cmd+Z and drops the last point; taking back the last one closes the draft. Shift+Cmd+Z is left alone so it stays Redo. With an empty draft (pen just switched on) the key also closes the draft instead of reaching Clear on the selected clip; happy to switch if you'd rather let it through.

Validation:
- `masks_ui::delete_and_undo_take_back_the_last_pen_point`: fails on main (Delete with the Timeline focused clears the clip being masked; with that assert dropped, Cmd+Z empties the undo stack), passes here
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-ui-egui --test masks_ui`, `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: codecs: import raw ADTS .aac files (#1291)
author: bfenty
body:
## Problem

Raw ADTS `.aac` files are offered by File ▸ Import and the Media Browser, but importing one always failed with `unrecognised format` — including the `.aac` FilmCraft's own AAC export writes. `.m4a` worked; standalone ADTS never reached a decoder because `audio::opener` didn't list the extension and symphonia doesn't probe ADTS.

Closes #1291

## Change

- `audio::opener` now accepts `aac`.
- `AudioFileSource::decode` gains a `decode_adts_aac` path: `filmcraft_aac::split_adts` frames the stream, the first ADTS header builds the `Decoder` (`from_adts`), and each payload decodes as one access unit. A stream that doesn't start with ADTS frames returns `None` and falls through to the symphonia probe as before, so nothing that used to import changes path.
- Codec reported as `AAC`, container `AAC`, duration from decoded frames at the header's sample rate.

## Testing

- New `crates/codecs/tests/adts_import.rs`: ffmpeg writes a stereo ADTS fixture (440 Hz left / 880 Hz right so a swapped channel shows up), the test asserts the file imports with 2 channels at 48 kHz and matches ffmpeg's decode per channel (±3-sample lag tolerance for priming placement).
- **Red on main**: `ADTS .aac must import (#1291)` — panics at the `open_bytes` assertion.
- **Green with the patch**; negative control re-confirmed by stashing the fix.
- Regressions: `filmcraft-codecs` lib tests, `mp4_oracle`, `aac_channels_oracle`, `matroska_audio_oracle` — failure set identical to main (all pre-existing). `cargo fmt --check` and `clippy -p filmcraft-codecs --all-targets` clean.

title: Add a Nix flake (NixOS, GNOME and Hyprland)
author: untypequicode
body:
## What

Adds `flake.nix` and `nix/package.nix` so that `nix build`, `nix run` and an overlay give a source-built filmcraft and filmcraft-cli on NixOS, modelled on the existing LightCraft flake.

- `Cargo.lock` drives the dependencies (git sources through `cargoLock.allowBuiltinFetchGit`), so there is no `vendorHash` to maintain. The version comes from `[workspace.package]`.
- Installs the desktop file, hicolor icons, MIME types and AppStream metadata from `packaging/linux/`, validated at build time (`desktop-file-validate`, `appstreamcli`).
- Wayland and X11: the binaries are wrapped so the libraries winit/wgpu/rfd `dlopen` are found on NixOS — `libwayland-client`, `libxkbcommon` (incl. x11), the X11 libs, the Vulkan loader, `libEGL` and `libdbus` (xdg-desktop-portal file chooser). It runs natively on Wayland under GNOME and Hyprland, with X11/XWayland as fallback. Hyprland needs a portal backend for the file dialogs (`xdg.portal.extraPortals = [ pkgs.xdg-desktop-portal-gtk ]`); this is noted in `nix/package.nix`.
- The fonts from `storytold/craft-fonts`, where the app embeds them, are a pinned non-flake input at the revision the release workflow uses.
- Also: `overlays.default`, `apps.default`, a dev shell, `nix fmt` and a formatting check.
- `doCheck` is off: the suite needs corpora and a GPU the sandbox cannot provide (`cargo xtask ci` stays the gate); it can be turned on with `overrideAttrs`.

No Rust, packaging or CI file is touched.

## Testing

`nix build .#filmcraft` builds both binaries and passes the desktop-file and AppStream validation, on NixOS.

title: #1229: Finder opens the project it hands the app
author: schubam
body:
Fixes #1229 — the half that is left after #1310.

## What #1310 does and does not do

#1310 declares the document type, which is what stops Launch Services reporting

> The document "cut.fcproj" could not be opened. FilmCraft cannot open files in the "FilmCraft
> Project" format.

and gets the file to the app at all. It does not open it. macOS hands a document over as the Apple
Event `aevt`/`odoc`; AppKit gives that event to the **application delegate**, and the delegate
belongs to the windowing layer — `winit` registers `WinitApplicationDelegate` and its event loop
panics when it finds another one there — so nothing in FilmCraft ever saw the file, and the app
came up with its default project whether it was already running or had just been launched.

Measured, on one binary built from `main` with only the two `Info.plist.in` variants (Launch
Services launches the app with no arguments in both cases, the data directory and control channel
coming from the launchd session so the app can be asked what it has open):

| bundle | `open -g -a <app> cut.fcproj` | what the app reports |
|---|---|---|
| no document type (main) | Launch Services refuses the file | `FilmCraft Demo`, the file was never opened |
| #1310's document type | Launch Services accepts and launches it | `FilmCraft Demo` — still not opened |

## What this does

`crates/platform` registers its own `odoc` handler with `NSAppleEventManager`, which replaces
AppKit's handling of that one event without touching the delegate. It is the crate that owns OS
FFI (AGENTS.md §0.3, ADR 0001) and its second non-media call after `cursor.rs`; the API is safe —
paths come out as `String`s. The paths land in a queue and the UI drains them once a frame through
`HostHooks::os_open_files`: a project opens the way File ▸ Open opens one, anything else imports the
way the same file on the command line does, so an open event and the launch arguments agree —
including what counts as a project (`filmcraft_ui_egui::is_project_path`, o…

title: fix(media-browser): don't freeze the UI while probing files
author: ossini
body:
## Problem
Opening the Media Browser froze the app for ~9 s when the last folder held large videos. For the Frame Rate / Duration / … columns, every file was probed synchronously on the UI thread (2 per frame), and a 4–5 GB MKV takes 2–4 s to probe.

## Fix
- `media_browser::probe_background`: probes on a background thread (max. 4 at once, under `catch_unwind`), returns `None` until the result is in. Web build stays synchronous.
- List and thumbnail view use it and poll for results every 100 ms.

## Result
First open: **~9 s → ~0.4 s** (one normal frame). The columns fill in once the probes finish.

title: Add edit.rippleDeleteHead (Ripple Delete Head Frame)
author: bfenty
body:
## What

Adds `edit.rippleDeleteHead` — Ripple Delete Head Frame (#1357): removes the portion of the selected clip from its in point through the playhead and ripples the sequence closed.

## How

The command groups the selection by link id (with `with_links`, so a picture and its sound act as one group) and delegates the edit to `edit::ripple_trim_group` — the engine's existing linked-group ripple trim, which moves every member's in point by one delta and shifts synced tracks once. The head is the deepest member's head (clamped to each member's duration by the group trim's own clamping). When the playhead is past every member's out point the group is removed whole through `edit::ripple_delete_items`, so the gap closes with the same span/marker semantics as plain Ripple Delete. Sequence markers follow the closed stretch when `ripple_sequence_markers` is on. A playhead at or before a selected clip's in point is refused (nothing to remove); locked members are refused.

No new edit primitive was needed — this composes `ripple_trim_group` / `ripple_delete_items`, same as `edit.rippleDelete` composes `ripple_delete_items`.

## Tests

`crates/engine/src/ripple_head_tests.rs` — 4 tests on a 4-clip linked picture+sound sequence:
- head closes and later clips (and their sounds) shift left, sequence shortens
- the trimmed clip's `source_in` advances by the head length
- playhead at the in point is refused, nothing moves
- playhead past the out point removes the whole clip and closes its gap

Red/green: all 4 fail on pristine `main` (`0 passed; 4 failed` — unknown command), all 4 pass with the patch (`4 passed; 0 failed`), negative control by `git stash` round-trip. Full `cargo test -p filmcraft-engine` suite green; `cargo fmt` + `clippy` clean on the crate.

title: #1429: MPEG-1 program stream cut inside a pack header no longer panics
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1429

## Cause
`packet_len` in `crates/mpegts/src/ps.rs` returned `Some(12)` for an MPEG-1 pack header once 6 bytes were available, but `scan` reads the SCR from `head[4..9]`. A program stream ending inside its last pack header (e.g. the file `00 00 01 BA 21 00 00`) panicked with `range end index 9 out of range`. The MPEG-2 branch is fine: it needs `b.get(13)` and `scan` reads only 10 bytes.

## Fix
`packet_len` now requires the full 12-byte MPEG-1 pack header (`b.get(..12)?`); a shorter tail is not a packet and takes the existing resync path.

## Tests
- `program_stream_cut_inside_a_pack_header_never_panics`: the minimal 7-byte input and every cut of a 12-byte MPEG-1 pack header.
- `program_stream_truncation_at_every_length_never_panics`: a valid MPEG-1 and a valid MPEG-2 program stream truncated at every byte length, opened and every unit read.

Both new tests panicked before the fix: with the one-line fix temporarily removed they failed with `range end index 9 out of range for slice of length 7` (and `6`) at `ps.rs:159`; restored, they pass.

## Commands run
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-mpegts -p filmcraft-codecs` (all pass)
- `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-mpegts -p filmcraft-codecs --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt --check -p filmcraft-mpegts`
- `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`

Not run: `cargo test --workspace`, workspace-wide clippy/fmt, `cargo xtask assets` (shared machine; the change is two files in one crate).

title: #1432: mpegts: bounds-check frame_info, cap chunks, units and allocations, drop non-PES data
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1432

## Cause and fix (crates/mpegts only)
- **Panic**: `frame_info` read `b[6]` of an AC-3 header that `frame_len` only guarantees 6 bytes for (reachable via `fixed_packet_samples`). Now `b.get(6)?`. E-AC-3 with fscod 3 / fscod2 3 returns `None` instead of sample rate 0.
- **Chunk list**: `Splitter::feed` recorded a chunk per packet in the PES-delimited modes (LPCM, subtitles, unknown PIDs, H.264/HEVC), where nothing pruned it. `locate()` is only used by the MPEG-video and audio modes; in the PES modes `begin_pes_unit` leaves `pos` unresolved and `feed` fills it from its own `pos` argument (verified by reading the code, and by the test below checking `pos`/`offset` of every unit). Chunks are now recorded only for those two modes.
- **Allocations**: `read_unit` preallocates at most 1 MiB (`UNIT_PREALLOC`) and refuses units over `MAX_UNIT_BYTES` = 128 MiB (largest real units are intra pictures of a few MB). E-AC-3 frames shorter than `EAC3_MIN_FRAME` = 8 bytes are not frames. The unit table is capped at `MAX_UNITS` = 2^23 per stream (a `Unit` is 64 bytes, so 512 MiB; that is 47 h of 48 kHz AAC, the densest real stream at 46.9 units/s, or 9 h of 240 fps video). Beyond it units are not indexed and the scan adds a warning (TS only; see below).
- **PesAsm**: new `dropping` state until the next unit start, so continuation packets of a non-PES unit start no longer reach the splitter; a unit-start packet without payload (adaptation field only) no longer resets the PES in progress.

## Tests
New: `ac3_header_prefix_of_six_bytes_is_not_indexed_out_of_bounds`, `eac3_reserved_sample_rate_is_refused`, `four_byte_eac3_frames_make_no_units`, `pes_delimited_modes_do_not_retain_chunks` (5000 feeds, counter based), `unit_table_is_capped`, `non_pes_payload_is_dropped_until_the_next_unit_start`, `adaptation_field_only_unit_start_keeps_the_pes_in_progress`, `oversized_unit_is_refused_without_reserving_it`.

title: #1430: mpegts: resync inside the loaded block, bad adaptation field is not lost sync
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1430

## Cause
`ts::scan` took the "lost sync" branch for every `packet()` failure, set `k = usize::MAX` and re-read a whole 4096-packet block (~770 KB) from an offset that advanced about one packet. `packet()` returned `None` both for a bad sync byte and for an adaptation_field_length that overruns the packet, so perfectly aligned packets `47 11 00 30 FF ...` cost one block read each: a 564 KB file made `ByteSource::read_at` fetch 846 MB (1500x), a 1 GB file would read petabytes. Also: the fallback `off = pos + got` overshot by `k * packet_size` and skipped unread data, and the five-packet window only tried the first `packet_size` start positions, then fell back to a single `0x47` (possibly a payload byte).

## Fix (`crates/mpegts/src/ts.rs`)
- `packet()` returns `Result<Packet, Bad>`: `Bad::Sync` (grid lost) vs `Bad::Adaptation` (sync byte fine, adaptation field overruns).
- `Bad::Adaptation`: packet treated as "no payload", scan continues with the next packet, counted as a new warning ("N packet(s) with an invalid adaptation field"), not lost sync. `read()` skips such a packet instead of ending the unit.
- `Bad::Sync`: new `resync()` searches the already-loaded block (any distance) for the first start where five sync bytes line up; the block is refilled from the exact new offset only when exhausted. Candidates whose five-packet window does not fit yet are deferred to the next block rather than accepted on a single `0x47` (except at EOF).
- Valid streams take the same path as before.

## Tests (`crates/mpegts/src/tests.rs`)
- `bad_adaptation_fields_do_not_amplify_reads`: 3000 aligned packets with a bad adaptation field, counting `ByteSource`, asserts bytes read <= 4x file size (counter, no timing) and that it is a warning, not lost sync.
- `garbage_without_sync_does_not_amplify_reads`: a 0x47 every 189 bytes, same bound.
- `transport_stream_resyncs_after_garbage`: 188- and 192-byte packets, garbage prefix, mid-stream garbage of several lengths placed around…

title: #1437: mpegts: drop TEI/duplicate packets, skip scrambled, first PMT wins
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1437

## Cause
`ts.rs` ignored `transport_error_indicator`, `transport_scrambling_control` and duplicate packets, so garbage / encrypted / twice-sent payload reached the splitter. PMT handling ignored `current_next_indicator` and `section_number`; a new PMT version only added PIDs (a PID that changed codec kept its old splitter, removed PIDs stayed); the CRC ran before the version check; the PAT was re-parsed on every repeat.

## Decisions (maintainer)
- TEI packets are dropped; scrambled packets are skipped with a warning (not an error); exact duplicates are dropped, conservatively (same PID, same counter as the previous payload packet, identical payload bytes, has payload; anything else is kept). All three are counted in the scan warnings.
- The first PMT wins. A later differing PMT (new version, changed codec, removed PIDs) is ignored with one warning. `current_next_indicator` 0 is ignored (PAT and PMT); a PMT must be section 0 of 0 (as H.222.0 requires, matching the existing single-section handling). The PAT is not processed once the PMT PID is known. The version check runs before the CRC (a repeat of the used PMT costs no CRC); a differing version is CRC-checked before it counts as a change.

## Notes
- `read_unit` applies the same TEI / scrambled / duplicate filter as the scan, so unit offsets into the elementary stream stay consistent.
- The TEI check runs before packet parsing, so a flagged packet with a garbage adaptation field is dropped rather than treated as lost sync. Scrambled packets still contribute their PCR and keep the continuity counter in step (no spurious CC error).
- PAT is not restricted to section 0 (a program may be listed in a later section; the existing code accepted the first program of any section).

## Tests (crates/mpegts/src/tests.rs)
TEI packet dropped; scrambled packet skipped with warning; duplicate dropped (units identical to the clean stream) while a same-counter packet with different payload is kept; later differing PMTs…

title: #1436: mpegts: H.264/HEVC units are access units; H.264 recovery points are key
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1436

## Cause
`crates/mpegts/src/es.rs` made an H.264/HEVC unit out of one PES packet with a timestamp (the crate docs claimed access-unit splitting). Two defects followed:
- **B8**: several access units in one PES (only the first has a PTS) became one unit: several frames under one PTS to the decoder, `key`/`disposable` OR-combined.
- **B7**: H.264 `key` was IDR only (NAL type 5). Broadcast/camcorder/cut TS with non-IDR I pictures plus recovery point SEI had no (or only one) key unit, so `mpeg.rs` failed with "no random-access picture in the video stream" or seeks always went back to the start.

## User decisions implemented
- B8 (A): split units by access unit. A new unit starts at the first NAL that cannot belong to the slices already seen (H.264 7.4.1.2.3: AUD, SPS, PPS, SEI, NAL 14..18; H.265 7.4.2.4.4: AUD, VPS/SPS/PPS, prefix SEI, 41..44, 48..55) or at a slice with first_mb_in_slice == 0 / first_slice_segment_in_pic_flag. Only the first access unit of a PES keeps its PTS/DTS; later ones have none. A 4-byte start code's leading zero byte goes with its own NAL. Redundant pictures and arbitrary slice order are not specially handled (spec's frame_num/pps-id comparison needs the SPS; not done).
- B7 (A): an H.264 unit containing a recovery point SEI (payload type 6, found among other messages, emulation prevention removed) is `key`. HEVC already marks IRAP (BLA/IDR/CRA) as key; gradual-refresh HEVC with only recovery point SEI is left as is.

## Behaviour before recovery completes
No decoder change was needed or made (`crates/codecs/src/mpeg.rs` untouched). `filmcraft_h264` already starts at a non-IDR picture: the frame_num gap fill inserts concealment frames, so missing references never panic or error. Frames shown before a recovery point's `recovery_frame_cnt` completes are therefore presented but may be imperfect (open-GOP leading pictures are still dropped by the existing presentation logic; with recovery_frame_cnt == 0 everything shown is bit-exact, s…

title: fix(media-browser): drag every selected file to the Timeline, not just one (#1360)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1360.

When several files were selected in the Media Browser and dragged onto the Timeline, only one of them was placed. `start_file_drag` imported the selection but started the drag with only the first new item. If the file under the pointer was already in the project, the drag carried only that item and imported nothing else.

The fix:
- Files from the selection that are already in the project are reused. Only the others are imported.
- When the drag carries more than one item, the Project selection is set to all of them, and the drag starts from the first one. The Timeline drop already places the whole Project selection when the dragged item is part of it (`dragged_selection`, the same path as a multi-item drag from the Project panel). So the files go in back to back, in one undo step. The bin drop in the Project panel also uses that selection.
- A drop that lands nowhere (or is cancelled with Escape) still undoes only the import done by this drag.

Tests:
- `media_browser_drag_places_every_selected_file` (headless, `crates/ui-egui/tests/project_panel_ui.rs`): selects two WAV files in the Media Browser, one already imported and one not, and drags them onto the Timeline. It checks that only the new file is imported and that both clips are placed. On `main`, only one clip is placed.
- A unit test for the helper that builds the dragged item list.

title: fix(bitstream): map se(v) through the 64-bit codeNum so i32::MIN round-trips
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1428.

`read_se` narrowed the codeNum to `u32` through `read_ue` before applying the signed mapping, so codeNum 2^32 (which is -2^31) was rejected, and codeNum 2^32 - 1 (+2^31) came back as `i32::MIN` via the `as i32` wrap. `write_se(i32::MIN)` needed codeNum 2^32 too, which overflowed the `u32` multiply (panic in debug, a silent `0` in release). Both now go through private `u64` codeNum helpers shared with `read_ue`/`write_ue`: the reader maps in `i64` and uses `i32::try_from`, so an out-of-range value is `InvalidExpGolomb` instead of a wrapped number, and the writer computes the code from `unsigned_abs()` in `u64`. Public signatures and `read_ue`'s `u32` range and 32-leading-zero limit are unchanged.

Validation:
- `signed_exp_golomb_extremes_roundtrip` (0, ±1, `i32::MAX`, `i32::MIN`): fails on main (`attempt to multiply with overflow`), passes here
- `signed_exp_golomb_reads_minimum_from_spec_bits` (codeNum 2^32): fails on main (`Err(InvalidExpGolomb)`), passes here
- `signed_exp_golomb_rejects_positive_overflow` (codeNum 2^32 - 1): fails on main (`Ok(-2147483648)`), passes here
- `unsigned_exp_golomb_keeps_u32_range`: guards that `ue(v)` still rejects codeNum 2^32
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-bitstream --lib`, `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-bitstream --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: fix(monitor): the playback and paused resolution set the rendered frame size
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1420.

The monitor rendered at `min(resolution, on-screen size)`: before applying Playback/Paused Resolution it capped the scale at the frame pixels the monitor shows. On a typical layout the Program monitor shows a 1080p sequence at ~0.35, so Full, 1/2 and often 1/4 all rendered the same 0.375 frame and switching between them changed nothing. Now the frame renders at the chosen fraction of the frame size and the monitor scales it to fit, as Premiere does. The trade-off is that Full on a small monitor now renders every pixel of the sequence (that's what Full means, and lowering the resolution is the way to make it cheaper). Happy to switch to keeping the cap for Full only if you'd rather not pay for that.

Validation:
- `crates/ui-egui/tests/preview_resolution.rs`: fails on main (Paused Resolution Full shows a frame at scale 375 instead of 1000), passes here; 1/2 and 1/4 give exactly half and a quarter of the sequence's width and height
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-ui-egui --test preview_resolution --test view_ui`, `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: #1449: mpegts: PCR from the PMT's PCR_PID, per-stream unwrap, SCR unwrap, sane language
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1449

## Cause
- `ts::scan` took the PCR of every PID and unwrapped them against one `last_pcr`; the PMT's `PCR_PID` was never read. Two PIDs with PCR bases 1000 and 2^32+5000 gave `pcr_range = (300000, 1288515988800)`.
- One `Unwrap` was shared by all elementary streams (TS and PS). A stream on another time base moved the shared `last` and shifted the others by 2^33. A pre-wrap timestamp arriving after a small first one was not corrected because of the `base > 0` condition. The doc said "relative to the first one", the code returns absolute values.
- The program stream SCR was never unwrapped; `pcr_range` doc said "First and last" but the value is min/max.
- PMT language used `from_utf8_lossy(..).trim()`: `00 00 00` gave `Some("\0\0\0")`.

## Fix
- New `ClockRange` (lib.rs): 27 MHz unwrap plus min/max. TS keeps one per PCR-carrying PID; `pcr_range` is the clock of the PMT's `PCR_PID` (section bytes 8..9). Rule: PMT `PCR_PID` if a PMT was parsed (so `None` for `0x1FFF` or a PID without PCR), otherwise the first PID seen with a PCR. The PS SCR uses the same type.
- One `Unwrap` per TS PID and per PS stream. Values stay absolute; a late pre-wrap timestamp now goes below the wrap even when the stream has not wrapped yet (e.g. `5` then `2^33-3` gives `-3`, and does not shift the timeline). Arithmetic saturates. Doc corrected.
- Language: exactly three ASCII letters, lowercased, else `None`.
- Docs of `File::pcr_range` and `Unwrap` match the code.

## Tests (crates/mpegts/src/tests.rs, deterministic)
`pcr_range_follows_the_pmt_pcr_pid`, `pcr_range_without_a_usable_pcr_pid`, `pcr_range_unwraps_the_33_bit_base`, `timestamps_of_different_streams_unwrap_independently`, `a_late_pre_wrap_timestamp_first_after_the_wrap_goes_below_zero`, `program_stream_scr_is_unwrapped_and_ordered`, `language_descriptor_accepts_only_three_letters`.
Without the fix to lib.rs/ts.rs/ps.rs (stashed, tests kept) 6 of 7 fail (e.g. `left: Some((300000, 1288515988800))`, `[1000, 8589937752, 8589…

title: ui: Ctrl-click multi-select in Effect Controls feeds Save Preset (#1394)
author: bfenty
body:
## What

Effect Controls rows now support Ctrl-click (⌘ on macOS) multi-selection, and **Save Preset…** captures every selected effect of the clip instead of only the right-clicked row. Fixes #1394.

## Why

The engine command `presets.save` already accepts an `effects: [index]` array, but the UI context menu hardcoded `vec![idx]` — a single row. Saving a multi-effect look meant one preset per effect.

## How

- `UiState.fx_multi: Vec<(ClipId, usize)>` tracks the multi-selection (per clip, ordered).
- Plain click on a row replaces the selection with that row; Ctrl-click toggles the row in/out (same modifier-detection idiom as the multicam panel, so synthetic `ui.click` modifiers work in tests).
- The row context menu's Save Preset… passes all selected indices of that clip (sorted) to `presets::open_save`; falls back to the clicked row when the menu is opened on an unselected row.

## Tests

`crates/ui-egui/tests/preset_multiselect_ui.rs` (headless kittest):
- `ctrl_click_multi_select_saves_all_selected_effects_into_one_preset` — two effects, Ctrl-click both, Save Preset… → draft carries both indices, saved preset lists both effects.
- `a_plain_click_replaces_the_selection_with_one_effect` — plain click collapses the selection to one row.

Red/green verified: both fail on main (context menu offers only single-row save), pass with the fix; negative control via stash round-trip. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-ui-egui --all-targets` clean.

title: mpegts: simplify and avoid redundant work
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1450

Behaviour is unchanged. One commit per change.

## Changes and proof

| Change | Proof |
| --- | --- |
| Remove unread `PesHeader.stream_id` / `packet_length` (`pes.rs`) | Simplification: existing `pes::tests` and all mpegts tests pass (the one assertion on `stream_id` is dropped). |
| Doc fixes: `Unit.pos` is a byte offset for TS too (scan stores `off + k * packet_size`); stale doc line above `frame_bytes` | Docs only. |
| Table-driven `crc32_mpeg` (`ts.rs`) | `work_tests::table_crc_equals_the_bitwise_crc` keeps the old bitwise loop as the reference: equal for all 256 single bytes, random inputs of 15 lengths 0..4096, the CRC-32/MPEG-2 check value `0x0376E6E7`, and section + own CRC == 0. No counter test: one lookup per byte instead of eight shift steps is not observable through a counter. |
| Cap the program stream window refill at the bytes left in the file (`ps.rs` `Win::get`) | `ps::tests::capped_window_returns_what_the_uncapped_window_returned`: the old refill is the reference, same slices for 10 file lengths x many positions x 10 sizes (incl. EOF edges). `misses_near_the_end_zero_at_most_the_bytes_that_are_left`: a cfg(test) counter of zero-filled bytes is at most 1000 in a tail scenario with 500 misses; the old refill zeroes about 500 MiB there. No timing. |
| Borrow packets from the window instead of `to_vec()` in `ps::scan` / `ps::read` | `work_tests::program_stream_with_large_pes_packets_gives_back_every_frame` (two streams, over 2 MiB, MPEG-1 and MPEG-2 packs, cuts inside the last packets): passes on the old code (checked) and the new code, as do the existing round-trip and truncation tests. The allocation saving follows from the removed copies and is **not measured**: the workspace forbids `unsafe`, so there is no counting allocator. |

## Deferred (would edit hunks of open PRs)
