title: feat(updater): crash-resilient self-updating for desktop app
author: ARYAN007H
body:
### Summary
Closes #1272

Implements self-updating for the FilmCraft desktop application via a new, dependency-light L5 crate (`filmcraft-updater`) and wires it end-to-end into the desktop app and UI.

The updater adheres strictly to FilmCraft's **"Never Crash"** rule, clean-room standards, and zero-bloat principles: pure Rust (rustls + RustCrypto TLS, flate2, tar), no C code, zero `unsafe`, and zero background daemons.

---

### Architecture & Pipeline

```text
check()    GET github.com/storytold/filmcraft/releases/latest (redirect → vX.Y.Z; no API tokens / rate limits)
           GET …/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/SHA256SUMS.txt (pinned domain allowlist)
stage()    Stream tarball to .part with size cap & live SHA-256 → rename on match
           Safe extraction (no .., absolute paths, links, or zip bombs; fsync durability)
           Smoke test: execute <staged>/bin/filmcraft --version (catches incompatible glibc / arch before touching disk)
           Write staged.json
apply()    Helper mode (`--update-apply`): wait for parent PID exit → <name>.new fsync → <name> to <name>.prev → atomic swap
on_boot()  Track unconfirmed boots. If a new version crashes twice before `confirm()`, the 3rd start restores .prev (keeps broken build as .broken)
confirm()  Called on healthy app launch (after 2 painted frames). Old `.prev` backups are cleaned after 7 days
```

---

### Key Features & Guarantees

1. **Zero-Rate-Limit Discovery (`net.rs`, `release.rs`):**
   * Follows the HTTP redirect of `/releases/latest` to resolve the newest tag without hitting unauthenticated GitHub API rate limits (which 403 after 60 req/hr).
   * Pinned HTTPS allowlist for release assets.
   * Throttles automated background checks to at most once per 24 hours (`~/.config/filmcraft/update_state.json`).

2. **Hardened Extraction (`extract.rs`):**
   * Guarded against Zip-Slip and path traversal (rejects any entry with `..`, absolute paths, symlinks, or special devices).
   * Enforces decompression bomb limi…

title: NVENC H.265 export on Linux, and NVENC export at all (#1624)
author: ComfyChloe
body:
## Summary

`--format hevc` on Linux with an NVIDIA GPU failed with *"no encoder registered"* and H.265 was unusable in the export dialog (#1624).

**Correcting an earlier version of this description:** I wrote that "NVENC was never registered as an export encoder on Linux at all". That was wrong. `main` registers `nvenc::export::factory` on 64-bit Linux as the first statement of `register()` (`crates/platform/src/lib.rs`), so H.264 already reached NVENC on Linux. The real gap was narrower and is two lines of it:

- `nvenc::export::factory` returns `None` for `Format::Hevc` on anything but Windows, so H.265 never reached NVENC even though the factory was registered;
- no `Format::Hevc` probe and no HDR probe were installed on Linux, so `available(Format::Hevc)` was false and the format was never offered. With no built-in HEVC encoder, that surfaces as "no encoder registered".

## Problem

| | |
|---|---|
| `crates/platform/src/nvenc/export.rs` | `factory` returns `None` for `Format::Hevc` on anything but Windows (`cfg!(target_os = "windows")`) |
| `crates/platform/src/lib.rs` | the Linux `register()` block installs no `Format::Hevc` probe and no HDR probe |
| `crates/platform/tests/nvenc_hevc*.rs` | all six H.265 test files are `#![cfg(target_os = "windows")]` |

Nothing in the encoder itself is platform-specific. `nvenc/session.rs` and `nvenc/device.rs` already carry Linux paths (a retained primary CUDA context through the run-time `libcuda.so.1`), and `tests/nvenc.rs` and `tests/nvenc_export.rs` — the H.264 tests — have been built and run on 64-bit Linux since they were written. The H.265 logic (profile / level / tier choice, the `hvcC` built from the encoder's own SPS) sits on that same session and ring.

## Fix

- **`nvenc::export::factory`** sends H.265 to `hevc_factory` everywhere. Choosing the format is the opt-in; there is no software encoder to fall back to, so a decline is an error that names the reason.
- **`register()`'s Linux block** installs the `Forma…

title: scrub bars: dragging the playhead keeps the audio stream open instead of stopping it every move
author: ReReddo
body:
## What and why

Dragging the playhead along a monitor's scrub bar was choppy and silent, while dragging its timecode scrubbed smoothly and played audio. The scrub bar called `stop()` on every move of the drag. With nothing playing, `stop()` still stops the audio output, which closes the scrub stream the drag had just opened (`scrub.rs` keeps one stream open for the whole drag and only re-aims it), so the next frame built the sequence's mix and reopened the output on the interface thread, again for every move; and each new stream was stopped by the next move before it could play a grain. The timecode drag does not call `stop()`, which is why it was fine.

`FilmcraftApp::stop_for_scrub` stops only when something is playing or about to (preroll). The four surfaces that move the playhead on a press or drag use it: the Program Monitor's scrub bar, the Timeline ruler, the Effect Controls ruler and the transition controls' ruler. Pressing one while playing still stops playback, as before.

## How it was tested

- `dragging_a_scrub_bar_keeps_one_output_stream_open` (`meters_ui`): drag along the Program Monitor's scrub bar and the Timeline ruler; the output is started at most once during the drag (it was started on each of the 8 moves for the monitor bar) and the callback produces sound.
- `the_meters_move_while_scrubbing` unchanged and green.
- `cargo fmt` on the changed files, `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p filmcraft-ui-egui` (two failures that also fail on main: `alt_box_selects_only_video_and_delete_keeps_linked_audio`, `graphics_notice_ui::the_notice_follows_the_interface_language`).

## Overlap

No open PR touches `scrub_playhead`, the monitor's scrub bar arm or `stop()`; a merge into main is clean.

title: window: Toggle Full Screen fullscreens on the Program monitor (#1369)
author: notdezzi
body:
Fixes #1369

## What
`window.toggleFullScreen` (View menu / Ctrl+`) already put the OS window into full screen, but the whole editor layout stayed on screen — the reporter's "it just does a full view of the app". As in Premiere, entering full screen now also maximizes the **Program monitor**, so the picture fills the screen; leaving full screen brings back exactly the layout that was there before (or the panel that was maximized before, if any, e.g. via `window.maximizeFrame`).

## How
- New pure state machine `fullscreen_maximize` in `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/keyboard.rs`, driven by the existing `KeysState` (new `saved_maximized` / `full_screen` fields, serde-defaulted so existing saved states keep loading): enter → save the current maximize state and maximize the Program monitor (reusing `apply_dock(Activate)`); exit → restore. A repeated enter while already in full screen keeps the original layout saved (guards against viewport-state lag / double fire).
- The command route calls it right after sending `ViewportCommand::Fullscreen`.

## Tests

title: ui: keep the waveform anchored while a remix drag previews (#1424)
author: bfenty
body:
## Problem (#1424)
Dragging a clip edge to remix it made the waveform jump/squash mid-drag: while the preview was active the clip body shrank to the new width, but the waveform still mapped through the *original* item, so the whole waveform squeezed into the previewed width until the drag committed.

## Fix
In the `Drag::Remix` arm, insert an edited item into the `edited` map the way Trim and Roll already do — clone the item and bump only `duration` (the commit path keeps `start`/`source_in` and changes only duration). The preview render loop then derives the waveform mapping from the edited item, so media-per-pixel stays constant during the drag.

## Tests
Headless egui test `remix_drag_keeps_the_waveform_anchored` (in `panels/timeline.rs`): starts a remix drag and asserts the waveform's media-per-pixel scale under the preview equals the committed scale.
- RED without the fix (original duration over previewed width ≠ 1/pps)
- GREEN with the fix
- Negative control: reverting only the fix hunk makes the test fail again
- `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-ui-egui --all-targets` clean, `cargo fmt` clean

title: captions: pin the setStyle margin contract with a regression test; clearer track error (#1542)
author: notdezzi
body:
Fixes #1542

## Investigation
I could not reproduce the reported placement on current main. With the reporter's exact parameters (1080×1920 sequence, `captions.setStyle {anchor: "bottom", margin: 0.31, size: 78}`), `render_caption` puts the caption's bottom edge at y=1325 — 595 px above the bottom, i.e. exactly `0.31 × frame height`, matching the documented contract. The burn-in code is byte-identical between v0.6.0 (what the reporter used) and main, and the Program monitor preview, `render_frame` and exports all go through the same `caption_overlays` path.

The reported position (~200 px ≈ 0.1 of the frame) matches the **default** margin (0.08 ≈ 154 px), which points at the margin never having reached the rendered track's style in that session — most plausibly a `track` id mismatch whose error was swallowed by the client (the reporter also noted they had not retested on 0.7.2). The reporter's workaround (anchor middle) ignores margin by design, which is why it "worked".

## What this PR does
- Adds a regression test pinning the documented contract in `crates/captions/src/burn.rs`: bottom anchor → content bottom edge at `h − margin·h`, top anchor → top edge at `margin·h`, and margins 0 / 0.45 / out-of-range-clamped stay inside the frame.
- `captions.setStyle` now names the offending track value in its error ("no such caption track (…) — pass the track id from captions.list, or \"C1\"…") so a silently-swallowed id mismatch is diagnosable.

## Tests
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-captions --lib`: 43 passed (incl. the new `margin_is_a_fraction_of_frame_height`).
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-engine --lib captions`: 6 passed. Clippy (`-D warnings`) and fmt clean on both crates.

If the reporter can retest on 0.7.2+ with the improved error message, a remaining reproduction would pinpoint the client-side path; the rendering contract itself is now test-enforced.

title: mcp: --automation-read-root / --automation-write-root confine the server to folders (#985)
author: notdezzi
body:
Fixes #985

**What:** `filmcraft-cli mcp` now accepts `--automation-read-root <dir>` and `--automation-write-root <dir>` (each an existing folder; repeat/missing-value rejected), the flags VectorCraft and EffectCraft ship. While roots are in force every command may only read under a read root and only write under a write root — a root left out grants no access of its kind; without both, behavior is unchanged.

**Why:** an agent connected to the server could read/write anywhere the user can (#985, follow-up to #476/#595).

**How:** enforcement lives in `FilmcraftMcp::run` (the one funnel for `command_run`, `command_batch`, `media_import` and long exports), so both the headless engine and `--bridge` are covered (in bridge mode commands are checked in the CLI before they reach the app; the desktop app process itself is not confined — out of this issue's scope). Paths are resolved (links followed, `..` and dangling links refused, Windows device names refused) and compared component-wise against the canonicalized root; rejections are tool errors naming the root. 30 read + 34 write commands are tabled, plus a sweep of any other absolute path in params; the UI-driving tools (`ui_click`/`ui_key`/ui_control`) are refused while confined, since they could drive the app's native file dialogs — mirroring EffectCraft.

**Tested:** 12 new roots unit tests (containment, traversal, links, Windows case/devices), 2 new server tests, CLI flag-shape tests; `cargo test -p filmcraft-automation` 33 passed, `cargo test -p filmcraft-cli` 19 passed; fmt + clippy `-D warnings` green; end-to-end stdio run verified reads/writes outside the roots are refused and in-root writes land.

## How it was tested

title: fix(vp9): keep a decoder-pool worker available to the loop filter wavefront (#1283)
author: earlvanze
body:
## Summary
- Fix the VP9 loop-filter work schedule so at least one decoder-pool worker remains available while wavefront helpers wait for their predecessor row.
- Add a 1080p two-thread regression test that compares decode output against the FFmpeg reference.

## Reproduction and root cause
The reported 1080p WebM export hangs in `render_batch` at 0% CPU, while a single-frame `render` succeeds. A smaller 320×180 clip exports normally because its loop filter never creates enough wavefront rows to saturate the thread pool.

`PostJob::run` scheduled `pool.current_num_threads() + 1` wavefront participants. The post thread executed one row inline and spawned helpers for every other row. Those helpers waited on the decoder's row-progress condition variable *inside* Rayon workers. Rayon only treats a worker as intentionally blocked when the wait happens through a nested Rayon scope/join, so it could not replenish blocked workers. If stale post jobs were already queued, all pool workers could become blocked and the never-returning condvar wait appeared as the export deadlock.

## Fix
- Limit the number of spawned wavefront helpers to the pool thread count, keeping at least one pool worker unblocked. The post thread still runs its own wavefront row(s) inline.
- Behavior is unchanged for one decoder thread, which does not use the pool.

## Testing
- `crates/vp9/tests/conformance.rs::loop_filter_wavefront_keeps_a_pool_worker_available`: decodes the 1080p fixture with `Decoder::with_threads(2)` and checks it bit-exactly against the FFmpeg reference.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo fmt --all`
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-vp9 --release -- --test-threads=1`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --release -- -D warnings`
- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --release`
- `cargo xtask ci`: format, Clippy, layers, assets, WebAssembly checks, and workspace tests all pass, except the pre-existing repo-wide `apps/filmcraft dev_icon::tests::desktop_file_matches_the_packaged_…

title: codecs: start an edited MP4 at its first presented picture
author: earlvanze
body:
## Problem

An MP4 whose video edit list starts with an empty edit (a start offset, e.g. from `-output_ts_offset`) renders every picture one frame too early against ffprobe's own timeline.

Reproduced from #1276: `testsrc` prints each frame's generation time on the picture, and the file's edit list is `[~53 ms empty, then media from the B-frame skip]`. ffprobe reports `start_time ≈ 0.053` and frame 0 at `pts_time ≈ 0.052979`. Sequence time 2.1042 s inside a Sequence From Clip (24 fps) must show the picture ffprobe places there; before this fix the source answered one frame early.

## Root cause

`filmcraft-isobmff` already computes `edit_offset` as the sum of empty edits minus the first `media_time` (e.g. −369 + 1024 = +655 ticks in the repro), so the demux side is correct.

`Mp4Source`, however, gated its "start at first picture" rebase on `t.edits.is_empty()`. With a leading empty edit the positive `edit_offset` was never applied, so every later `sample_at_presentation_time` lookup stayed one empty-edit shift ahead of the actual presentation.

The B-frame rebase case (#714) and the new leading-empty-edit case share the same first-presentation math: `min pts + edit_offset`.

## Change

- Drop the `t.edits.is_empty()` gate in `rebase_unedited_video` so the shift applies to any file whose first presented picture sits after media time zero.
- Make the function return the applied `Tick` shift.
- After a successful rebase, subtract that shift from the edit-list presentation duration. The media duration already excludes the delay, and fragmented files keep the media duration regardless.

Call order is intentionally `snap_to_frame_grid` first, then `rebase_unedited_video`. The #1282 snap only moves samples onto the frame grid; the subsequent rebase updates `edit_offset` so later presentation-time lookups stay consistent after the shift.

## Tests

- Updated the existing `duration_follows_the_edit_list` unit test: a one-frame empty edit followed by four frames now reports …

title: #1644: save dialogs add the file's extension and ask before replacing what that names
author: txiki739
body:
On GNOME and other GTK desktops, the XDG portal shows GTK's file chooser, which saves the name exactly as typed. Type `edit` in Save As and the project is written as `edit`, with no `.fcproj`, so File > Open's "FilmCraft Project" filter hides it. Export dialogs do the same: `cut` for an EDL is written without `.edl`. This came up in #1644.

## Fix

Every native save dialog, whether opened through `FilmcraftApp::pick` or `pick_ui`, now ends its answer in one of the dialog's extensions (`native_dialogs::with_save_extension`):

| Typed | Saved as |
|---|---|
| `cut` | `cut.fcproj` |
| `cut.` | `cut.fcproj` |
| `a.filmcraft` | `a.filmcraft.fcproj` |
| `CUT.FCPROJ` | `CUT.FCPROJ` (unchanged) |
| `subs.vtt` in the captions dialog | `subs.vtt` (any listed extension is kept) |

Windows and macOS dialogs already add the extension, so nothing changes there.

Adding the extension can name a different file from the one the dialog asked about, so its own replace prompt doesn't cover it. Example: you type `keep`, and `keep.fcproj` already exists. In that case the app now asks before writing:

> "“keep.fcproj” already exists in “edits”. Do you want to replace it?"

- **Replace** runs the save.
- **Cancel** does nothing, as if the dialog had been cancelled. Escape also cancels.
- No other file dialog opens while the prompt is up.
- Automation ids: `overwrite.replace` and `overwrite.cancel`.

A name that already ends in the extension goes straight through, because the dialog itself already asked.

Translations: es, fr, it, ja, pt-BR and zh-CN.

## Tests

- `native_dialogs::tests::a_saved_name_gets_the_first_extension_unless_it_has_one_of_them`: bare names, trailing dot, other extensions, any case, Windows paths, several extensions, wildcard, odd input.

title: #1468: Speed/Duration ▸ Maintain Audio Pitch time-stretches a clip's audio instead of resampling it
author: txiki739
body:
Premiere's Clip Speed / Duration dialog has a **Maintain Audio Pitch** option. FilmCraft had no equivalent: a clip's audio was always resampled (varispeed), so at 200 % it played an octave up and at 50 % an octave down. #1468 is likely this case. The shuttle preference fixed in #959 only covers J/L playback.

## What changes

- **Clip > Speed/Duration…** has a **Maintain Audio Pitch** checkbox between Reverse Speed and Ripple Edit, as in Premiere. It is prefilled from the clip.
  - `clip.speedDuration` takes `"maintainPitch": bool`, and a call without it leaves the setting as it is.
  - The setting goes on the clip and its linked partners, like the speed.
  - `sequence.inspect` shows it.
- **`TrackItem::maintain_pitch`** is a new project field. It uses `serde(default)` and is skipped when false, so existing projects load and save unchanged.
- **Rendering.** A clip with the option on, at any speed other than 100 % and not frame-held, is time-stretched instead of resampled.
  - Forward and reversed clips are both supported, and nested sequences too.
  - Playback, export and Loudness Auto-Match all go through the same `raw_channels` path.
- **`filmcraft-audio-dsp::stretch::Wsola`** (L1, no dependencies, wasm-clean) does the stretch with WSOLA:
  - 30 ms raised-cosine grains overlapped by half;
  - each grain moved by up to 8 ms to where its first hop best matches the previous grain's natural continuation (normalised cross-correlation, coarse then refined), so the crossfaded halves are in phase.
- **`filmcraft-render::stretch`** keeps the chain of grain positions per clip, the same way `audio_fx` keeps effect chains:
  - Output hops lie on an absolute grid of timeline samples, so a chain read in order gives the same samples however playback or export cuts the reads.
  - A read elsewhere (a seek) starts a new chain four grains early.
  - A read whose source span would exceed 2²⁴ samples falls back to varispeed.

Translations for "Maintain Audio Pitch": es, fr, it, ja, ko…

title: cfb: reject NUL in entry names, checked sector arithmetic, allocation-free name compare
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1716

## Cause
- `validate_name` accepted U+0000. Directory entry names are NUL-terminated, so `Writer::stream(ROOT, "a\0b", ..)` was written and read back as `"a"`; `find("a\0b")` returned `NotFound` and two distinct names could collide on read.
- `sector()` and `read_mini_chain` did `n as usize + 1`, `s as usize * 64` and `at + 64` unchecked: overflow on a 32-bit `usize` (wasm32). Not reachable on 64-bit.

## Changes (crates/cfb only)
- `validate_name` rejects `\0`.
- New `read::span(index, skip, unit)` with `checked_add`/`checked_mul`; `sector()` range-checks against `MAXREGSECT` first and uses `usize::try_from`, `read_mini_chain` uses the same helper.
- `compare_names` compares via iterators, no `Vec<u16>` allocations (`child()` calls it once per sibling). Same ordering.
- `read_chain` pre-sizes its buffer with `limit.min(data.len())`.
- Removed dead code: the `FREESECT` check in `read_chain` (already rejected as `> MAXREGSECT` at the top of the loop; only the error text for that case changes) and the `steps` counter in `build_tree` (the `owner` set already prevents revisits).
- `Entry::children` doc: sorted order only holds for well-formed files.

## Tests
- `nul_in_a_name_is_rejected`: failed before the fix (`assertion failed: validate_name("a\0b").is_err()`), passes after. The old behaviour was also seen directly: the name read back as `"a"`.
- `compare_names_matches_the_allocating_version`: the old implementation is kept in the test and compared against the new one over a name list (ASCII, case pairs, ß/ss, Ü/ü, titlecase digraphs, CJK, fullwidth, surrogate pairs, U+FFFF) and over every Unicode scalar against several fixed names, both argument orders. The new version allocates nothing: it only creates iterators over the `&str`s.
- `span_is_checked`: exercises the checked helper directly with `usize::MAX`. This tests the arithmetic on 64-bit; the actual 32-bit overflow (and wasm32 at run time) is NOT exercised. `cargo xtask wasm` only type-checks.

title: codecs: the frame rate is what a clip's rounded durations average to (#1700)
author: lu123bing
body:
Fixes #1700.

**What happens**

A video track's frame rate came from the median sample duration. Phones and messaging apps stamp frame times rounded to whole milliseconds inside a 90 kHz track: a 30 fps clip's samples then last 2970 and 3060 units in turn, a 60 fps clip's 1440 and 1530. The median is either of the two, so the clip read as 30.303 / 58.824 fps, New Sequence From Clip made a sequence at that rate, and frames were dropped — exporting the 4-second 60 fps clip gave 235 frames, and a sequence frame asked at an exact 60 fps grid time returned the picture before.

**What changes**

`crates/codecs/src/mp4.rs` takes the nominal rate from the mean of the sample durations within a quarter frame of their median (a duration further out is a picture the file holds longer, not rounding, so it stays out of the mean), read as a standard rate when it is within half a percent of one (`FrameRate::from_f64_within`, `crates/time/src/lib.rs`). `snap_to_frame_grid` uses that same rate, so the rounded pictures land back on the 30/60 fps grid instead of the grid the median implied.

On the files from the report: 30 fps reads 30 fps, 60 fps reads 60 fps, every frame of the clip is shown once and no frame is repeated.

**Tests**

- `crates/codecs/src/rounded_pts_tests.rs`: a synthetic 90 kHz MOV with durations 2970/3060 and 1440/1530 reads as 30 / 60 fps, and every frame of a 3-second clip is shown exactly once. On `main` it fails with `reads as Some(FrameRate { num: 30303, den: 1000 })` and 30 of 90 frames never shown.
- `crates/codecs/tests/mp4_oracle.rs`: the same clips written by ffmpeg with the report's command (durations 2880–3150 and 1350–1620), checked against the probe and the clip's frame count.
- `crates/time/src/lib.rs`: `FrameRate::from_f64_within` takes the standard rate, and the closest one when two are in range.

The existing variable-rate tests are unchanged: a file that is not a constant rate gone slightly off its grid keeps its own times.

title: fix(codecs): recover fps/frame-grid of ms-rounded phone clips
author: earlvanze
body:
## Summary

Phones and messaging apps round every frame duration to a whole millisecond inside a 90 kHz MP4 track. A 30 fps clip then alternates 33/34 ms frame durations, whose mean is exactly 33.5 ms. Taking just the longer side of that pattern reports **30.303 fps** instead of 30 fps. A 59.94 fps clip with alternating 1501/1502 unit durations at 90 kHz reports a similarly wrong rate instead of `60000/1001`.

## Root cause

The median sample duration is not the nominal frame duration on this millisecond grid: the median lands on the longer side of the alternating pattern and misses the mean.

## Fix

- Compute the mean of the sample durations within one unit of the median.
- Snap that mean to the half-millisecond grid the phone rounder used (round to the nearest 0.5 ms).
- On that grid, derive the reported frame rate integer-exactly from the rounded duration rather than through a float reciprocal that can collapse standard rates to a rational approximation.
- Apply the same derivation in `snap_to_frame_grid`, so the frame grid is rebuilt around the recovered rate instead of a misread float.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p filmcraft-codecs --lib` → 125 passed, 0 failed (was 124 before; the new regression test `rounded_pts_tests::mp4_ms_rounded_frame_times_get_back_to_their_rate` covers 30 fps and 59.94 fps phone fixtures).
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` → clean.
- `cargo xtask layers` → ok.
- `cargo xtask assets` → ok.
- `cargo xtask wasm` → ok.

Resolves https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/issues/1700

Signed-off-by: Earl Co <hello@tekiz.ai>

title: gpu tests: one GPU test at a time in the lib test binary
author: iannitram
body:
## What broke

`cargo test -p filmcraft-gpu --lib` crashes on Linux with RADV some of the time. Each lib test
opens its own wgpu device and submits work, and libtest runs them in parallel. Several tests in the
Vulkan driver at once crash the whole test binary inside `libvulkan.so.1`: a segfault, exit 139,
no test result line. The kernel log shows lines like

    tests::gpu_draw[...]: segfault at 1a4 ... in libvulkan.so.1.4.321

## The fix

A test-only `hold_gpu_lock()` in `crates/gpu/src/tests.rs`: a process-wide mutex that the calling
test thread takes and keeps until the thread exits (libtest gives every test its own thread).
Calling it again on the same thread does nothing. The `device()` helpers (`tests.rs`,
`blend_tests.rs`), the three export renderer tests and the host-adapter test in `adapter.rs` take
it first, so one GPU test talks to the driver at a time. EffectCraft's gpu crate uses the same
pattern (`crates/gpu/src/tests.rs`).

Test code only. Nothing in the library changes.

## What was measured

Machine: ASUS ROG Flow Z13 (Radeon 8060S, Strix Halo), SteamOS, Linux 6.18, Mesa 26.2.0-devel
RADV. The lib test binary was built once without and once with the change, and each was run 10
times on the host:

| | crashed (exit 139) | passed (41/41) |
|---|---|---|
| upstream main cee1feb1 | 7 of 10 | 3 of 10 |
| this branch | 0 of 10 | 10 of 10 |

Three more runs with the change and the `export_pipeline` integration test also passed.
`cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-gpu --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean.
The full workspace `cargo xtask ci` was not run on this machine.

A GPU lib run takes about 1.7 s with the lock instead of about 0.7 s in parallel.

Note: open PR #1284 also edits `crates/gpu/src/export_renderer.rs` (the test module there), so one
of the two may need a small rebase.

title: platform: VA-API H.264 stays in hardware after an open-GOP seek on Mesa radeonsi
author: iannitram
body:
## What broke

On AMD with Mesa radeonsi, H.264 VA-API decoding drops to the software decoder after a seek to an
open-GOP I picture, and stays there for the rest of the stream. On upstream main, the host test
`tests/vaapi.rs` `bit_exact_with_the_software_decoder` fails on this machine with:

    va_h264_open_gop.mp4: stayed in hardware (FilmCraft H.264)

## Why

After a seek to a non-IDR I picture, the frames before it are frame_num gap stand-ins (`vaPutImage`
copies, or mid-gray). They were listed in `ReferenceFrames`, and the leading pictures were
submitted with them in their reference lists. Mesa 26.1.2 radeonsi (VCN dynamic DPB) keeps its own
copy of each picture it decoded and has none for a stand-in. It looks for the decoded references
only among the first `ReferenceFrames` entries (as many as it knows). With stand-ins listed first,
`vaEndPicture` failed (0x1) on the first B picture after the I, and the hybrid decoder went to
software. Giving the firmware pictures that use stand-ins anyway made it fault and reset the VCN ring
on damaged streams.

## The fix

No stand-in is ever a hardware reference:

- `ReferenceFrames` lists only pictures the hardware decoded. Entries that no list uses do not
  change the lists the hardware builds.
- A picture predicted from frames missing at the start of a run is concealed with a copy of the
  latest decoded picture, not submitted. These are the leading pictures of an open-GOP seek, shown
  before the seek point. A `log::debug!` line notes each one.
- A picture predicted from a frame_num gap within the stream is an error ("the hardware decoder does
  not take a picture predicted from a frame_num gap"), so the hybrid decoder replays it in
  software.

Each DPB surface now records what it holds (`Held::Decoded`, `Missing` or `Gap`).

## Tests

- The recording stand-in in `src/vaapi/tests.rs` now checks that every reference it is given is a
  picture the hardware decoded, not a stand-in.
- New `a_picture_predicted_from_a_frame_…

title: macOS DMG: hdiutil create -srcfolder, so the installed app passes codesign --strict
author: Deeev201
body:
## What

The macOS DMG is built with `hdiutil create -srcfolder` instead of `hdiutil makehybrid -hfs` + `convert`, the way VectorCraft (storytold/vectorcraft#1085) and PdfCraft (storytold/pdfcraft#823) already do, with the same five-try `hdiutil_retry` for CI's "Resource busy". After signing, the image is mounted and the app inside is checked with `codesign --verify --strict --deep`, so this can't regress silently.

## Why

`makehybrid -hfs` stamps a `com.apple.FinderInfo` extended attribute on every file in the image. Gatekeeper still accepts the app (`spctl` says "Notarized Developer ID"), but `codesign --verify --strict --deep` on the app in the mounted DMG, or on a copy installed from it with Finder or `ditto`, fails:

```
FilmCraft.app: resource fork, Finder information, or similar detritus not allowed
```

This shows up in the current releases of PhotoCraft, FilmCraft, EffectCraft and DesignCraft (VectorCraft, LightCraft and PdfCraft, which already switched, pass).

## Checked

- `bash -n packaging/macos/package.sh`
- A small signed test bundle packed both ways: `makehybrid -hfs` left FinderInfo on all 7 files and `--strict` failed; `create -srcfolder -fs HFS+` left none and `--strict` passed.
- I couldn't run the full signed/notarized packaging locally (no Developer ID), so CI's packaging job is the real test.

title: Pack opaque SDR export readback on the GPU
author: Gustitolito
body:
Opaque SDR GPU exports currently read back an RGBA16Float accumulator, expand it
to CPU floats, and convert it to RGBA8 for the encoder. This adds transfer and CPU
conversion work even when no post-render operation needs the float image.

This change packs RGBA8 on the GPU with FilmCraft's exact 4096-entry sRGB table,
reducing accumulator readback from 8 to 4 bytes per pixel. It is an optimization
of the existing pipeline, not a replacement encoder or zero-copy implementation.

- Add an optional `FrameRenderer::render_rgba8` hook, wired in desktop and CLI.
- Use it only for opaque SDR with identity placement and no video export effects.
  HDR, alpha, export overlays/limiting and extra resampling retain the float route.
  Timeline effects and burned captions still run normally.
- Initialize packing resources lazily, reuse bounded buffers, check device compute
  limits, and fall back on unsupported or invalid output.
- Explicitly enable native wgpu backends for standalone CLI builds; previously
  `cargo build -p filmcraft-cli` could lack a compositor backend unless desktop or
  test feature unification enabled one.
- Fix the existing renderer test helper to actually insert its video clip, and add
  exact GPU conversion, buffer reuse/limits and full PNG export parity coverage.
- Include a separate prerequisite gate-repair commit: honor `linked: false` in
  `timeline.select`, as already requested by Alt marquee selection; the existing
  `alt_box_selects_only_video_and_delete_keeps_linked_audio` regression exposed the
  ignored parameter. Preserve that individual UI selection when `edit.clear`
  deletes it; explicit command targets retain existing link expansion.
- Update one preexisting Spanish graphics-notice test expectation to match the
  unchanged catalog (`procesamiento por software`); the full workspace gate exposed

- No new dependency, proprietary code/assets, media fixtures or encoder-setting

- Start/centre/end alignments, explicit source ticks, constant speed, reverse and hold frames are covered.
- Malformed edges, NaN/infinite speeds and finite offset overflow are covered without panicking or saturating into invalid timing.

title: Captions: default TTML tick rate follows the frame rate multiplier
author: webdevtodayjason
body:
Follow-up to #1223.

TTML tick offsets now use the effective frame rate times the subframe rate when `tickRate` is omitted, as required by [TTML1 §6.2.10](https://www.w3.org/TR/2018/REC-ttml1-20181108/#parameter-attribute-tickRate). For example, 30 ticks at 30 times 1000/1001 fps imports at 1.001 seconds instead of 1 second. The default rate stays rational, explicit tick rates keep precedence, and oversized arithmetic returns an invalid time expression.

How it was tested:

- The regression fails on unchanged main: `Tick(508032000000)` instead of `Tick(254016000000)` for 50 ticks at 25 times 2 fps.

- `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: pass.

title: Ultra Key: colour-difference matte for green/blue screens; red edges solved from their surroundings
author: Guilhermeb-Ferrarezi
body:
Ultra Key's matte was a distance in Y′CbCr chroma from the key colour. On real green-screen footage that fails in two common ways:

- **Fire, flames, smoke over green.** Yellow flames and the olive their soft edges blend with sit close to a green key in CbCr, so the matte either keeps the olive (a dark green halo on the keyed result, the centre of the screen only half removed) or, with a stronger Setting, eats the flames too.
- **A red/orange foreground (shirt, skin) on green.** Its edge pixels are red mixed with the screen's green: an olive/yellow line that stays opaque, a visible green-yellow outline around the subject.

## What changes

**Colour-difference matte for keys one channel clearly leads** (green and blue screens; `render/src/vfx/color.rs`). A pixel's share of key colour is the lead of the key's channel over the other two, against the key colour's own lead. Flames, skin and anything with no green lead stay opaque; a pixel that is part screen gets the alpha of its foreground share (Transparency pulls these towards transparent, Tolerance sets the share at which a pixel is all background). A partly transparent pixel keeps its own colour with the green spill taken out (Spill Suppression 50, the default, takes out all of the excess), as Premiere Pro does: thin smoke turns a soft grey and the dense parts of a fire stay golden. Keys no single channel leads (cyan, magenta, yellow, grey…) keep the existing chroma-distance matte.

**Edges solved from their surroundings.** The olive edge of a red foreground has the colour of a pure yellow, so no per-pixel rule can separate them without keying yellows too. The pixels a few steps inside the edge are known foreground, though: their average colour is what the edge is made of, so an edge pixel's alpha is where it falls on the line from the key colour to that colour, and its colour becomes that colour. This only runs where the surrounding foreground colour is steady and the soft zone is a thin edge; wide hazes of semi-tr…

title: #1519: Effect Controls selects several effects (Ctrl/Cmd-, Shift-click) and saves them as one preset
author: txiki739
body:
#1519 asks to save several effects as one preset. The engine already supports that: `presets.save` takes a list of effect indices. Effect Controls, however, could select only one effect, so its right-click > Save Preset… always saved a single effect.

## What changes

Effect Controls selects effects as Premiere does:
- **Click** an effect's header to select it alone.
- **Ctrl/Cmd-click** to add an effect to the selection or take one out. Taking out the selected effect hands the selection to the next one.
- **Shift-click** to select the range from the selected effect to the clicked one, in the panel's order (fixed effects first).
- **Right-click > Save Preset…** on a selected effect saves all the selected effects as one preset, in the clip's order. On an effect outside the selection it saves only that one, as before.
- When the preset holds several effects, the Save Preset dialog lists them ("Effects: Gaussian Blur, Mosaic"), with automation id `savePreset.effects`.

## Design

The engine's `selected_effect` is unchanged. Open PR #1319 builds Cut/Copy/Delete on it, and this PR doesn't touch it.

The extra effects live in `UiState::effect_multi_selection`, which is serde and so drivable over the control channel. They are stored together with the effect they were added to (`anchor`) and count only while that is still the engine's selected effect. Any other selection change therefore drops them: an `effects.select` from an agent, a different clip, undo, or a removed effect.

Translations for "Effects: {names}": es, fr, it, ja, pt-BR and zh-CN.

title: perf: auto-scale memory budgets, GOP cache, and GPU upload cache to host RAM/VRAM
author: ProgrammerDSJ
body:
### Summary
This PR introduces dynamic host-RAM memory scaling, bounded GOP decoding budgets, and dual LRU eviction on texture uploads. It resolves memory runaway, pagefile thrashing, and potential OOM crashes on resource-constrained systems (such as 8 GB RAM and 4 GB VRAM laptops) without degrading throughput on high-end workstations.

### Changes
1. **Dynamic Host-RAM Detection (`platform` crate):**
   - Added `platform::system_memory_bytes()` using native OS APIs (`GlobalMemoryStatusEx` on Windows, `sysctl` on macOS, and `/proc/meminfo` on Linux).
2. **Auto-Calibrated Preferences (`engine` crate):**
   - Added `MemoryPrefs::for_total_memory()` to dynamically compute conservative buffer and GOP cache budgets based on installed system RAM.
3. **Bounded GOP Cache (`codecs` crate):**
   - Added `GopCache::set_byte_budget()` with atomic byte tracking to ensure GOP decoding stays within allocated memory bounds across clips.
4. **Bounded Frame Pool (`frame` crate):**
   - Bounded the frame pool shelf capacity by RAM tier to prevent unconstrained buffer accumulation.
5. **GPU Upload LRU Ceiling (`gpu` crate):**
   - Implemented dual LRU eviction (max item count + max byte ceiling) on `GpuCompositor` texture uploads to protect 4 GB GPUs from VRAM exhaustion.
6. **Software Fallback Detection (`ui-egui` crate):**
   - Added detection for Windows Basic Render Driver / WARP to gracefully handle fallback environments.
7. **Attribution:**
   - Added `ProgrammerDSJ` (Devansh Jhanwar) to `contributors/people.toml`.
### Empirical Benchmarks (Windows 11, 8 GB DDR4, 4 GB RTX 2050)
| Scenario | Before PR | After PR | Improvement |
|---|---|---|---|
| **CPU-Only / Fallback** | 1,476 MB RAM / 41% CPU | 1,138 MB RAM / 20% CPU | **-338 MB RAM (-23%)**, **-21% CPU (51% drop!)** |
| **GPU Accelerated** | 702 MB RAM / 10% CPU | 723 MB RAM / 10% CPU | Parity within margin of error, with active safety bounds |

title: ui-egui: the UI tests as one test program
author: seif9116
body:
Every file in `crates/ui-egui/tests/` was a test program of its own, and each one links the whole app. `cargo xtask ci` runs `cargo test --workspace --release`, and the release profile has `lto = "thin"`, so each of the 78 programs also ran its own LTO pass over the app. Building the UI tests took hours, while running them takes about two minutes.

## What changes

- The 78 files move unchanged into `crates/ui-egui/tests/ui/`. `tests/ui/main.rs` names each one as a module, so Cargo builds them as one test target, `ui`.
- `every_ui_test_file_is_a_module` (in `main.rs`) fails in two cases:
  - a file in `tests/ui/` has no `mod` line, so it would never build or run
  - a new `.rs` file lands in `tests/` itself, where it would be a program of its own again. A file that really needs its own process can be listed in `OWN_PROGRAM`.
- Docs and doc comments that name a test file or `--test <file>` point at the new place. For example, `--test scripted -- --ignored screenshots` becomes `--test ui -- --ignored scripted::screenshots`, and one file's tests are `--test ui color_ui::`. `docs/testing.md` explains the layout.

## Numbers

Measured on 0.7.2, which had 75 files. 4 cores, Ubuntu 22.04, Rust 1.99, `cargo test --release` with `CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_CODEGEN_UNITS=16`:

| | 75 programs | one program |
|---|---|---|
| build every UI test after a change to the library | about 3.5 h | 16 min |
| build after a change to one test file | 2 min 47 s | 3 min 4 s |
| run them | 130 s | 119 s |
| size in `target/release/deps` | 75 × about 91 MB (6.8 GB) | 99 MB |

Each program cost about 590 CPU seconds, nearly all of it LTO. The profile's own `codegen-units = 1` makes that pass slower still, so the gap under `cargo xtask ci` should be larger. The cost is that editing one test file rebuilds the whole UI test crate, 17 s more in this run.

The same 412 tests passed and 4 were ignored in both layouts. No test needed a process of its own: the tests already ran on parallel threads within…

title: Hostile-input hammer for container crates; 3 panic fixes
author: g1obalworlds
body:
Adds a deterministic mutation hammer (`filmcraft_testkit::hostile::hammer`: every truncation, bit flips, 1/2/4/8-byte extreme-value overwrites in both endiannesses, deletions; each run under catch_unwind with a 5 s budget; `FILMCRAFT_HOSTILE_MULT=N` for soak runs) and applies it to mpegts, isobmff, matroska, avi, mxf, ogg, cfb and format.

## Bugs found and fixed (each has a regression test that panicked before)
- **ogg** `OpusTiming::of` (lib.rs): i64 arithmetic on file-supplied granule positions overflowed (`attempt to subtract with overflow`), e.g. granule i64::MIN/MAX on an Opus page. Now saturating. Test: `extreme_granules_do_not_overflow_opus_timing`.
- **mxf** `EssenceTrack::sync_before` (file.rs): indexed `samples[0]` when a track has no samples (reachable on files with sound chunks but no samples). Now `get()`. Test: `sync_before_on_an_empty_track`.
- **format** `autosave::civil`: `unix + offset` overflowed for extreme timestamps. Now saturating. Test: `autosave_timestamps_survive_extreme_clocks`.

## Clean (no real bug found)
mpegts (TS/M2TS/PS + es frame parsers), isobmff, matroska (all lacing modes, demuxer seek/index), avi (idx1, rec, OpenDML), cfb, and project decode (every numeric token replaced by extremes, deep nesting): no panics, hangs or slow runs at 15x default iterations.

## Notes
- cfb and format gain `filmcraft-testkit` as a dev-dependency (no cycles; `cargo xtask layers` ok).
- Gates run: fmt, clippy -D warnings, tests for touched crates, layers.

title: Hostile-input hardening for video decoders (AV1 panic + oversize allocation, MPEG-2 allocation) and fuzz tests
author: g1obalworlds
body:
Mutation-fuzz sweeps (truncate at every length, every header byte to 0/0xff/0x80/0x01/0x7f, every bit flip, random mutation; panics in decoder worker threads are counted too) over h264, hevc, vp8, vp9, av1, mpeg2v, apv, prores and dnx.

## Bugs found and fixed
1. **av1 panic** (`crates/av1/src/tile.rs`, `get_tx_size`: index out of bounds, len 22 index 22). Input: a 4:2:0 stream with the sequence profile bit flipped (4:2:2). Blocks such as 4x16 then have no chroma size (`BLOCK_INVALID`), which indexed `MAX_TX_SIZE_RECT`. Fix: `decode_block` returns `Error::Invalid` when `plane_residual_size(sub_size, 1) == BLOCK_INVALID` (a spec conformance requirement). Regression: `block_without_chroma_size_is_an_error_not_a_panic` (659-byte embedded stream; panicked before).
2. **av1 giant allocation** (`decoder.rs`): frame sizes up to 65536x65536 were accepted, so a few header bytes asked for gigabytes. Now capped at 16384 per side and 2^27 samples (level 6.3 tops out at 16384x8704). Regression: `hostile_dims.rs` (hand-built reduced still-picture stream; 65536x16 was decoded to a picture before).
3. **mpeg2v giant allocation** (`lib.rs`, `Seq::new`): 16383x16383 4:4:4 sequences (~800 MB per frame plus references and the gray frame; the fuzz run peaked at 1.7 GB RSS). Area capped at 2^25 (8K UHD still fits). Regression: `gigantic_sequences_are_refused` (failed before).

## Clean
h264, hevc, vp8, vp9, apv, prores, dnx: no panic, hang or runaway allocation found (long runs of 15k to 60k random mutations per seed, debug build with overflow checks). The new tests stay in as regression guards. `FILMCRAFT_FUZZ_ITERS=n` raises the random rounds for a longer hunt.

## Tests
- `fuzz_hostile.rs` in each crate (ffmpeg-generated seeds go to `target/fixtures`, skipped without ffmpeg; dnx/apv/prores use their own encoders).
- vp8 and vp9 gain `filmcraft-testkit` as a dev-dependency.
- fmt, clippy `-D warnings` and `cargo test` for all nine crates, `cargo xtask layers`: green.

The Source monitor's waveform (`monitor_view::waveform`) always spread the whole clip across its width and never looked at the monitor's time zoom range, so dragging the zoom bar under the ruler changed the ruler but left the waveform exactly as it was. title: #1061: watchdog for a graphics start that hangs: save the next mode, and the next launch ends the stuck start
author: liangforstudy
body:
A graphics driver can hang inside wgpu instance, adapter or device creation instead of crashing. The process lives on with no window and no crash log. The start-up ladder from #827 only counts starts that *died*, so it never moved on, and every launch hung the same way (#1061, probably #1038).

**What this does:**
1. A watchdog gives the graphics device 30 s from launch.
2. If it still isn't there, the hang is logged in `filmcraft.log` and the crash log, and the next mode (DirectX 12, then software) is saved at once, like a reported start-up error.
3. The stuck process also leaves a marker, `graphics-hung/<pid>.json`, with its launch time.
4. The next launch reads the markers **before** loading the graphics driver and ends those stuck processes. Then it opens in the saved mode, with the existing fallback notice and its reset button.

**Why the next launch does the ending:** the stuck process can't recover or end itself. On the test laptop it couldn't start a new process or `abort()`, most likely because of the Windows loader lock the driver holds. Another process ends it instantly.

**`crates/platform/src/stuck_process.rs`** (the only `unsafe`):
- `end_stuck_process` uses `OpenProcess`, `QueryFullProcessImageNameW`, `GetProcessTimes` and `TerminateProcess`, which needs the `Win32_System_Threading` feature.
- It only ends a process that is **still the same executable and was created when the marker says**. A reused process id (another program, or a FilmCraft that started fine) is left alone.
- Like `cursor`, it's a non-media OS call kept in the one crate allowed `unsafe` (AGENTS.md §0.3, ADR 0001). It has a safe `Result` API and a `// SAFETY:` comment on each `unsafe` block, and it does nothing outside Windows.

**What it doesn't cover:**
- Hangs after the graphics device exists (first paint, opening a project). The watchdog stands down there on purpose, so a slow project load isn't mistaken for a driver hang.
- A mode picked by hand (`--graphics`, `WGPU_BACKEND`), a…

title: Windows: guard initial AV1 color metadata for hardware decoding
author: jahvari

title: codecs: eliminate gap/dropout clicks in Matroska PCM audio playback
author: woldercraft
body:
### Problem
In Matroska containers, block timestamps are quantized to `TimestampScale` (usually 1 ms). For 48 kHz audio with 1024-sample blocks (~21.33 ms), timestamps round to 0, 21, 43, 64 ms...
While `contiguous_starts` was previously implemented for AAC, MP3, MP2, AC-3 and E-AC-3 (#236), `Codec::Pcm` was omitted and placed blocks directly at raw rounded timestamp positions.
As a result, PCM audio (such as OBS recordings with uncompressed 16-bit or 24-bit audio tracks) experienced periodic 16-sample overwrites and 32-sample gaps of silence every ~40 ms, audible as constant harmonic clicks and distortion during timeline playback and export.
### Fix
- Updated `crates/codecs/src/mkv.rs`: calculate sample count per block for `Codec::Pcm` (`(size + prefix_len) / (bps * channels)`) and pass packets through `contiguous_starts`.
- Updated `crates/codecs/tests/matroska_audio_oracle.rs`: added `tone_pcm24_48k.mkv` and `tone_pcm16_48k.mkv` test cases.
- Added contributor entry in `contributors/people.toml`.
### Validation
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-codecs --test matroska_audio_oracle`: both PCM fixtures pass with max second difference matching FFmpeg's reference decode (`0.00183 vs 0.00183`).
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy` passed cleanly with 0 warnings.

title: Fonts: faces with no outline tables are no longer listed
author: dotCooCoo
body:
`read_face` (`crates/text/src/sfnt.rs`) returns a face for every TrueType or OpenType face whose `name` table gives a family name, so the font database also lists faces with none of the tables skrifa reads glyph outlines from (`glyf`, `CFF `, `CFF2`, `VARC`), such as faces whose glyphs are bitmaps only or whose outlines are in Apple's `hvgl` table. The renderer draws glyphs only from those outlines (`outline` in `crates/text/src/render.rs`), so text set in such a face is blank. On macOS 27.0.1 the system scan lists "GB18030 Bitmap" (`/System/Library/Fonts/Supplemental/NISC18030.ttf`, `bdat` bitmaps), so it appears in the Font menus and in `fonts.list`. "中文字体" set in it at 48 px maps to four of its glyphs, the layout reports no missing font, and `render::draw` leaves the mask empty.

- `read_face` now returns no face when the table directory has none of those four tables (`OUTLINE_TABLES`). The check runs before the `name` table is read.
- The system scan, the bundled fonts, craft-fonts and `add_font_data` all read faces through it. The bundled faces and the craft-fonts faces (at `8dcdacd`) each have one of the tables and are listed as before.
- In a collection, the faces with outlines are still listed, each with its own index.

VectorCraft's font scan has the same check (https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/pull/781), and https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/pull/443 adds it to DesignCraft.

With the change, the scan on the same Mac adds 850 system faces instead of 851, and "GB18030 Bitmap" is the one left out. Text set in it is reported as a missing font and falls back to Inter, as text in any other missing family does.

Test: `sfnt::tests::faces_without_outline_tables_are_left_out` renames the `glyf` record of a copy of Inter Regular in memory. It checks that skrifa reads no outline for 'A' in the copy, that `read_faces_bytes` lists no face for the copy and one for the original, and that a two-face collection built in memory from both lists only the origin…

Two commits, one feature: FilmCraft could not read or write an uncompressed QuickTime movie. This is the `docs/codec-parity.md` row “Uncompressed / v210 / RGB — decode + encode (AVI, MOV): partial (MOV PCM-style video not verified) / none”.

**What happened**

`2vuy` (8-bit 4:2:2), `v210` (10-bit 4:2:2) and `raw ` (24-bit RGB) sample entries parsed as `CodecConfig::Unknown`: an imported uncompressed `.mov` opened with a picture of codec “unknown” and failed to read a frame, though the AVI layouts (UYVY, RGB) have decoded for a long time. On the export side there was no format at all that kept the picture uncompressed.

`raw ` also names 8-bit PCM in a sound track, and the fourcc list won that test: an ffmpeg `-c:a pcm_u8` movie (fourcc `raw `, handler `soun`) was read as a *visual* sample entry and did not even open — `decode error: container: truncated data while reading sample entry`. title: fix(codecs): read the frame rate phone clips average to (#1700)
author: earlvanze
body:
Closes #1700.

## Problem

`New Sequence From Clip` inferred the rate from the median MP4 sample duration. Some phone/messaging-app writers stamp frame times rounded to whole milliseconds inside a 90 kHz track. A nominal 30 fps clip therefore alternates 33 ms and 34 ms durations (2970 and 3060 units), whose median reads as 30.303 fps; a nominal 60 fps clip can read as 58.824 fps. Frame-grid snapping used the same median-based estimate, so import could drop frames as well as label the sequence incorrectly.

## Fix

- Derive a track's nominal rate as the mean of positive sample durations within a quarter frame of the median. The near-median durations are the two quantized sides of the normal frame period, so their mean recovers 3000/1500 units.
- Snap near-standard means to the closest common standard rate when within 0.5% of that standard rate; otherwise retain the measured rate.
- Reuse the same `nominal_rate` helper for media probing and frame-grid snapping so they cannot disagree.
- Add writer-based synthetic 30/60 fps regression fixtures with whole-millisecond-rounded frame times.

## Testing

- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-time -p filmcraft-codecs --lib`
- `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-time -p filmcraft-codecs --all-targets -- -D warnings`

The broader workspace test run passed the relevant crates and reached an unrelated pre-existing failure in `apps/filmcraft` comparing against a locally modified packaged `.desktop` file. No ffmpeg fixture is required: the synthetic MP4/MOV writer directly reproduces the quantized timestamps.

title: fix(codecs): read AC-3/E-AC-3 MP4 layout from dac3/dec3 (#1701)
author: earlvanze
body:
## Summary
- Read the AC-3/E-AC-3 program channel count from the codec-specific `dac3` / `dec3` descriptors instead of the mandated stereo sample-entry count, matching FFmpeg's MP4 reader.
- When no usable descriptor exists, keep the existing parser fallback, but only trust the first packet for E-AC-3 when it is a primary independent substream.
- Add MP4 oracle coverage for 5.1 AC-3 and E-AC-3, descriptor-only stereo entries, and descriptor-less primary-frame fallback.

## Root cause
ISO-BMFF AC-3/E-AC-3 sample entries advertise two channels, while the true layout lives in the `dac3` / `dec3` payload. `Mp4Source::info()` used the sample-entry count, so ffmpeg-created 5.1 MP4s reported two channels. The `dac3` decode now follows FFmpeg's `mov_read_dac3` (`acmod = bit 11`, `lfeon = bit 10`), and `dec3` follows `mov_read_dec3`'s 24-bit field beginning at byte 2.

## Testing
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-codecs --test ac3_mp4_layout`
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-codecs --test eac3_oracle`
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-codecs`
- `cargo fmt --check -p filmcraft-codecs`
- `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-codecs -p filmcraft-isobmff --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`

Closes #1701.

title: captions: keep TTML cue IDs unique and preserve valid Unicode
author: sanyamsingh001
body:
TTML and DFXP exports could emit duplicate XML IDs or replace valid Unicode cue IDs. A cue named `s1` could collide with the document’s style ID, and a generated `c1` could take an ID belonging to a later cue.

The writer now reserves valid explicit cue IDs before generating replacements for missing, invalid or repeated IDs. Style, region, cue and speaker IDs remain unique across the document. Valid Unicode IDs retain their exact spelling, including combining characters, under these collision rules. Speaker IDs are allocated after cue IDs, preserving a valid cue named `agent1`.

The README documents the behavior and the [Namespaces in XML 1.0 Third Edition](https://www.w3.org/TR/2009/REC-xml-names-20091208/#NT-NCName) and [XML 1.0 Fifth Edition](https://www.w3.org/TR/2008/REC-xml-20081126/#NT-NameStartChar) character rules.

title: interchange: overflow-safe FCPXML times and FCP7 timebases, mutation-fuzz harness
author: ahmed0magdy
body:
Two integer overflows in the interchange importers, found by a new mutation-fuzz test (AGENTS.md §0 asks parsers to have one). Both fixes come with regression tests that panicked before the fix.

## Fixes

- **FCPXML time parsing** (`parse_time`, `crates/interchange/src/fcpxml.rs`):
  - A time such as `"99999999999999999999s"` or `"<huge>/1s"` overflowed. Debug builds panicked; release builds silently wrapped to a wrong tick count.
  - It now uses checked arithmetic and returns `None`, so the value is treated like any other unreadable time: callers fall back to `Tick::ZERO`, or skip the keyframe, as they already do.
  - Regression test: `fcpxml::tests::times_too_long_are_rejected`.
- **FCP7 XML rate parsing** (`rate_from_timebase`, `crates/interchange/src/common.rs`):
  - A hostile NTSC `<timebase>` overflowed `timebase * 1000`. It now saturates.
  - Regression test: new assertions in `common::tests::rates`.

## Fuzz test

`crates/interchange/tests/fuzz.rs`: mutated EDL, FCP7 XML, FCPXML, OTIO, AAF, OMF and ALE files must import without panicking, checked under `catch_unwind`.

- **Mutations:** truncation, bit flips, hostile numbers, removed or duplicated spans, and hostile 32-bit sizes.
- **Default run:** 2,000 mutations per format.

title: #1545: effects.apply answers with the applied instances (clip, index, effect)
author: 00xJS
body:
Fixes the third point of #1545: `effects.apply` answered `null`, so an agent had to call `sequence_inspect` and search the clip's effect list to find the index it had just created before it could `effects.setParam` or `effects.remove` it.

It now answers `{"applied":[{"clip":id,"index":n,"effect":id}]}`, one entry per instance it added, in the same spirit as `timeline.place` (`{"clips":[..]}`) and `file.newSequence` (`{"sequence":n}`). For an audio effect applied through a video clip, `clip` is the linked audio clip the effect was retargeted to, so the answer always names the clip that really holds the instance. Transitions applied through `effects.apply` keep their existing `{"transition":id}` answer.

No behaviour of the edit itself changes; every existing caller ignores the result (the UI uses `let _ =`), and the parameter doc string is unchanged so the `cmd!` line stays within `max_width`.

Test: `effects_apply_reports_where_each_instance_landed` in `crates/engine/src/vfx_tests.rs` checks the index addresses the new instance and is usable by `effects.remove` at once, one entry per clip for several clips, and the audio retarget case.

Gates run locally on Windows 11 (x86_64, Rust 1.99): `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --release -p filmcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --release -p filmcraft-engine effects_apply`.

title: #1591: file_url_to_path probes for localhost with get, not a byte slice (Unicode URLs panicked)
author: 00xJS
body:
Fixes #1591. `file_url_to_path` checked for a `localhost` host with `rest[..9]`, a byte slice; when a multi-byte character fell within the first nine bytes after `file://` (`file:///日本語.mov`, `file://srv/日本語.mov`) the slice landed inside a character and panicked with "byte index 9 is not a char boundary", so an EDL (or any interchange document) naming such a file could not be imported.

The probe now uses `str::get(..9)`, which answers `None` instead of panicking when byte 9 is not a boundary; such a URL cannot be the `localhost` form anyway. Nothing else in the function slices by byte offset that an input could move: `url[7..]` follows a successful `get(..7)` match of the ASCII scheme, and `decoded[1..]` follows `starts_with('/')`.

Test: `unicode_urls_do_not_panic` in `crates/interchange/src/common.rs` covers the two reported URLs, a short host, a host entirely of multi-byte characters, `localhost` in both cases followed by Unicode, and the empty `file://`. The first two panic before the fix.

Gates run locally on Windows 11 (x86_64, Rust 1.99): `cargo fmt --check -p filmcraft-interchange`, `cargo test --release -p filmcraft-interchange`.

title: #1565: image sequences with a non-ASCII character before the frame number no longer panic
author: 00xJS
body:
Fixes #1565. `Numbered::parse` found the character before the frame number with `rfind` and took the digits from `i + 1`, assuming that character is one byte. For `é0001.png`, `日本語0012.png` or an emoji before the number, `i + 1` is inside the character and the slice panicked with "byte index 1 is not a char boundary", so a valid image sequence with a non-ASCII name could not be imported.

The start of the digit run is now `i + len_utf8` of the character at `i`. `number_of` needed no change: it compares the suffix as bytes with ASCII case folding, which never changes a byte count, so its cut stays on a boundary.

Test: `unicode_prefix_before_the_number` in `crates/media/src/sequence.rs` covers accented, CJK, emoji and decomposed (`e` + combining acute) prefixes, a non-ASCII character earlier in the name, the parsed file naming itself and its next sibling through `number_of` / `file_name`, and a Unicode name without digits. The accented, CJK, emoji and decomposed cases panic before the fix.

Gates run locally on Windows 11 (x86_64, Rust 1.99): `cargo fmt --check -p filmcraft-media`, `cargo test --release -p filmcraft-media`, `cargo test --release -p filmcraft-engine image_sequence`.

title: #1687: FCP7 XML clip edges under a transition come from the neighbouring transitionitem
author: 00xJS
body:
Fixes #1687. In FCP 7 XML a clip edge that sits under a transition is written as `-1`: the neighbouring `transitionitem` defines it. Premiere and Resolve both write it this way. The importer treated `-1` as "missing": one `-1` edge was recovered from the clip's source length, two `-1` edges skipped the clip, and the dissolves next to it were then skipped for want of an adjacent clip. A six-piece cut from Resolve came in with two pieces and holes.

The clip edge is now resolved from the adjacent `transitionitem` sibling: the transition's cut, which is its middle for `center` (the default), its start for `start` / `start-black`, its end for `end` / `end-black`. A clip whose start was defined that way has its `in` / `out` moved up by the handle between the transition's start and the cut, because the document's `in` is the source at the transition's start (the clip's first frame under the dissolve), not at the cut. Resolve's API readback of the reporter's timeline confirms both rules: the six pieces land at 54 / 252 / 291 / 607 / 833 / 909 with source ins 589 / 795 / 841 / 1176 / 1787 / 1876, exactly as before.

One existing expectation changes: in `golden_premiere_style_nested_and_transitions` the clip after the centred 36–60 dissolve (`in` 100) now has `source_in` 112, the source at the cut, instead of 100, the source at the dissolve's start. The clip's place and length are unchanged, as is everything the exporter writes (it always writes explicit edges, so round trips are unaffected).

Test: `transition_defined_clip_edges_come_from_the_neighbouring_transition` in `crates/interchange/tests/fcp7.rs` rebuilds the reporter's Resolve 21 track (six takes, five centred 12-frame dissolves, four clips with both edges at `-1`) and checks every place, end, source in, and that all five dissolves join their two takes. Before the fix four clips and three dissolves are skipped.

title: #1593: the Timeline zooms out no farther than its whole extent in view
author: 00xJS
body:
Fixes #1593. Every zoom path clamped the Timeline's zoom to a fixed floor of 0.05 points a second, so zooming all the way out showed hours of empty space: a 38 s sequence ended up a few points wide, an empty one showed eight hours, although the Timeline's extent is the sequence plus ten minutes.

One lower bound now, `timeline::min_pps(sequence_seconds, width)`: the view's width divided by `timeline_extent`, so the farthest zoom-out shows the whole extent and no more, and the zoom bar's thumb fills its track there. It is applied where the zoom is applied with the view and sequence at hand (`zoom_about` for the keys, Zoom to Sequence, the zoom bar's handles), and once per frame in the animation step, which covers the wheel, pinch, the Zoom tool and the control channel's `ui.set timeline.pps` without each needing the view width. The ceiling is unchanged (`MAX_PPS`, 24 000). A very long sequence may now zoom out further than 0.05 allowed, since the floor follows its extent.

Tests: `zoom_floor_tests` in `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/timeline.rs`: for 0 s, 38 s, 10 min and 8 h the floor puts exactly the extent in a 1000-point view, the 38 s sequence covers the first sixteenth of it, degenerate widths never give a zero or infinite zoom, and repeated zoom-out through `zoom_about` stops at the floor with the scroll at 0 while zoom-in stops at the ceiling.

Gates run locally on Windows 11 (x86_64, Rust 1.99): `cargo fmt --check -p filmcraft-ui-egui`, `cargo test --release -p filmcraft-ui-egui --lib timeline`.

title: #905: the Hard Limiter's Look-Ahead Time sets how early the gain falls
author: 00xJS
body:
Fixes #905. The Hard Limiter effect offers Look-Ahead Time (0–30 ms, default 7 ms), but the DSP limiter had a fixed 5 ms window and the effect mapping never passed the parameter, so the control did nothing.

The limiter now takes a `lookahead` parameter (0–30 ms, DSP default 5 ms, so every other user of `Limiter`, such as the export loudness limiter, behaves as before) and the Hard Limiter mapping passes the effect's Look-Ahead Time to it.

Design note: an effect's latency must not depend on its parameters (`premiere_tests::latency_is_fixed...` checks it, and `audio_fx::latency_of` measures a fresh instance once for the mixer's compensation). So the delay line is always the longest look-ahead, 30 ms, and the parameter sets only the length of the gain ramp (the moving average) before a peak. The sliding minimum holds a peak's gain for as long as the peak sits in the delay line, so the ramp always completes exactly when the peak comes out, whatever its length: 0 ms is a brick-wall step at the peak, 30 ms a gentle fall starting 30 ms earlier. Release timing relative to the peak's exit is unchanged. Changing the look-ahead mid-stream resizes the moving average seeded with the current gain, so the output does not step.

Cost: the limiter's latency grows from 5 ms to 30 ms plus the true-peak filter delay. The mixer and the export loudness path already compensate it (`latency()`), and the existing latency / transparency tests pass unchanged.

Test: `limiter_lookahead_sets_how_early_the_gain_falls` (a quiet 997 Hz sine with a 1 ms pulse at 0.25 s, the scenario from the report): with 0 ms the sine in the 5 ms before the pulse comes out is untouched; with 30 ms the gain has already fallen there; 7 ms sits between; both limit the pulse to the ceiling; the latency is identical for all three. Before the fix the three runs are indistinguishable.

title: #1540: engine.execute over the control channel never opens a parameter dialog
author: 00xJS
body:
Fixes the first half of #1540. Over the control channel, `engine.execute {"command":"sequence.settings","params":{}}` opened the Sequence Settings dialog in the app window, which an agent can neither see (it is not in `ui.elements`) nor close; the same went for every command whose menu form asks for its parameters in a dialog (Add Tracks…, Delete Tracks…, Audio Gain…, Interpret Footage…, Remix Properties…, New Sequence…, Color Management…).

`engine.execute` now never opens a parameter dialog. `control::handle` marks the call (`FilmcraftApp::engine_call`) and `menus::invoke` skips the dialog branches for it, so the engine command runs with the parameters given: `sequence.addTracks {}` adds its documented default track, `clip.audioGain {}` answers "need `db`", and `sequence.settings {}` answers `{"settings"}`, the active sequence's settings as `sequence.inspect` reports them, which is what the reporter expected. Menus, shortcuts and `ui.menu.invoke` are unchanged and still open the dialogs; the confirmations (`file.revert`, `file.recover`) still ask either way, since they guard against losing work. Documented in `docs/control-protocol.md`.

The second half of the report, listing an open dialog in `ui.elements` so an agent could close one, is not in this change.

Test: `engine_execute_never_opens_a_parameter_dialog` in `crates/ui-egui/tests/scripted.rs`: `sequence.settings {}` answers the settings and opens nothing; `clip.audioGain {}` fails as the engine command and opens nothing; `sequence.settings` with a parameter still applies; `ui.menu.invoke` of `sequence.settings` still opens the dialog.

Gates run locally on Windows 11 (x86_64, Rust 1.99): `cargo fmt --check -p filmcraft-ui-egui`, `cargo test --release -p filmcraft-ui-egui --test scripted --test menus_ui --test clip_dialogs_ui`.

author: vbasky
body:

title: #1675: keyframes on a Frame Hold clip go where the playhead is (they all landed on the held frame)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Refs #1675.

This is the one case I could reproduce where Add/Remove Keyframe fails; if your clip had a Frame Hold this fixes it, otherwise I'd need the steps.

On a clip with a Frame Hold (Hold Filters off) the keyframe commands took the playhead's time from `source_time_at`, which stays on the held frame. Every click of Add/Remove Keyframe landed on the same instant, so the second one removed the first and turned animation off, while the render kept animating through the hold with `effect_time_at`. The keyframe commands (`effects.addKeyframe` and friends, `toggleAnimation`, `setParam`, `reset`, `resetParam`) and the Effect Controls / Properties panels now use `effect_time_at`, the time the render uses, so the diamond, the navigator and the keyframe that gets written agree. With Hold Filters on, `effect_time_at` still returns the held frame, so that behaviour doesn't change.

A possible follow-up, left alone here: removing the last keyframe with Add/Remove Keyframe also turns the stopwatch off (`is_animated` is "has keyframes"), whereas in Premiere the stopwatch stays on. Happy to look at it if you want it.

Also left as they are: Lumetri, the masks panel, the audio effects editor and the Program monitor's transform handles still read effect values at `source_time_at`, so on a held clip they show the held frame's values rather than the animated ones. Same one-line change in each; happy to add them here or send them separately.

Validation:
- `keyframes_on_a_frame_hold_go_where_the_playhead_is` (engine): fails on main (`left: (0, 50.0)`, `right: (2, 100.0)`: no keyframes left), passes here, also run on its own
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-engine --lib keyframe` and `frame_hold`, `cargo test -p filmcraft-ui-egui --lib effect_controls`
- `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-engine -p filmcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: #1831: proxy and transcode jobs run one at a time, in the order they were asked for
author: Guilhermeb-Ferrarezi
body:
Refs #1831

Asking for a proxy while another one was still encoding started a second background export right away. Each export already uses every core and holds decoded frames, so several at once only slow each other down and multiply the memory in use. The report asks for them to go into a queue.

## What changes

- New `media_queue` (first-in first-out line). `start_job` in `proxies.rs` takes a place in it when a media job is started, so the order is the order of the clicks, and the job waits for its turn on its own thread. It covers `media.createProxies`, ingest transcodes and every other job built on `start_job`.
- While it waits, the job list shows `Waiting for N earlier job(s)` and no progress.
- A job cancelled while it waits gives its place up and does not hold up the ones behind it. A ticket that is dropped out of order is skipped when its turn comes.
- A job that is waited on (`wait: true`) takes its turn in the line as well, so a CLI call never runs next to a background job.
- The web build (no threads) is unchanged.

## What I could not reproduce

The report also mentions "smaller ratio proxy files". I did not find a cause for that; each transcode takes its size and preset from its own item and settings, so I think it is a separate problem (or came from the machine running out of memory with several encodes at once). That is why this says `Refs` and not `Fixes`.

## Tests

- `media_queue`: jobs run one at a time and in ticket order even when their threads start in the wrong order; a job cancelled while waiting does not stall the line; a ticket dropped out of order is skipped.
- `proxies_tests::proxy_jobs_wait_in_line_and_run_in_order`: with the line held, two `media.createProxies` jobs both report `Waiting for…` and encode nothing; once it is released both finish, both proxies are attached, and the second proxy file was created after the first was written. It fails if the `wait` in `start_job` is removed (checked).
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-engine`: 637…

title: #1381: the Warp Stabilizer analyses a clip a block of frames at a time
author: Guilhermeb-Ferrarezi
body:
Refs #1381

Warp Stabilizer's first-use analysis decoded every frame of the clip, built the tracking pyramid of each one (`Prepared`, 4 levels of f32 gray), and kept all of them until the steps between frames were known. Memory grew with the length of the clip: about 0.7 MB per frame at the default 480 px analysis width and about 2.8 MB at Detailed (960 px). A 10-minute clip at 30 fps is 18,000 frames, so tens of gigabytes, which ends the process. The report says the crash is worse on long 4K clips.

## What changes

- `chunked_steps` works through the clip 64 frames at a time (`ANALYSIS_BLOCK`): the block is decoded and prepared in parallel as before, the steps inside it (plus the one joining it to the previous block) are tracked in parallel, and the frames are dropped. Only the last frame of a block is kept for the next one.
- The result is the same as before: the same steps, the same analysis size (taken from the first readable frame), identity steps for unreadable frames and for frames whose width differs from their neighbour, and `None` when nothing could be read or the analysis was cancelled (checked between blocks and per frame, as before).
- Nothing else about the effect changes; the cache key, the smoothing and the rendering are untouched.

## What this does not do

The report also asks for the analysis to run in the background so the UI stays usable (clicking during the analysis hangs the window). That is a different change (the analysis runs inside the first rendered frame, so it needs a job and a progress state) and is not part of this one, which is why this says `Refs` and not `Fixes`. I did not have an 18,000-frame clip to measure; the memory bound is shown by a test that counts how many frames are alive at once.

## Tests

- `the_steps_do_not_depend_on_the_block_size`: 37 frames give identical steps for block sizes 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 36, 37, 38 and 1000.
- `unreadable_and_resized_frames_give_identity_steps_and_the_first_size_is_used`: frames missing at th…

title: perf: Warp Stabilizer works out the corrections of a clip once per set of settings
author: Guilhermeb-Ferrarezi
body:
Warp Stabilizer worked out the correction of every frame of the clip, and the zoom that hides the worst border, again for every frame it rendered. That is the smoothing of the whole analysed path, so the cost of one rendered frame grows with the length of the clip, on every frame of playback and of an export.

## Measured

`corrections` plus the worst `cover_scale` scan on a synthetic path (Smoothness 15 frames at 30 fps), `cargo test --release`, Windows 11, 20 threads:

| clip | frames | work repeated on every rendered frame |
|---|---|---|
| 30 s | 900 | 0.79 ms |
| 2 min | 3,600 | 6.8 ms |
| 10 min | 18,000 | 14.8 ms |

Playback has 33 ms per frame at 30 fps, so on a long clip this is a large share of it before the picture is even warped, and a 10-minute export spends about 4.5 minutes of render-thread time on it.

## What changes

- `corrected(path, smoothness, result, preserve_scale)` keeps the corrections (and, per zoom limit, the worst border) of one analysed path for one set of settings in a small cache, so frames after the first one only look them up. `warp_stabilizer` uses it for both framings that need the worst border (Crop Less Smooth Motion and Auto-scale).
- The cache is keyed by the path's `Arc` address and holds that `Arc`, so the address can't be reused by another path while the entry exists. It keeps at most 16 entries and clears itself beyond that, so a keyframed Smoothness (a new value on every frame, as slow as before) doesn't make it grow.
- The numbers are the same as before: the cache calls the existing `corrections` and `cover_scale`.

## Tests

- The same path and settings return the same cached corrections (`Arc::ptr_eq`), equal to `corrections` number for number.
- Another Smoothness, Result, Preserve Scale or another path gets its own entry, and the first entry is still there.
- The cached worst border equals a direct scan for zoom limits 1, 1.2, 1.5 and 4.
- 100 different Smoothness values stay correct and the cache stays bounded.
- Th…

title: PNG Sequence writes RGB files when Include Alpha Channel is off
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1863.

The PNG branch of `encode_still_with` always wrote `Rgba8` and ignored the `alpha` flag that the TIFF, Targa and OpenEXR branches already honour, so an alpha-off PNG Sequence was flattened over black but still carried a constant 255 alpha channel (colour type 6). With alpha off it now writes 8-bit RGB (colour type 2), reusing `raster::rgb` like the JPEG branch. `encode_png` (thumbnails, previews, graphic templates) and the 8-bit PNG Export Frame used to rely on "PNG always keeps alpha" while passing `false`, so they now pass `true` explicitly and keep writing RGBA as before. `estimate_bytes` counts three channels for PNG when alpha is off, following the TIFF fix from #908.
