title: fix(macOS): show file dialogs as sheets instead of a nested modal run loop (#2018)
author: vark-debug
body:
Closes #2018.

## Root cause

On macOS, the synchronous `rfd::FileDialog::pick_file` runs the `NSOpenPanel` with `run_modal` — a nested, blocking run loop — inside the winit event-handling scope (Lumetri ▸ Input LUT ▸ Browse… → `show_lut_dialog` → `FileDialog::run_now`).

While that modal loop is running, a Finder drag onto the open panel queues a winit event. winit's `maybe_queue_event` sees that an event is currently being handled and posts the deferred `handle_event` call as a block on the common modes of the host `CFRunLoop`. The nested modal loop executes those blocks, so `ApplicationDelegate::handle_event` re-enters while the outer `handle_event` still holds the `RefCell` borrow — the re-entrancy guard panics. Because the deferred block was scheduled by winit as `panic_cannot_unwind`, the panic is not catchable by the UI's `catch_unwind` guard and the process aborts (SIGABRT).

This matches the reporter's observation (crash log shows the panic in the re-entrancy guard; the `.ips` shows SIGABRT), and why it depends on the macOS version: on some builds the modal run loop executes common-mode blocks (drag-and-drop events arriving during the dialog), on others it does not.

## Fix

macOS now implements the `HostHooks::run_dialog` channel (#260, already used on Linux via the XDG portal): `apps/filmcraft/src/main.rs` registers a `run_dialog_sheet` hook that

- creates the `rfd::AsyncFileDialog` future on the main thread (AppKit requirement) and begins the panel with a completion handler — the frame loop keeps running while the dialog is open, so there is no nested run loop and no re-entrancy;
- awaits the future on a worker thread under `catch_unwind` and sends the resulting paths back through the existing `mpsc` answer channel, where `poll_native_dialog` delivers them to the pending dialog continuation each frame, exactly as on Linux.

`prepare_dialog` and `project_patterns` (project-file extension filters) move from `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]` to `#[cfg(any(targ…

title: HEVC: select the x86-v3 inverse transform at runtime, retaining the baseline path
author: fanthomas-creator
body:
Refs #1039. Draft for discussion of a small, localized software-decoder optimization.

The inverse transform currently uses the baseline target even when a compatible x64 CPU could compile the same integer kernel with x86-v3 features. This change caches Pulp's safe CPU/OS feature token once, then selects the appropriate compiled kernel in the same executable. Older x64 processors and other architectures retain the baseline implementation. There is no launcher, global target-CPU flag, new frame buffer or second source implementation.

`pulp` 0.22.3 is MIT-licensed and already present transitively in the workspace lockfile. The change adds a direct x64-only dependency with `std` and `x86-v3`. The existing matrix regression test now compares automatic dispatch and forced baseline against the independent specification formula over 6,000 cases, including 8/10/12-bit shifts. An ignored decode benchmark records every sample and output checksums, with validation and hashing outside the clock.

### Evidence and tradeoff

On a Windows x64 i5-10400F, four paired AB/BA rounds (12 decodes per variant and fixture) gave median decode-time reductions of 1.2% for 1080p Main and 1.8% for 4K Main 10. Output checksums matched. The performance-test executable grew by 35,332 bytes; this is not a full-app size measurement. Both compiled kernels remain in the executable, and the OS manages code-page residency. The cache measured 8 bytes on this target; this is not total application RAM.

On a physical Sandy Bridge i5-2400S with 4 GiB RAM and Linux Mint 22.3, runtime detection correctly selected the baseline path. All 34 required compatibility steps passed: 29 HEVC unit tests, 24 exact pixel-hash comparisons across 12 fixtures at one and four decoder threads, GUI import/playback, rendering, H.264 export/redecode, and project save/reopen. All 529 package files passed integrity checks. [Physical-machine report and diagnostic records](https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/issues/1039#issuecom…

title: Reject .3dl LUTs whose input mesh is larger than 256 entries
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/color/src/lut.rs:371` (no existing issue): color: a .3dl LUT with a huge input mesh overflows `n*n*n`; release builds accept an empty cube and panic when it is applied.

## Cause
`Lut::parse_3dl` took the cube size `n` from the number of values on the mesh line with no upper bound. `n * n * n` then overflowed. In debug builds parsing panicked. In release builds the product wrapped to 0, so an empty cube was accepted and the first `apply()` panicked with an index out of bounds.

## Fix
`parse_3dl` now rejects mesh lengths outside 2..=256, the same range `.cube` allows for LUT_3D_SIZE. With that cap `n³` always fits, so the row-count check and the data allocation cannot overflow. The regression test covers a 2^22-entry mesh and a 257-entry mesh.

## Verified
- Regression test `huge_3dl_mesh_is_rejected`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p filmcraft-color --lib huge_3dl_mesh_is_rejected`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `dev_icon::tests::desktop_file_matches_the_packaged_fields`, which also fails on `main` without this change (macOS); the remaining CI steps pass.

## Not changed
The `.cube` parser and `Lut3d` indexing are unchanged.

title: Android arm64 port: mouse input and keyboard modifiers
author: Kaedo17
body:
Android arm64 port: mouse input and keyboard modifiers

Fixes the two on-device input bugs on the Samsung Tab S11: hardware keyboard
chords (Undo, Save, panel shortcuts) were dead, and a mouse had no hover,
wheel or right/middle click — the port read as "it just supports touch".

Two layers:

1. Vendored winit 0.30.13 (third_party/winit, pinned via [patch.crates-io]):
   the Android motion branch gains the mouse path (the "// TODO mouse events"
   that upstream still has): wheel notches -> MouseWheel{LineDelta}, buttons
   -> MouseInput (right/middle/back/forward), primary -> MouseInput(Left)
   from Down/Up, and hover/move -> CursorMoved/CursorEntered/CursorLeft.
   Touchscreen and touch-dragged stylus keep the untouched Touch path; every
   other target compiles the published crate byte-for-byte. eframe 0.36 pins
   winit to 0.30, 0.30.13 is the last 0.30 release, and upstream still has
   the same gap, so there is no upstream route to the fix — see the README
   inside for the delta and rebase steps.

2. In-app modifier stamping (crates/ui-egui, stamp_android_modifiers,
   unit-tested on the host): winit's Android backend ignores the meta state
   on every KeyEvent and never emits ModifiersChanged, so egui's modifiers
   were always empty. raw_input_hook now tracks Ctrl/Shift/Alt from the key
   events themselves, stamps each key event with what was held at that

title: Add native NTSC DV25 decoding for MOV imports
author: andymenard

NTSC DV camera MOV files currently import without a usable native video decoder. This adds a dependency-free, pure-Rust decoder so FilmCraft can play and seek the original files directly, alongside its existing PCM audio support.

A separate prerequisite commit fixes the Linux development desktop entry's missing MIME types, bringing it into agreement with the packaged entry and its existing regression test.

- Six progressive/interlaced patterns compared against an external FFmpeg oracle (maximum sample error ≤3, mean squared error <0.5).

body:
## What and why

GNOME/Wayland does not provide server-side window decorations. These desktop builds enable eframe's Wayland backend with default features disabled, which leaves winit's Adwaita frame disabled as well. This can leave decorated windows without usable window controls.

Enable `winit/wayland-csd-adwaita` specifically for Linux. Its minimize, maximize/restore and close icons are vector paths, so the close icon does not depend on a font glyph. X11 and compositors offering server-side decorations retain the window manager's frame.

Attribute the dependency's unmodified Cantarell fallback font and include its OFL text and sctk-adwaita's MIT notice in `NOTICE`. Ensure the existing package-document helper ships those notices. No font files are added to the repository. The README documents the behavior and its limits; this does not claim GTK theme parity.

## How it was tested

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` pass.
- The resolved Linux dependency graph includes winit's `wayland-csd-adwaita` feature; the previous lockfile did not include sctk-adwaita.
- Executed `copy_docs` into a temporary package directory and verified that its `NOTICE` exactly matches the source.
- Built the shared eframe/winit configuration and the patched ArtCraft Launcher, then visually checked an isolated GNOME Shell 51.1 Wayland session: minimize, maximize/restore and an X for close are visible, without duplicate controls in the launcher header. This is shared-frame validation, not an app-specific visual check for every application.

A complete app-specific build/test run has not been performed locally. The shared frame configuration, resolved Linux dependency graph, formatting and package-notice checks above passed.

GitHub reports `action_required` for the upstream workflow run(s), with no jobs executed. Maintainer intervention is needed before upstream CI can validate this contribution. This PR remains a draft pending complete app-specific validation.

title: #776: Corner Pin gets corner handles on the Program monitor
author: ruck-syu
body:
Fixes #776.

Corner Pin's four points could only be set by typing numbers in Effect Controls: with the effect selected, the Program monitor showed nothing to grab. Now, while Corner Pin is the selected effect of a selected clip under the playhead, the monitor draws the outline through its four corners with a handle on each:

- dragging a handle moves that corner (`effects.setParam` on `upper_left` / `upper_right` / `lower_right` / `lower_left`), with a resize cursor pointing the way the corner faces;
- dragging inside the outline moves all four corners together (move cursor), so the pinned picture can be repositioned without leaving the monitor;
- each drag is one undo step (`merge`), and "auto" (unset) points start on the clip's corners where the render puts them.

The corners are mapped to the screen the way the render applies them: Corner Pin warps the clip's own pixels, then Motion places the result (`motion_matrix` after the clip-pixel → frame mapping), so the handles stay on the warped corners when the clip is scaled, moved or rotated. Handles that would fall off the monitor are kept in reach like the transform box's. New automation ids: `program.cornerPin.box`, `program.cornerPin.handle.0`–`3` (Upper Left, Upper Right, Lower Right, Lower Left).

`selected_placement` is split so Motion/Transform and Corner Pin share `selected_effect`; `within` is made generic over the number of points. No change to the transform box.

**Not in this PR:** the render crops the warped picture to the clip's own frame, so pulling a corner outward past the clip's edge clips the picture there. Letting Corner Pin stretch past its source bounds is a renderer change I'd rather send separately.

## Testing

- New `corner_pin_handles_move_its_corners` in `crates/ui-egui/tests/transform_handles_ui.rs` (fails on main: no `program.cornerPin.handle.0`): handles appear only while Corner Pin is selected and start on the picture's corners; dragging handle 0 moves only `upper_left` and the handle…

title: fix(engine): enable Reveal Nested and Join Through Edits only when they can act (#2103)
author: ssandweiss
body:
Fixes #2103.

### What was wrong

The Timeline's clip right-click menu enables items by their command's enabled check, and these two were too broad:

- **Reveal Nested Sequence** (`sequence.revealNested`) used `has_seq`. On a plain clip it was enabled and failed with "select a nested sequence clip".
- **Join Through Edits** (`sequence.joinThroughEdits`) used `has_seq`. With no through edits in the sequence (the demo project, for one) it was enabled and failed with "there are no through edits to join".

I found these by right-clicking each kind of timeline element in a demo project and choosing every menu item, each in a fresh app, collecting the ones that failed.

### Change

- `keyboard.rs`: the clip-finding part of `reveal_nested` moves into `nested_to_reveal` (the first selected nested clip, else the topmost one under the playhead on a targeted track). The new check `has_nested_to_reveal` uses it, so the check and the command agree.
- `sequence_tools.rs`: the new check `has_through_edits` asks for a through edit on an unlocked track anywhere in the sequence. I kept it sequence-wide on purpose:
  - A selection-based check would also refuse explicit `cut` / `all` calls, since `Session::enabled_for` only stands named clips in for the selection.
  - A named `cut` already has to be an existing through edit, so this check never refuses a call that could succeed.
  - A selection without a through edit, in a sequence that has one elsewhere, still answers with the command's own reason.

### Tests

`sequence_tools_tests::reveal_nested_and_join_through_edits_are_enabled_only_when_they_can_act`:

- A plain clip in the demo: both items disabled.
- After `clip.nest`, the nested clip: Reveal Nested enabled, and it runs.
- After Add Edit to All Tracks: Join Through Edits enabled. It joins them all, then is disabled again.
- Without the change, the test fails at its first assertion.

title: fix(ui): disable the Project panel's Clear and Automate buttons with nothing selected (#2106)
author: ssandweiss
body:
Fixes #2106.

### What was wrong

With nothing selected in the Project panel, two buttons in its bottom bar looked clickable and only put a message in the status bar:

- **Clear (Delete)** (trash): "Select items to clear"
- **Automate to Sequence**: "select an item in the Project panel"

The panel's own ≡ menu already greys out Delete and Automate to Sequence… in that state, and Premiere's Project panel disables these buttons too.

### Change

`panels/project.rs`, the bottom button bar:

- **When the buttons are enabled:** Clear when there is something to clear (`project_views::clear_params`, the same test as the ≡ menu's Delete). Automate to Sequence when Project items are selected.
- **When disabled:** no hover highlight, the icon is drawn in `text_faint`, and a click does nothing. This is the convention the Media Browser's navigation buttons use. The tooltip still shows.
- **Unused string removed:** "Select items to clear" is gone from the code and from the 8 catalogs that translated it (es, fr, id, it, ja, ko, pt-BR, zh-CN), one line each, so the dead-entry checks stay clean.

### Tests

`project_panel_ui::clear_and_automate_buttons_need_a_selection`:

- Nothing selected: clicking either button shows no message, changes nothing, and opens no dialog.
- An item selected: Automate to Sequence opens its dialog, and Clear removes the item.
- Without the change, the test fails with "no message: Select items to clear".

### Gates

Locally on macOS, toolchain 1.96.1:

- `rustfmt --check` on the changed files: pass

- `filmcraft-ui-egui` UI tests `project_panel_ui`, `menus_ui`, `clipboard_paste_ui` and `panels_ui`: pass

title: Fix potential GPU export deadlock by preparing frame plans outside renderer pool
author: ZpdyGonzales
body:
## Summary

Fix a potential GPU export deadlock caused by performing frame planning while holding a renderer from the renderer pool.

## Problem

During repeated GPU exports, rendering could stall. Debugging showed Rayon workers waiting during nested frame-planning operations while other workers were waiting for an available renderer.

This suggested a possible worker-starvation deadlock.

## Changes

- Prepare GPU frame plans before acquiring a renderer from the pool.
- Add optional `supports_prepared_plan()` and `render_prepared()` methods to the `FrameRenderer` trait.
- Update GPU renderers to consume prepared frame plans.
- Preserve the existing rendering path for renderers that do not support prepared plans.
- Add tests for renderer-pool capability detection.

## Validation

- `cargo check -p filmcraft-export -p filmcraft-gpu -p filmcraft-cli -p filmcraft` — passed.
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-export --lib` — 120 passed.
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-gpu --lib -- --test-threads=1` — 41 passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

Repeated GPU exports also completed successfully on the original development branch, which included separate VA-API changes. Those runtime results have not yet been reproduced on this clean upstream-based branch.

## Notes

Parallel GPU unit tests have intermittently terminated with SIGSEGV on both the original baseline and the modified development branch. Sequential GPU tests pass. This PR does not claim to resolve that separate issue.
